## What The Migration Creates

The migration candidate creates four Route Relation persistence tables:

- `route_relations`
- `route_relation_revisions`
- `route_relation_member_spans`
- `route_relation_way_participation_aggregates`

It also creates or defines:

- lookup, revision, member span, aggregate, owner/access, status, invalidation, and write-request indexes;
- relation, revision, member span, and aggregate constraints;
- composite same-relation `current_revision_id` FK;
- current-revision safety trigger/function;
- substrate `source_kind` guard preventing substrate hints from becoming accepted `source_way` or `source_node` ownership truth;
- RLS enabled on all four Route Relation tables;
- conservative public/owner read policies;
- privacy-thresholded aggregate read policy;
- comments and boundary notes documenting that Route Relations are not `route_cache`, scoring truth, route family, heatmap, UI, or runtime reload behavior.

## What The Migration Does Not Do

The migration does not approve or implement:

- app writes;
- relation lookup;
- reload;
- source hydration;
- geometry fingerprint implementation;
- service-write implementation;
- `route_cache` integration;
- scoring changes;
- heatmap changes;
- UI changes;
- route save/history behavior changes;
- production V1 behavior changes;
- main app pane-of-glass RouteLine V2/substrate/relation integration.

After migration, app behavior must remain unchanged. Full reconstruction remains fallback.

## Rollback Decision Tree

Rollback triggers:

- migration syntax or execution failure;
- partial migration application;
- lock/timeout failure with uncertain state;
- table, index, policy, function, trigger, extension, or naming conflict;
- RLS policy behavior mismatch;
- production role/grant behavior mismatch;
- smoke check failure;
- wrong-environment detection;
- unexpected app behavior after migration.

Stop immediately when:

- the target project is uncertain;
- credentials or project reference appear wrong;
- migration output includes an unexpected error;
- smoke checks fail;
- RLS behavior is unclear;
- any app write, lookup, reload, `route_cache`, scoring, heatmap, UI, or route save/history behavior changes unexpectedly.

Inspect manually when:

- the migration partially applies;
- an object already exists;
- a policy or trigger exists with an unexpected definition;
- a fixture-style smoke check fails;
- a timeout leaves catalog state unclear.

Do not retry blindly. Preserve:

- migration command output;
- migration file checksum;
- target project id/name;
- operator identity;
- timestamps;
- smoke check queries and output;
- catalog state for partial object inspection.

Preferred rollback path:

- restore from the confirmed production backup/snapshot.

SQL-drop rollback caveat:

- drop-based rollback is secondary and must be reviewed before use;
- it should remove only Route Relation objects;
- dependency order must account for RLS policies, trigger, function, FK, indexes, and tables;
- do not drop unrelated project objects.

Rollback is safer now because app writes should not yet exist. If no Route Relation writes occur during the first migration rollout, production Route Relation data should not need preservation. The operator must still account for unrelated production activity during the migration window when considering backup restore.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13: Main App V2 Shadow Integration Closeout

**Status:** Main-app RouteLine V2 shadow integration closeout and manual test readiness audit
**Date:** 2026-05-22
**Related:** EXEC-030 Phase 13A, Phase 13B, Phase 13C, DS-040, DS-041, DS-042

## Scope

This document closes out Phase 13 main-app shadow integration work for RouteLine V2, cyclist substrate candidate hints, and diagnostic Lanterne Route Relation candidates.

This is an audit/report only. It does not execute SQL, add persistence writes, implement relation lookup, implement reload, integrate `route_cache`, cut over scoring, cut over heatmap behavior, change production V1 behavior, add default rider-facing UI, change route save/history behavior, or expand the shadow path beyond GPX/RWGPS.

Files reviewed:

- `docs/04-execution/exec-030-phase-13a-main-app-v2-shadow-integration-design.md`
- `src/lib/route-relations/main-app-shadow-route-relation.ts`
- `src/lib/route-relations/main-app-shadow-route-relation.test.ts`
- `src/pages/Index.tsx`
- `src/lib/debug-flags.ts`
- `src/lib/debug-registry.ts`
- `src/lib/route-line-v2/substrate-candidate-hints.ts`
- `src/lib/route-line-v2/review-page-adapter.ts`
- `src/lib/route-relations/serialize-lanterne-route-relation-v1.ts`
- `src/lib/route-relations/lanterne-route-relation-v1.ts`

## What Phase 13 Now Has

Phase 13 now has:

- Phase 13A design for running RouteLine V2, substrate hints, and diagnostic Route Relation generation as a main-app sidecar.
- Disabled-by-default debug flag `ROUTE_LINE_V2_MAIN_APP_SHADOW`.
- Debug registry entry describing the flag as compact diagnostics only, with no persistence, reload, cache, scoring, heatmap, or rider UI change.
- Main app GPX/RWGPS shadow hook in `src/pages/Index.tsx`.
- Source gating for `fresh_upload` and `rwgps`; manual create, history reload, draw, route-to, and detour flows remain out of scope.
- Shadow cancellation on new route load, analysis cancel, route clear, and Index unmount.
- Shadow orchestrator at `src/lib/route-relations/main-app-shadow-route-relation.ts`.
- Module tests at `src/lib/route-relations/main-app-shadow-route-relation.test.ts`.
- RouteLine V2 worker launch through the existing V2 worker boundary.
- In-memory diagnostic Route Relation candidate serialization and validation.
- Compact production comparison summary after current production analysis reports.
- Stale/cancelled result handling.
- Timeout and failure isolation.
- Malformed route point rejection before worker start.
- Compact substrate hint diagnostics with `nonCanonical: true`.
- Explicit false boundary flags for persistence, lookup, reload, `route_cache`, scoring, heatmap, default UI, route save/history, current revision pointer, member index writes, and aggregate writes.

## Proven Behavior

Phase 13 proves the shadow orchestration boundary and main-app hook wiring. It does not yet prove a manual browser run.

Proven by tests and code review:

- Flag disabled means the shadow start predicate returns false for GPX/RWGPS.
- Flag enabled can run the shadow path for a synthetic route.
- Only GPX/fresh upload and RWGPS sources are eligible in the first scope.
- Manual create and history reload sources are rejected by the source predicate.
- Shadow worker startup failure becomes diagnostic-only output.
- Shadow timeout becomes diagnostic-only output.
- Stale shadow results are ignored and do not emit diagnostics.
- Cancelled shadow results are ignored and do not emit diagnostics.
- Malformed route points fail before the worker starts.
- Relation serialization failure stays diagnostic-only.
- Relation validation failure stays diagnostic-only.
- The Route Relation candidate summary is diagnostic-only and has `persisted: false`, `lookup: false`, and `reload: false`.
- Substrate hint diagnostics remain noncanonical and compact.
- Substrate accepted-truth attempts produce `substrate_hint_as_source_truth_blocked` and cannot make a relation diagnostic valid.
- Diagnostics omit forbidden payload surfaces such as full topology, full relation members, route spine payloads, Supabase payloads, `route_cache` payloads, scoring payloads, heatmap payloads, and raw substrate source labels.
- The shadow module has no forbidden production imports for Supabase, `route_cache`, route persistence, scoring, heatmap, viewport runtime, reload, lookup, workers, components, or pages.
- Main app wiring dispatches a clearly labeled `lanterne-route-line-v2-main-app-shadow` diagnostic event and console label only when the flag permits the shadow path.

## Not Yet Proven

Phase 13 does not yet prove:

- manual browser testing in the normal app pane of glass,
- GPX load with the flag off observed in a browser,
- GPX load with the flag on observed in a browser,
- RWGPS load with the flag on observed in a browser,
- production DB persistence,
- Supabase Route Relation writes,
- relation lookup,
- reload,
- `route_cache` integration,
- scoring cutover,
- heatmap cutover,
- main app UI diagnostic drawer,
- Draw shadow path,
- Route To shadow path,
- Detour shadow path,
- History/saved-route shadow path,
- production RouteLine V2 cutover,
- persisted Route Relation records,
- manual confirmation that stale logs do not appear after rapid successive route loads.

## Manual Test Checklist

Use this checklist for Phase 13E manual/local app shadow testing:

- Start the app locally.
- Confirm `ROUTE_LINE_V2_MAIN_APP_SHADOW` is off.
- Load a normal GPX.
- Confirm normal production route analysis completes.
- Confirm no `lanterne-route-line-v2-main-app-shadow` event or `[ROUTE-LINE-V2-MAIN-APP-SHADOW]` console output appears.
- Confirm no default rider-facing UI changed.
- Enable `ROUTE_LINE_V2_MAIN_APP_SHADOW`.
- Load a simple GPX.
- Confirm production analysis still completes and remains authoritative.
- Confirm a `[ROUTE-LINE-V2-MAIN-APP-SHADOW]` console diagnostic appears.
- Confirm the diagnostic event name is `lanterne-route-line-v2-main-app-shadow`.
- Confirm diagnostics are compact and do not include full graph arrays, full substrate graph, full relation payload, or full route geometry arrays.
- Confirm no default rider-facing UI changed.
- Confirm no `route_cache` write beyond existing production behavior.
- Confirm no Supabase Route Relation write.
- Confirm no relation lookup.
- Confirm no reload.
- Test a malformed or too-small route if feasible and confirm failure is diagnostic only.
- Start a new route load while shadow is still running if feasible and confirm stale/cancelled output does not overwrite or confuse the newer route.
- Test RWGPS open/import if that path is available locally.
- Disable `ROUTE_LINE_V2_MAIN_APP_SHADOW`.
- Load another GPX and confirm shadow diagnostics are silent again.

## Expected Diagnostic Fields

Manual logs should contain only compact fields:

- `event`
- `shadowRequestId`
- `routeLabel` if available
- `routeSourceType`
- `routePointCount`
- `routeDistanceM` if available

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AC: Hinted Source Coverage Repair

Date: 2026-05-22

## Scope

Phase 13AC repaired the short urban debug/test substrate fixture source coverage gap identified in Phase 13AB.

Fixture:

- `public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx`

No hinted-result selection behavior was changed.

## Input Finding

Phase 13AB showed that direct substrate matching was fixed but source coverage was still not equivalent:

- direct accepted hints: `6`
- rejected hints: `0`
- route-distance coverage equivalent: `yes`
- source coverage equivalent: `no`
- hinted ownership spans: `169`
- full-baseline ownership spans: `171`
- baseline-only spans: `3`
- hinted-only spans: `1`
- span delta root cause: `meaningful_missing_source_coverage`
- future hinted selection blocker: `meaningful_missing_span`

The baseline-only spans were compactly identified as:

- `anonymous_connector` way `1389989213`, `11835-11920m`
- `anonymous_connector` way `556215894`, `11920-11923m`
- `motor_road` way `820307510`, `11923-12010m`

The hinted-only span was:

- `motor_road` way `820307510`, `11835-12010m`

The delta was not near blockers or handoffs. It was a meaningful source-coverage gap.

## Root Cause

The short urban fixture return-leg merged substrate run included way `820307510`, but omitted the two connector source refs that the full-baseline path used immediately before it:

- `1389989213`
- `556215894`

Because those connector refs were absent from the fixture constituent refs, the hinted candidate universe could cover the same route distance with a longer `820307510` span while missing source-owned connector coverage from the full baseline.

## Repair Made

The debug fixture provider now includes the connector refs in the `fixture:kc-47th-return` merged run:

- `1389989213`
- `556215894`
- `820307510`

The merged substrate run id remains diagnostic metadata only. The canonical matching metadata is still carried through:

- `constituentOsmWayIds`
- `sourceMemberRefs`

No road names, display labels, family labels, or merged substrate run ids were made canonical matching identity.

## Safeguard Expansion

No safeguard expansion behavior was changed in this phase.

The repair is fixture-local because the missing source refs were known constituent source coverage for the short urban return leg. RouteLine fallback/safeguard behavior and selected result policy remain unchanged.

## Expected Diagnostic Effect

Expected on the next manual short urban run:

- direct accepted hints remain greater than `0`
- rejected hints remain `0`
- candidate reduction remains meaningful, with possible slight post-filter candidate growth from the added connector refs
- route-distance coverage remains equivalent
- source coverage should become equivalent or report a narrower remaining blocker
- selected result remains unchanged in this phase
- relation validation remains valid
- substrate remains noncanonical

## Tests

Added/updated tests prove:

- the short urban fixture carries return-leg connector refs `1389989213` and `556215894`
- the refs are exposed as canonical `sourceMemberRefs`
- continuity hint constituent refs include the repaired connector refs
- repaired connector span coverage can classify as equivalent source coverage
- source coverage remains blocked when those refs are absent or replaced by a different source identity
- compact diagnostics remain free of geometry and substrate truth payloads

## Manual Smoke

Manual browser smoke was not run in this phase.

The next local/manual phase should reload `public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx` with:

- V1 on
- V2 Shadow on
- substrate fixture on

and capture whether baseline-only meaningful span count falls to `0` or narrows to a more specific remaining source-coverage blocker.

## Boundary Statement

- No SQL was executed.
- No persistence writes were added.
- No lookup or reload path was added.
- No route_cache mutation was added.
- No scoring, heatmap, or default UI behavior changed.
- Substrate remains noncanonical.
- Route Relation candidate remains diagnostic-only.
- Full reconstruction remains fallback.

## Recommended Next Phase

Recommended next:

**Phase 13AD: manual retest of short urban hinted source coverage repair.**

If the repair makes source coverage equivalent, the following phase can consider a debug-only hinted selection policy. If meaningful spans remain, continue source coverage or safeguard expansion repair before DC or Cape May fixtures.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AF — Substrate Constituent Source-Ref Derivation

Status:

Accepted for diagnostic implementation.

## Purpose

Phase 13AC repaired the short urban substrate fixture by manually adding missing connector refs.

Phase 13AE proved debug-only hinted selection works when source coverage is clean.

However, source coverage was clean only because one fixture was patched by hand.

This phase fixes the bug class: merged substrate hints must preserve or derive complete canonical constituent source refs before they can reduce candidates directly.

## Core Decision

A merged substrate hint may be direct-matchable only if its canonical constituent source refs are complete enough to reproduce full-baseline route-distance and source coverage.

The following are diagnostic metadata only:

- merged run id
- debug run id
- display label
- display name
- family key
- presentation group id

The following may support direct matching:

- constituentOsmWayIds
- constituentOsmNodeIds
- sourceMemberRefs
- sourceKind + sourceMemberId
- source snapshot / fixture version metadata

If canonical refs are missing, the system must derive them from source-owned evidence.

If it cannot derive them, it must reject direct matching for that hint.

No display label guessing.

No magic connector IDs.

No fixture-local hand patching.

## Invariants

- substrate is not route truth
- a merged substrate run id alone is never direct-matchable
- display identity is never direct-matchable by itself
- family key is never direct-matchable by itself
- source refs must be canonical or derived from canonical evidence
- missing refs must be explicit
- direct matching must fail closed
- diagnostics must explain which refs were explicit, derived, rejected, or missing
- short urban must pass without manually injected connector refs
- debug-only hinted selection may remain enabled, but only after derivation/validation succeeds
- full baseline remains fallback

## Non-Goals

This phase does not:

- skip full-baseline comparison
- persist substrate
- create production substrate cache
- mutate route_cache
- write route relations
- read route relations
- change scoring
- change heatmap
- expand to DC or Cape May
- promote V2 to production

## Implementation

Added a pure source-ref derivation helper:

- `src/lib/route-line-v2/substrate-constituent-source-refs.ts`

The helper normalizes explicit refs, expands source-member refs, derives connector/source refs only from route-aligned source evidence, and fails closed for display-only merged hints.

The helper does not import Supabase, React, route cache, scoring, heatmap, browser globals, `localStorage`, or `sessionStorage`.

The short urban fixture provider now separates:

- explicit merged-run constituent refs
- compact source-owned connector evidence
- derived final constituent refs

The previously hand-added connector ways are no longer in the return-leg explicit constituent list. They are present only as compact source-owned topology connector evidence and appear in final hint refs through derivation:

- `1389989213`
- `556215894`

Derivation evidence for those refs is `topology_connector_bridge`.

## Diagnostic Fields

The V2 Shadow/Test drawer diagnostics can now surface:

- substrate source-ref derivation status
- explicit constituent way count
- derived constituent way count
- final constituent way count
- derived connector way count
- missing source ref count
- diagnostic-only hint count
- source-ref derivation blocker
- source-ref derivation evidence count

For the short urban fixture, the expected clean state is:

- source-ref derivation status: `complete_with_derived_refs`
- missing source ref count: `0`
- diagnostic-only hint count: `0`
- derived connector way count: at least `2`
- substrate accepted as truth: `false`

## Tests

Added/updated tests prove:

- merged run id alone is diagnostic-only
- display label alone is diagnostic-only
- family key alone is diagnostic-only
- explicit constituent OSM way refs are accepted
- sourceMemberRefs expand to OSM way refs
- malformed refs are rejected
- duplicate refs normalize away
- connector bridge refs derive only from route-aligned topology-supported evidence
- nearby/cross-street evidence is rejected
- display names cannot derive connector refs
- missing canonical refs fail closed
- explicit and derived refs are recorded separately
- the short urban connector refs are derived, not explicit final-output fixture patch refs
- direct accepted hints remain `6`
- rejected hints remain `0`
- debug-only hinted selection remains available when equivalence is clean

## Boundary Statement

No SQL was executed. No persistence writes, relation lookup, reload, route_cache mutation, browser-persistent equivalence receipt, scoring cutover, heatmap cutover, default rider UI behavior, route save/history behavior, or production V1 behavior was added.

Substrate remains noncanonical. The Route Relation candidate remains diagnostic-only. Full reconstruction and full baseline comparison remain available.

## Recommended Next Phase

Recommended next:

**EXEC-030 Phase 13AG: debug-only equivalence receipt and baseline-comparison skip.**

Do not implement 13AG until this source-ref completeness path has passed manual verification.

## Source File: docs/04-execution/exec-030-phase-13ag-debug-equivalence-receipt-baseline-skip.md

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AG — Debug Equivalence Receipt and Baseline Skip

Status: Accepted for diagnostic implementation.

## Purpose

Phase 13AE allowed debug-only hinted selection when hinted and full-baseline construction were equivalent.

Phase 13AF removed the short urban hand-patch by deriving missing connector refs from source-owned route-aligned topology evidence.

Full-baseline comparison still ran every time, so the optimized hinted lane could be selected while still paying the comparison cost.

Phase 13AG adds a debug-only equivalence receipt so the short urban fixture can skip the full-baseline comparison run after equivalence has already been proven for the same route, fixture, hint/source-ref derivation, builder, and policy signature.

## Core Decision

The V2 Shadow short urban substrate lane may skip the full-baseline comparison run only when all debug receipt gates pass:

- debug baseline skip is explicitly enabled
- debug hinted selection is enabled
- the short urban substrate fixture route is matched
- substrate provider is available
- hints were requested and accepted
- rejected hint count is zero
- source-ref derivation status is `complete` or `complete_with_derived_refs`
- missing source ref count is zero
- diagnostic-only hint count is zero
- a valid in-memory equivalence receipt exists
- receipt route, fixture, hint, source-ref derivation, builder, selection policy, source-ref policy, and fixture version signatures match the current run
- current hinted construction remains relation-valid at the RouteLine structural gate
- current validation errors count is zero
- current hinted ownership span and blocker counts match the receipt
- current hinted-only blocker count is zero
- receipt baseline-only and hinted-only span counts are zero
- receipt source and route-distance coverage were equivalent
- receipt blocker equivalence was equivalent
- receipt structural equivalence was `hinted_equivalent_to_baseline` or `hinted_equivalent_with_shared_blockers`
- substrate accepted as truth remains false

If any gate fails, the full-baseline comparison runs as before.

## Receipt Source

Receipts are in-memory only and session-scoped. They may be created only after a clean full-baseline comparison in the current app session or test run.

Receipts are not seeded from docs, route_cache, Supabase, localStorage, sessionStorage, indexedDB, or production route relation persistence.

## First Run Behavior

On the first run after page load, no receipt exists. The system runs the full-baseline comparison. If equivalence is clean, it creates an in-memory receipt and selects `hinted_debug_equivalent`.

## Second Run Behavior

On a later run in the same app session with the same short urban route/fixture/hint/source-ref/build signature, the system may skip the full-baseline comparison and select `hinted_debug_receipt`.

## Diagnostic Truthfulness

Skipped full-baseline metrics are labeled as receipt-backed:

- full-baseline comparison: `skipped_due_to_debug_equivalence_receipt`
- receipt source: `in_memory_debug_equivalence_receipt`
- selected result source: `hinted_debug_receipt`
- receipt full-baseline ownership spans are distinct from current full-baseline measurements
- baseline compare/fallback topology time is shown as `skipped`, not `0ms`

## Invariants

- substrate accepted as truth remains false
- receipt accepted as truth remains false
- hinted construction still runs and validates in the current run
- the receipt only suppresses the comparison run
- shared blockers remain visible
- unique blockers force comparison/fallback
- rejected hints force comparison/fallback
- missing source refs force comparison/fallback
- diagnostic-only hints force comparison/fallback
- disabled/default behavior still runs comparison
- production/default UI behavior is unchanged

## Non-Goals

This phase does not persist receipts, create a production equivalence cache, skip candidate generation, move substrate filtering earlier, expand fixtures, create DC/Cape May substrate, mutate route_cache, save/read route relations, change scoring, change heatmap, replace V1, or claim total V2 optimization is solved.

## Implementation Summary

Added pure receipt helper:

- `src/lib/route-line-v2/debug-equivalence-receipt.ts`

Added in-memory store:

- `src/lib/route-line-v2/debug-equivalence-receipt-store.ts`

The V2 Shadow short urban path now passes a matching in-memory receipt into the worker when present. The topology builder checks the current hinted construction and source-ref derivation before consulting the receipt. When valid, it skips the full-baseline comparison and selects `hinted_debug_receipt`.

Receipt creation happens after a clean full-baseline comparison and is stored by the main-thread shadow orchestration only after relation candidate validation succeeds.

## Remaining Performance Truth

13AG removes only the redundant full-baseline comparison topology run after a valid receipt exists.

It does not remove substrate filter work, safeguard expansion, hinted topology construction, route-axis setup, candidate generation, worker startup, or diagnostic projection overhead.

## Recommended Next Phase

EXEC-030 Phase 13AH: candidate-generation timing and early substrate filter placement.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AH — Candidate Generation Timing and Early Substrate Prefilter

Status: Accepted for diagnostic implementation.

## Purpose

Phase 13AG removes redundant full-baseline comparison after an in-memory equivalence receipt exists.

However, the larger V2 Shadow cost may still live upstream in candidate generation, graph construction, or topology materialization.

This phase decomposes those timings and introduces a debug-only early substrate prefilter shadow lane for the short urban fixture.

The early lane filters source topology/candidate records before expensive candidate materialization only where it can prove every required canonical source way is retained, then compares against the existing late-filter hinted lane.

## Core Decision

Early substrate prefiltering is diagnostic-only in this phase.

The existing late-filter hinted lane remains the selected debug result source. The early-prefiltered lane may be planned, logged, and timed. It does not become selected output in 13AH.

Selected result source therefore remains governed by Phase 13AG:

- `hinted_debug_equivalent`
- `hinted_debug_receipt`
- `full_baseline_fallback`

13AH adds separate diagnostics:

- `candidateGenerationMode: late_filter_selected`
- `earlySubstratePrefilterMode: disabled | shadow_compare`
- `earlySubstratePrefilterStatus`
- `earlySubstratePrefilterSelected: false`

## Timing Model

Added timing buckets:

- `candidateGenerationTotalMs`
- `candidateMaterializationMs`
- `topologyGraphBuildMs`
- `pathSolveMs`
- `ownershipSpanBuildMs`
- `blockerBuildMs`
- `earlyPrefilterPlanMs`
- `rawSourceRecordFilterMs`
- `receiptValidationMs`

Unavailable or not-yet-separated buckets are rendered as `not separated yet`, `not measured`, `skipped`, or `unavailable`; skipped work is not shown as `0ms`.

Still not separated in this phase:

- substrate fixture match timing
- source-ref derivation timing
- sample candidate lookup timing
- candidate scoring timing
- candidate dedup timing
- diagnostic projection timing

## Count Model

Added count diagnostics:

- raw source records before/after early filter
- candidate rows before/after late filter
- unique candidate ways before/after late filter
- early allowed way count
- early required constituent way count
- early retained required way count
- early missing required way count
- retained/missing derived connector ways
- final constituent way count
- derived constituent way count
- derived connector way count
- direct accepted/rejected hint counts
- diagnostic-only hint count
- missing source-ref count

Counts are labeled by unit. Evidence rows and unique OSM way ids are not conflated.

## Early Prefilter Contract

The early prefilter is built only from canonical source identity:

- `finalConstituentOsmWayIds`
- `explicitConstituentOsmWayIds`
- `derivedConstituentOsmWayIds`
- source-member refs expanded through source-owned evidence
- derived topology connector evidence from Phase 13AF
- raw source records with canonical `osmWayId`

It does not use:

- display label alone
- display name alone
- family key alone
- merged run id alone
- debug run id alone
- presentation group id alone
- route-specific hardcoded allowlists

The prefilter fails closed if any required constituent way or derived connector would be dropped.

## Implementation Notes

The safe early boundary currently exists in `topology-path-builder.ts` before `buildTopologyEdges`, where raw `RouteLineV2RoadCandidate` records still carry canonical `osmWayId`.

Added pure helpers:

- `src/lib/route-line-v2/early-substrate-prefilter.ts`
- `src/lib/route-line-v2/route-line-v2-timing.ts`

The early prefilter planner is pure and does not import Supabase, React, route cache, scoring, heatmap, browser storage, or browser globals.

## Short Urban Finding

The short urban enabled manual smoke did not reach early-vs-late shadow equivalence.

The early prefilter correctly failed closed:

- status: `unavailable_missing_required_constituent_way`
- reason: `required_constituent_missing_from_raw_source_records`
- required constituent ways: 56
- retained required ways at raw source boundary: 53
- missing required ways: 3
- derived connector ways retained: 2
- derived connector ways missing: 0
- `1389989213` retained: true
- `556215894` retained: true

This means the Phase 13AF connector repair is preserved, but the raw source record boundary used for early filtering does not currently contain every final constituent way needed to reproduce the late hinted lane.

Because the missing required-way count is nonzero, early prefiltering remains disabled for the short urban fixture. This is intentional fail-closed behavior.

## Manual Timing Snapshot

- selected result source: `hinted_debug_equivalent`
- full-baseline comparison: `ran_to_generate_equivalence_receipt`
- candidate rows before late filter: 9,783

Timing should not be over-interpreted: the enabled run still used the late-filter selected lane, and the early lane did not run because it failed closed.

## Boundary

- no SQL executed
- no persistence writes added
- no relation lookup/reload added
- no route_cache mutation/coupling added
- no `setCachedRoute` / `getCachedRoute` coupling added
- no browser-persistent early-filter cache or receipt storage added
- no scoring cutover
- no heatmap cutover
- no default production UI behavior change
- no V1 replacement
- no DC or Cape May fixture work
- substrate remains noncanonical
- early prefilter remains diagnostic-only and unselected

## Recommendation

Recommend EXEC-030 Phase 13AI as a source-boundary repair/early-filter readiness phase before any early-prefilter selection:

1. Explain why three final constituent way ids are absent from the raw source records at the early filter boundary.
2. Decide whether those ways should be preserved in raw source evidence, excluded from required early constituent coverage, or carried through a separate source-member expansion boundary.
3. Only after early-vs-late equivalence is clean should a later phase consider early-prefilter selection or an early-vs-late receipt.

Do not move to DC/Cape May until the short urban early prefilter can either run equivalently or has a documented architectural blocker.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AI — Bounded Topology Bridge Probe Before Broad Candidate Generation

Status: Accepted for diagnostic implementation.

## Purpose

Phase 13AH proved that early substrate prefiltering fails closed when required constituent source records are missing at the raw source boundary. That failure is correct, but it showed an architectural gap: falling immediately back to broad candidate generation is too expensive if the missing records can be discovered through a narrow topology bridge probe.

Phase 13AI adds a bounded bridge-probe seam before the early prefilter shadow comparison. The probe distinguishes exact-ID hydration from narrow topology bridge discovery:

- exact-ID hydration is used only when missing canonical OSM way IDs are already known.
- narrow bridge discovery is shaped around unresolved route gaps, neighbor way/node context, route-slice bounds, topology connection, and route alignment.

## Core Decision

The V2 Shadow short urban lane may attempt a bounded topology bridge probe only when the substrate fixture route is matched, source-ref derivation is clean, no hints are rejected, and the early prefilter is blocked by missing required source records.

The probe output is diagnostic source evidence only. It is not route truth, not substrate truth, and not a selected output.

Allowed identity inputs:

- canonical OSM way IDs
- canonical OSM node IDs
- source-member refs expanded through source-owned evidence
- route gap/window topology context
- neighboring way/node context

Rejected identity inputs:

- display labels
- family keys alone
- merged/debug substrate run IDs
- route-specific allowlists
- broad corridor searches

## Implementation

Added:

- `src/lib/route-line-v2/topology-bridge-probe.ts`
- `src/lib/route-line-v2/topology-bridge-probe-provider.ts`
- `src/lib/route-line-v2/topology-bridge-probe.test.ts`

Updated:

- early prefilter planning to preserve route-aligned safeguard refs in the shadow allowed set
- topology path builder bridge-probe wiring before late topology construction
- short urban fixture-backed narrow topology-window records for the missing source records
- V2 Shadow substrate diagnostics and Test drawer controls for bridge-probe status, counts, IDs, timing, and ordering

The short urban fixture-backed provider is narrow source/topology evidence, not a final-output patch. It exposes compact source records for the three missing raw-boundary refs:

- `1511491234`
- `1516936489`
- `1516936492`

The previously derived connector refs remain retained:

- `1389989213`
- `556215894`

## Corrective Narrow-Discovery Result

The first 13AI implementation proved exact-ID hydration, not unknown connector discovery. It was too weak because the bridge probe request was handed the missing way IDs.

The corrected proof path keeps exact-ID hydration as a fallback helper, but the short urban success path now uses a route-gap topology context with no target IDs supplied to the provider.

Corrected probe result:

- probe status: `complete_with_narrow_bridge_discovery`
- probe mode: `narrow_topology_bridge_discovery`
- provider mode: `fixture_topology_window`
- known missing IDs supplied to provider: false
- topology bridge probe used gap context: true
- neighboring way/node context present: true
- broad search used: false
- missing required before probe: 3
- missing required after probe: 0
- requested way IDs: none
- discovered way IDs: `1511491234`, `1516936489`, `1516936492`
- verified way IDs: `1511491234`, `1516936489`, `1516936492`

Early-vs-late shadow comparison still fails closed:

- early prefilter status: `shadow_compare_not_equivalent`
- early ownership spans: 167
- late ownership spans: 171
- shared spans: 157
- early-only spans: 10
- late-only spans: 14
- route-distance coverage: yes
- source coverage: no
- blocker equivalence: equivalent

Interpretation: the bounded probe can discover missing raw-boundary source records from gap geometry plus neighbor topology context without being handed the target IDs. Including those discovered records still changes source coverage relative to the current late-filter hinted path, so the early-prefiltered path remains unsafe to select.

## Invariants

- substrate remains noncanonical
- bridge-probe output is not route truth
- exact OSM identity is required
- bridge discovery fails closed on ambiguity, missing topology support, or broad-search usage
- early-prefiltered output is not selected
- selected result remains governed by Phase 13AG
- no persistence/cache/scoring/heatmap/default UI cutover was added

## Remaining Limitation

13AI proves the bounded narrow-discovery seam and fail-closed behavior, but it does not prove early-vs-late equivalence for short urban. The next repair should inspect why adding the discovered source records changes source coverage and whether those records should be:

- included in the late hinted comparison source boundary,
- excluded from the early required set as non-route-participating source refs,
- or handled through a narrower connector/source participation rule.

## Recommended Next Phase

EXEC-030 Phase 13AJ should not select early-prefiltered output yet. It should repair or explain the early-vs-late source coverage delta after bridge hydration, then only consider early-prefilter selection after equivalence is clean.

Boundary statement:

- no SQL executed
- no persistence writes
- no lookup/reload
- no route_cache mutation
- no scoring/heatmap/default UI behavior change
- substrate remains noncanonical
- Route Relation candidate remains diagnostic-only
- early-prefiltered output remains unselected

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AJ - Early/Late Source Coverage Delta Repair

Status: Accepted for diagnostic implementation.

## Purpose

13AI proved narrow topology bridge discovery without being handed the known missing IDs. The bridge probe discovered and verified:

- 1511491234
- 1516936489
- 1516936492

The early prefilter still failed equivalence against the late hinted lane:

- early / late spans: 167 / 171
- shared spans: 157
- early-only spans: 10
- late-only spans: 14
- route-distance coverage: yes
- source coverage: no
- blocker equivalence: equivalent

This phase explains that delta and repairs only the smallest real cause.

## Delta Table Before Repair

The compact unmatched span table showed no missing geometry, node IDs, domain, or source lineage on the rows. The important pattern was that the bridge-discovered records existed only in the early source boundary, while the late hinted lane was still built from the original source boundary.

| late-only | 1394-1400 | 1116973642 | footway | yes | yes | no | yes | source identity/window shift |
| late-only | 1400-1495 | 1116973641 | footway | yes | yes | no | yes | source identity/window shift |
| late-only | 1495-1530 | 378633061 | service | yes | yes | no | no | source identity/window shift |
| late-only | 1530-1668 | 552777439 | footway | yes | yes | no | yes | source identity/window shift |
| late-only | 1668-1668 | 552217956 | footway | yes | yes | no | yes | source identity/window shift |
| late-only | 1668-1746 | 552217957 | footway | yes | yes | no | yes | source identity/window shift |

Primary bucket: topology_input_diff_other.

Reason: the early lane had a source-completed boundary after bridge discovery, while the late hinted lane still built route-aligned safeguards, candidate roads, hinted topology, diagnostics, and full-baseline comparison from the original source boundary.

This was not display-label matching, family-key matching, or merged-run identity matching. Source member refs, source kind/member ID, node IDs, coords, lineage, and domain were available in the compact diagnostics.

## Repair

Verified bridge records are now merged into a source-completed debug source boundary before late candidate selection:

- route-aligned safeguard selection uses the completed source boundary
- hint canonical way filtering uses the completed source boundary
- late hinted candidate roads use the completed source boundary
- hinted topology uses the completed source boundary
- source-completed early/late diagnostics use the completed source boundary
- the independent raw full-baseline comparator is kept separate by the follow-up comparator-boundary repair below

The early-prefiltered output is still not selected. Selection remains governed by 13AG debug hinted selection / debug receipt policy.

## Comparator Boundary Audit

Follow-up audit result:

- independent full baseline preserved in bridge-enabled 13AJ path: no
- true raw full baseline span count from the no-bridge/original-universe run: 171
- source-completed late hinted span count from the bridge-enabled run: 167
- source-completed early-prefilter span count from the bridge-enabled run: 167

The bridge-enabled `baselineResult` currently runs against the source-completed debug boundary, not the original full candidate/source universe. In code terms, `sourceCompletedRoads` is used for route-aligned safeguards, late hinted candidate selection, hinted topology, diagnostics, and the debug baseline comparison.

That makes the 13AJ repaired result a source-completed early-vs-late equivalence proof. It is not an independent proof that the source-completed hinted lane remains equivalent to the original raw full baseline.

The 171 -> 167 count shift is not fully explained by this phase. The compact 13AJ delta showed the affected rows were concentrated around the bridge/gap source boundary and mostly involved safeguard/context records with complete node IDs, coords, lineage, and domain. The most likely bucket is removed source-boundary/safeguard context artifacts after bridge completion, but 13AJ does not compute raw full baseline, source-completed late, and source-completed early side by side in one diagnostic result. Therefore the four-span collapse should remain unproven until a follow-up comparator-boundary audit adds all three lanes.

Misleading labels:

- In the bridge-enabled 13AJ path, rows labeled `full-baseline` are source-completed baseline rows.
- Future diagnostics should either preserve a separate raw full-baseline comparator or rename these rows to `source-completed baseline`.
- No early-prefilter receipt or selection should be based on 13AJ until the independent raw comparator boundary is restored or explicitly separated.

## Comparator Boundary Repair Result

Follow-up correction restored the independent raw comparator and separates the three lanes:

1. `raw_full_baseline`
   - built from the original full source/candidate universe
   - no bridge-discovered/source-completed boundary injected
   - the only lane allowed to mean full baseline
2. `source_completed_late_hinted`
   - late hinted path using the source-completed debug boundary
3. `source_completed_early_prefilter`
   - early prefilter path using the source-completed debug boundary

Receipt signatures now include:

- comparator mode
- baseline source-boundary mode
- hinted source-boundary mode
- source-boundary fingerprint

Legacy receipts missing those fields fail closed. A receipt can only skip baseline comparison when the comparator mode is `raw_full_baseline` and the baseline source boundary is `raw_original_source`.

Manual short urban smoke after the repair:

| lane / field | value |
| --- | --- |
| independent full baseline preserved | yes |
| raw full-baseline span count | 171 |
| source-completed late hinted span count | 167 |
| source-completed early prefilter span count | 167 |
| raw-vs-source-completed delta count | 24 |
| source-completed early-vs-late delta count | 0 |
| raw-vs-source-completed source coverage | no |
| source-completed early-vs-late source coverage | yes |
| debug selection comparator mode | raw_full_baseline |
| baseline source boundary mode | raw_original_source |
| hinted source boundary mode | source_completed_debug_boundary |
| selected result source | full_baseline_fallback |
| fallback reason | hinted_source_coverage_not_equivalent |
| receipt status | missing |
| full-baseline comparison mode | ran_full_baseline_comparison |
| early prefilter selected | false |
| substrate accepted as truth | false |

The corrected result is honest: source-completed early/late equivalence is proven, but raw full-baseline equivalence is not. The 171 -> 167 shift remains an unresolved raw-vs-source-completed source coverage delta, not harmless fragmentation.

No full-baseline equivalence receipt is created from the source-completed comparison. No `hinted_debug_equivalent` or `hinted_debug_receipt` selection is allowed unless raw full-baseline equivalence also passes.

## Manual Smoke

The smoke below is the original 13AJ early/late repair capture before the comparator-boundary follow-up. The follow-up values in the previous section supersede the selection/comparator interpretation.

Fixture:

- public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx

Case 1, repair disabled / pre-repair capture:

- bridge probe mode: narrow_topology_bridge_discovery
- known missing IDs supplied to provider: false
- broad search used: false
- discovered/verified IDs: 1511491234, 1516936489, 1516936492
- raw source boundary missing required records: 3 -> 0
- early / late spans: 167 / 171
- shared spans: 157
- early-only spans: 10
- late-only spans: 14
- route-distance coverage: yes
- source coverage: no
- blocker equivalence: equivalent
- selected result source: hinted_debug_receipt
- early prefilter selected: false
- substrate accepted as truth: false

Case 2, repair enabled:

- known missing IDs supplied to provider: false

The selected source changed from receipt-backed to full-comparison-backed in the repaired smoke because the source-completed hinted signature no longer matched the previous in-memory receipt. That is expected 13AG behavior: receipt mismatch forces full-baseline comparison.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AK - Raw vs Source-Completed Span Delta Audit

Status: accepted diagnostic audit.

## Purpose

This phase answers the raw comparator question left after the independent comparator boundary repair:

Status: accepted diagnostic implementation.

Fixture: `public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx`

## Direct Answer

B. `raw_baseline_artifact_378633061`

The GPX line does not appear to traverse OSM way `378633061`.

The raw baseline can select it because it is present in the raw source universe and has topology support nearby, but the GPX route slice does not geometrically follow it.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AO - Artifact-Adjudicated Equivalence Receipt Hardening

Status: Accepted for diagnostic implementation.

## Audit Answer

B. `no_receipt_can_skip_without_artifact_adjudication_context`.

Before this hardening, the 13AG receipt contract carried comparator and source-boundary modes, but it did not bind the receipt to the artifact-adjudication policy, artifact fingerprint, raw/source-completed delta fingerprint, or meaningful-delta summary. A receipt also could not be created for the current artifact-adjudicated raw comparator equivalence path. That made the receipt path incomplete for the post-13AN short urban state.

## Implementation

The debug equivalence receipt now includes:

- `sourceCompletedBoundaryFingerprint`
- `rawVsSourceCompletedDeltaFingerprint`
- `artifactAdjudicationPolicyVersion`
- `artifactAdjudicationFingerprint`
- `meaningfulRawVsSourceCompletedDeltaCount`
- `rawArtifactAdjudicatedCount`
- `unknownDeltaCount`
- `meaningfulCoverageStatus`
- `selectedResultReason`

Validation now fails closed when artifact-adjudication fields are missing, the artifact policy/fingerprint changes, the source-completed boundary fingerprint changes, unknown deltas are present, meaningful deltas remain, or the meaningful coverage status is not clean. Source-completed early/late equivalence alone still cannot create a full-baseline receipt because receipt creation requires `comparatorMode: raw_full_baseline` and `baselineSourceBoundaryMode: raw_original_source`.

## Direct Answer

The source-completed early-prefilter lane does not yet prove it can build its 167-span result without the late broad source/candidate universe. # EXEC-030 Phase 13AQ - Early Standalone Source Boundary

Status: Accepted for diagnostic implementation.

Branch: `route-line-v2-substrate`

Base commit: `b55210ea`

Fixture: `public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx`

## Direct Answer

`A. yes_early_prefilter_independent`, with one important boundary: the proof lane is independent of the late hinted lane, late candidate universe, late safeguard expansion, late topology input, and late ownership spans. It still starts from the upstream pre-late source-record boundary emitted by the V2 worker, so this is not a performance cutover and does not prove candidate generation can be skipped.

## Dependency Audit

| dependency | producing file/function | consuming file/function | category | early-owned replacement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input.roads` | V2 worker/evidence pipeline into `buildRouteLineV2TopologyPathWithCandidateHints` | old early prefilter planning in `topology-path-builder.ts` | broad source boundary before late filtering | `buildEarlyStandaloneSourceBoundary` consumes this as the upstream source boundary, merges bridge records, and filters to early-owned topology input. |
| `sourceCompletedRoads` | `topology-path-builder.ts` source-completion step | old late hinted path, old early prefilter, diagnostics | shared source-completed boundary | proof mode builds its own boundary result and does not read late hinted outputs. |
| `routeAlignedSafeguards` | `routeAlignedSafeguardWayIds({ roads: sourceCompletedRoads })` | old late candidate selection and old early prefilter | late/shared safeguard expansion | `buildEarlyStandaloneSourceBoundary` computes its own bounded route-aligned context refs from the proof boundary. |
| `candidateRoads` | late hinted candidate selection in `topology-path-builder.ts` | late hinted topology and diagnostics | late topology input | proof mode does not build or consume `candidateRoads`; it builds early topology input from the standalone boundary. |
| `hintedResult` | late hinted topology run | early-vs-late comparison and selection diagnostics | late topology output / diagnostic-only | proof mode poisons/disables late hinted lane, omits early-vs-late comparison, and emits standalone proof metrics instead. |

## Implementation

Added `src/lib/route-line-v2/early-standalone-source-boundary.ts`.

The helper:

- merges upstream source records with bridge-discovered verified records
- includes canonical required constituent refs
- computes early-owned route-aligned safeguard/context refs
- emits dependency flags showing no late candidate universe, late safeguard expansion, or late topology input consumption
- fails closed for disabled, missing source records, or empty topology input
- does not use display labels, family keys, or merged run IDs as source truth

Proof mode is enabled only through the debug/Test drawer lane. It:

- skips late hinted topology construction
- sets `lateHintedLaneExecuted: false`
- sets `lateHintedLanePoisoned: true`
- builds an early standalone topology result
- keeps `earlySubstratePrefilterSelected: false`
- keeps selected output diagnostic-only and governed outside early selection

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AR - Pre-Broad Early Source Boundary

Status: Accepted as a diagnostic-only audit.

Branch: `route-line-v2-substrate`

Base commit: `d333772f`

Fixture: `public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx`

## Direct Answer

`B. early_source_boundary_still_requires_broad_generation`

The current early standalone source boundary is independent of the late hinted lane, but it is still not pre-broad. It starts from `merged.roads`, the V2 evidence-pipeline source-record boundary produced before late hinted selection but after V2 evidence fetch/merge work has already run.

This phase does not implement early-prefilter selection, receipts, or a performance cutover.

## Upstream Boundary Audit

| field | value |
| --- | --- |
| dependency name | `merged.roads` / topology-builder `input.roads` |
| producing file/function | `src/lib/route-line-v2/evidence-pipeline.ts` via `runRouteLineV2EvidencePipeline` and `mergeRouteLineV2EvidenceResults(...)` |
| consuming file/function | `src/lib/route-line-v2/topology-path-builder.ts` via `buildRouteLineV2TopologyPath(...)` and early standalone boundary diagnostics |
| input source | V2 evidence fetch windows merged into route-line V2 road candidates |
| already paid broad evidence/candidate cost | yes |
| record count | 9,783 |
| unique OSM way count | 9,783 |
| route-windowed or route-wide | route-windowed evidence, not whole-route bbox/corridor, but still broad enough to materialize thousands of records |
| depends on V2 broad evidence fetch | yes |
| depends on late candidate materialization | no |
| depends on late safeguard expansion | no |
| depends on late topology input | no |
| replaceable by bounded source acquisition now | no |
| blocker | `missing_bounded_pre_broad_source_record_provider` |

The missing piece is a bounded pre-broad provider that can acquire the same source-completed input needed by the early lane from canonical substrate refs, route windows, topology windows, and bridge discovery without first materializing the 9,783-record V2 evidence boundary.

## Implementation

Added `src/lib/route-line-v2/early-source-boundary-acquisition.ts`.

The audit helper reports:

- direct A/B/C answer

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AS - Bounded Source Provider Audit

Status: Accepted as a diagnostic-only audit.

Branch: `route-line-v2-substrate`

Base commit: `69af167e`

Fixture context: `public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx`

## Direct Answer

`C. partially_possible_but_requires_provider_contract`

The current codebase has low-level RouteLine V2 evidence sources that can fetch explicit small bounds and parse the result into `RouteLineV2RoadCandidate` records:

- `RouteLineV2OwnedRoadsEvidenceSource`
- `RouteLineV2RawOsmRoadEvidenceSource`

That is not enough to call the current early lane pre-broad. Those sources are wired as evidence-pipeline sources, not as an early-owned bounded source-boundary provider. They also do not currently expose exact OSM way lookup, node-neighborhood lookup, or a topology-gap provider contract.

Strict answer: RouteLine V2 is partially capable of tiny bounded road-record acquisition, but the current early prefilter path still requires the broad V2 evidence boundary until a real provider contract is added and wired before evidence fetch/merge.

## Current Source Boundary Chain

| step | file/function | output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Route axis | `src/lib/route-line-v2/evidence-pipeline.ts` / `runRouteLineV2EvidencePipeline` | `routeAxis` |
| Window planning | `planRouteLineV2EvidenceWindowsWithDiagnostics` | route-windowed evidence windows |
| Source fetch | `fetchForWindow(...)` in `evidence-pipeline.ts` | `RouteLineV2RoadEvidenceResult[]` |
| Owned source | `RouteLineV2OwnedRoadsEvidenceSource.fetchRoadEvidence` | Overpass-proxy small/bounded bbox results as V2 road candidates |
| Raw source | `RouteLineV2RawOsmRoadEvidenceSource.fetchRoadEvidence` | raw Overpass-proxy small/bounded bbox results as V2 road candidates |
| Merge | `mergeRouteLineV2EvidenceResults(...)` in `src/lib/route-line-v2/merged-source.ts` | `merged.roads` |
| Topology builder | `buildRouteLineV2TopologyPath({ roads: merged.roads, ... })` | full/late/early diagnostic topology inputs |

The boundary that 13AR audited is `merged.roads`, consumed as topology-builder `input.roads`. For short urban, that boundary contained 9,783 records / 9,783 unique OSM ways. It is route-windowed evidence, not a whole-route bbox/corridor fetch, but it has already paid V2 evidence fetch and merge cost.

## Provider Capability Audit

| candidate | real provider | returns V2 road candidates | tiny route window today | exact way lookup today | node/topology-window lookup today | pre-broad wired today | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RouteLineV2OwnedRoadsEvidenceSource` | yes | yes | yes, via explicit bounds/window | no | no | no | partial |
| `RouteLineV2RawOsmRoadEvidenceSource` | yes | yes | yes, via explicit bounds/window | no | no | no | partial |
| `RouteLineV2FixtureRoadEvidenceSource` | no, fixture-only | yes | yes | no | no | no | rejected |
| topology bridge fixture provider | no, fixture/in-memory only | yes | yes | no | no | no | rejected |
| `merged.roads` | no, already materialized boundary | yes | no | no | no | no | rejected |
| late candidate arrays | no, late artifact | yes | no | no | no | no | rejected |
| `osm_road_tile_cache` / tile cache | yes for V1 corridor data | no, returns `SpeedRoad[]` whole tiles | no | no | no | no | rejected |
| `route_cache` | no, completed-analysis cache | no | no | no | no | no | rejected |

## Direct Questions

- Producing file/function for `merged.roads`: `src/lib/route-line-v2/evidence-pipeline.ts`, `runRouteLineV2EvidencePipeline`, after `fetchForWindow(...)` and `mergeRouteLineV2EvidenceResults(...)`.
- Source for `merged.roads`: RouteLine V2 owned/raw evidence source results, fetched through Overpass proxy semantics and merged by OSM way id.
- Smaller window acquisition possible today: partially. Low-level sources can use `startDistM`, `endDistM`, and `explicitBounds`, but the early lane has no provider contract wired before evidence fetch/merge.
- Exact OSM way lookup possible today: no. `lookupRoads` influences verification/fallback strategy; it does not build a `way(id)` query.
- Node/topology-window lookup possible today: no. Node ids are parsed when the bbox query returns them, but there is no provider request by neighbor node ids or endpoint topology window.
- Requires new backend/source index: not for a debug tiny-bbox Overpass proof, but yes for a production-grade exact-way/node-neighborhood provider or compact sub-tile topology window provider.
- Client tile cache can answer this without fetching whole tiles: no. `tile-cache.ts` reads whole tile keys through `/rpc/get_road_tiles` and returns `SpeedRoad[]`, not compact sub-tile RouteLine V2 topology records.
- Estimated scope:
  - debug contract + tiny explicit-bounds provider proof: one focused phase
  - exact way-id and node-neighborhood query modes through Overpass/source-owned proxy: one to two additional focused phases
  - production indexed source provider or compact tile-window RPC: larger backend/schema/API phase

## Provider Contract Needed

Minimum missing piece:

`Add an early-owned bounded source provider contract before evidence fetch/merge, with exact way-id and/or node/topology-window query modes.`

The provider must support:

- request by route-distance window or topology gap, not whole route corridor
- request by canonical OSM way ids when already known
- request by neighboring node ids or endpoint coordinates when connector ids are unknown
- return `RouteLineV2RoadCandidate` records with `osmWayId`, `coords`, `nodeIds`, `tags`, source lineage, and domain
- report `broadSearchUsed` and fail closed when a broad corridor/tile fetch is required
- avoid fixture-only records, display labels, family keys, merged run ids, late candidate arrays, and `merged.roads`

## Diagnostic Output

Added `src/lib/route-line-v2/bounded-source-provider-audit.ts`.

Current audit result:

- direct answer: `partially_possible_but_requires_provider_contract`
- real tiny-window provider exists: true
- RouteLine V2 candidate records possible today: true
- exact OSM way lookup possible today: false
- node topology-window lookup possible today: false
- current early boundary still requires `merged.roads`: true
- client tile cache can answer without whole tiles: false
- usable provider kinds: `v2_owned_overpass_explicit_bounds`, `v2_raw_overpass_explicit_bounds`
- rejected provider kinds include fixture source, merged-roads boundary, tile cache, route cache, and late candidate arrays

No runtime selection behavior was changed.

## Boundary Confirmation

- no production SQL executed
- no Supabase writes added
- no persistence writes added
- no route_cache coupling added
- no scoring or heatmap cutover added
- no default UI behavior changed
- no early-prefilter selected output added
- no broad corridor search disguised as bounded acquisition added
- no route-specific hardcoded allowlists added
- no display/family/merged-run identity truth added
- substrate remains noncanonical

## Verification

Tests and checks:

- `npx vitest run src/lib/route-line-v2/bounded-source-provider-audit.test.ts`
- affected RouteLine V2 diagnostic tests listed in final summary
- `npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false`
- `git diff --check`
- boundary greps for route relation writes, route cache coupling, browser-persistent proof/receipt storage, scoring/heatmap/default UI cutover, and early selected-result names

## Recommendation

Do not move to early-prefilter selection. The next phase should define and wire a debug-only bounded source provider contract. The smallest honest proof can use existing owned/raw Overpass explicit-bounds capability, but it must be called through a new early-owned provider seam and must fail closed until exact-way or topology-gap request semantics are explicit.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AT — Substrate Granular Provider Audit

**Status:** Accepted as provider-gap audit.

## Direct Answer

**C. partial_granular_records_exist_but_need_provider_contract**

RouteLine V2 cannot currently build its minimal topology input from a queryable granular substrate cache before `merged.roads` is materialized.

The codebase has granular substrate record shapes, but they are build-time or preview/debug artifacts. There is no real runtime/debug provider that can query canonical substrate way/node records by route window, tile sub-window, source ref, or topology gap and return RouteLine V2-ready topology records before `merged.roads`.

## Audit Findings

| Source | Granular Fields Present | Queryable Before `merged.roads` | RouteLine V2 Topology Ready | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `CyclistSubstrateSourceWay` | partial: `osmWayId`, `nodeIds`, geometry, highway/tags, name/ref | no provider | no domain/family/freshness contract | partial shape only |
| `CyclistSubstrateCachePreviewCandidate` | partial: `osmWayId`, geometry, highway/tags, name/ref, corridor metadata | no provider | missing `nodeIds`, source freshness, RouteLine domain contract | partial artifact only |
| `CyclistSubstrateLogicalCorridor.memberGeometries` | partial: per-way id/geometry/highway/tags under corridor grouping | no provider | missing `nodeIds`, source freshness, RouteLine domain contract | partial artifact only |
| simplified substrate corridors / GeoJSON tiles | merged corridor geometry and source way ids | tile artifacts only | no canonical way/node records | rejected |
| fixture substrate records | can carry complete records | fixture-only | test-only | rejected as proof |
| heatmap/span adapters | no canonical way/node topology record contract | no | no | rejected |
| `route_cache` | completed route cache | no | no | rejected |

## What Exists

The substrate build path preserves enough information to show the direction:

- `CyclistSubstrateSourceWay` has `osmWayId`, `nodeIds`, source geometry, highway/tags, name/ref, and optional relation refs.
- `CyclistSubstrateCachePreviewCandidate` preserves per-way geometry and candidate/corridor metadata before simplified tile output.
- `CyclistSubstrateLogicalCorridor.memberGeometries` keeps per-way member geometries under merged corridor identity.

These are not exposed through a queryable granular substrate cache.

## What Does Not Exist Yet

No current provider can answer:

- route-window query for canonical substrate way/node records
- topology-gap query using neighboring way/node context
- exact source-ref/OSM-way query against substrate records
- tile sub-window query that returns only compact canonical records

without using one of the forbidden sources:

- heatmap spans
- merged display spans
- route cache
- scoring/heatmap adapters
- already-materialized `merged.roads`
- fixture-only records

## Required Provider Contract

A real granular substrate provider should expose a narrow query API:

```ts
interface RouteLineV2GranularSubstrateRecord {
  osmWayId: number;
  nodeIds: number[];
  coords: Array<[number, number]>;
  familyKey: string;
  displayLabel: string;
  highway: string;
  domain: string;
  sourceLineage: {
    source: string;
    sourceVersion?: string;
    osmSnapshotDate?: string;
    substrateVersion?: string;
  };
  freshness: 'fresh' | 'cached' | 'stale' | 'unknown';
}
```

Supported query modes should include:

- tiny route window
- topology gap / node-neighborhood window
- canonical OSM way ids or source refs
- bounded tile sub-window, not whole tile materialization followed by filtering

The provider must report:

- provider mode
- input query bounds
- returned record count
- unique way count
- freshness/source snapshot
- `broadSearchUsed: false`
- failure reason when it cannot answer narrowly

## Boundary

No production SQL was executed. No Supabase writes, persistence writes, lookup/reload, route cache coupling, scoring/heatmap cutover, default UI behavior change, or early-prefilter selection was added.

Substrate remains noncanonical and cannot become route truth from this audit.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AU — Urban Hazard Queryable Substrate Provider

Status: Accepted for diagnostic implementation.

## Purpose

Phase 13AT found that Lanterne has granular substrate-like artifacts, but no provider contract that RouteLine V2 can query before `merged.roads` is materialized.

Phase 13AU adds an urban-hazard-only, in-memory provider that wraps existing granular fixture artifacts behind a production-shaped query API. This is a contract proof over one tiny corpus, not a nationwide substrate and not a production source.

Graph records remain upstream. Derived substrate spans are derived from graph records. Heat tile payloads are display adapters only and are not topology truth.

## Provider

Provider mode: `urban_hazard_fixture_in_memory`

Provider version: `exec-030-13au-urban-hazard-queryable-provider-v1`

Implemented file:

- `src/lib/route-line-v2/urban-hazard-queryable-substrate-provider.ts`

The provider exposes debug-only equivalents of:

- `queryWaysByRouteWindow`
- `queryWaysByTopologyGap`
- `queryWaysBySourceRefs`
- `queryWaysByTileWindow`
- `queryNodesByWayIds`
- `querySubstrateSpansByTileWindow`
- `querySubstrateSpansByViewport`
- `querySubstrateSpansBySourceRefs`
- `querySubstrateHeatTile`

It also exposes a RouteLine V2 evidence-source adapter for debug topology compatibility.

## Source Artifacts

Source artifact types used:

- `topology_bridge_probe_record`
- `source_ref_derivation_evidence`
- `derived_substrate_span`
- `debug_heat_tile_adapter`

The topology read model returns granular way records with:

- `osmWayId`
- `nodeIds`
- `coords`
- `familyKey`
- `displayLabel`
- `highway`
- `domain`
- source lineage and snapshot/version
- constituent/source refs

The span read model returns derived spans with:

- `substrateSpanId`
- geometry
- display label and class
- heat/risk bucket
- constituent OSM way/node refs
- source refs
- source lineage and snapshot/version

The heat tile adapter returns features that preserve:

- substrate span ID
- constituent way IDs
- constituent node IDs
- source refs

## Contract Proof

Manual/contract smoke fixture:

- `public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx`

Observed by focused provider tests:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Provider mode | `urban_hazard_fixture_in_memory` |
| Topology route-window query | 3 bridge-discovered ways |
| Topology gap query | 3 bridge-discovered ways |
| Known missing IDs supplied to gap query | rejected |
| Source-ref way query | supported |
| Node-by-way query | supported |
| Span viewport query | 2 spans |
| Heat tile feature count | 2 features |
| `merged.roads` read | false |
| `route_cache` read | false |
| Persistence mutated | false |
| Broad search used | false |
| RouteLine V2 topology provider compatibility | yes, debug-only |
| Full-map heat provider compatibility | yes, urban hazard viewport only |
| Substrate accepted as truth | false |
| Production analysis changed | false |

Bridge-discovered records returned by topology gap/window query:

- `1511491234`
- `1516936489`
- `1516936492`

Derived connector refs returned with source-ref derivation metadata:

- `1389989213`
- `556215894`

Every returned derived span preserves constituent way refs. Every heat tile feature points back to a substrate span ID and constituent refs.

## Identity Rules

Accepted canonical identity inputs:

- OSM way refs
- OSM node refs where present
- source refs
- topology gap/window context

Rejected as standalone topology truth:

- display label
- family key
- merged run ID

`queryWaysByTopologyGap` rejects calls that pass known target IDs as the success path. This phase proves queryable gap/window records over the urban hazard corpus, not exact-ID-only hydration.

## Caveats

This is fixture-backed and in-memory. It proves the API shape and RouteLine V2 compatibility over one tiny corpus.

It is not a real pre-broad provider for production routes. A production implementation still needs a granular substrate provider backed by queryable source records with canonical way/node geometry, source lineage, and freshness.

The heat tile adapter is display-only. It is not used as topology truth.

## Boundaries

- No production SQL.
- No Supabase writes.
- No persistence writes.
- No lookup/reload.
- No `route_cache` coupling.
- No scoring cutover.
- No heatmap production cutover.
- No default UI behavior change.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13AX — Urban Hazard Substrate Topology-Grade Audit

Status: diagnostic-only; fail closed.

## Direct Answer

The earlier `unsupported_topology_edge_shape` bucket was too coarse. The 51 records had ordered node IDs and coordinates; they were classified as unsupported because the audit only treated bridge, connector, or corridor-member lineage as supported edge shape. That was not a DS-032 edge-shape failure.

After validating the actual node-to-coordinate adapter contract:

- `unsupported_topology_edge_shape`: 0 ways
- `topology_grade`: 56 ways
- `broken_node_continuity`: 54 ways as a secondary graph-continuity deficit

The provider still produces only 9 RouteLine V2 spans because the corpus is edge-shape-valid but not graph-continuous enough for the full DS-032 route path.

Follow-up graph-continuity audit answer:

The 56 individually topology-grade substrate ways still produce only 9 provider-sourced V2 spans because the provider graph is not yet a connected route graph. The records have valid per-way `nodeIds` and `coords`, but many neighboring route-ordered records either use synthetic per-way node namespaces at touching coordinates, have connector records present but not admitted by the provider path solve, or need bounded deficit-fill records for missing shared-node continuity.

Not the blocker:

- corpus count
- `merged.roads` hardwire
- node ID / coordinate field naming
- node-to-coordinate count mapping
- missing display label / family key
- missing domain / highway / source lineage
- heat tile/span adapter availability

| `unsupported_topology_edge_shape` | 0 |

## Repair Decision

No source harness repair was forced in this phase.

The existing DS-034/DS-035-shaped harness artifacts expose IDs, node IDs, coords, labels, domains, highway, and lineage. The adapter now recognizes all 56 as DS-032 edge-shape-valid. They still do not provide enough connected source geometry for the full Urban Hazard V2 path. Repairing the remaining 54 graph-continuity deficits requires a bounded source/topology hydration artifact, not a broad `merged.roads` copy and not heat/display spans.

Follow-up decision: no graph-continuity repair was forced. The audit reduced the blocker from a generic count to specific transition-level causes. The next bounded repair should normalize real shared-node identity where DS-034/DS-035 source artifacts provide it, admit already-present connectors only when route/topology evidence supports them, and use bounded deficit-fill windows for missing connectors.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13BA — Bounded Substrate Deficit Fill Execution

Status: Accepted as a diagnostic fill-provider proof.

## Direct answer

Why did the 19 fill-attemptable windows produce 0 fills in 13AZ?

`A. no_fill_provider_wired`

13AZ planned bounded fill windows but did not execute a fill provider. 13BA wires the debug-only executor for the two allowed attemptable modes:

- `exact_way_id`
- `tiny_topology_gap_window`

After wiring the executor, the measured Urban Hazard result is:

- fill provider answer: `mixed`
- exact ID fill attempted: 9
- exact ID fill succeeded: 0
- topology gap fill attempted: 10
- topology gap fill succeeded: 0
- fill rejected count: 19
- supplemental way count: 0
- graph deficit count before fill: 51
- graph deficit count after fill: 51
- provider + fill span count: 8
- provider + fill blocker count: 5
- broad `merged.roads` read: false

The failure is now concrete:

- exact-ID fill requests return canonical records, but those records are already present in the provider boundary and do not add supplemental topology.
- tiny topology-gap fill requests mostly return no records from the existing mini provider; one returns an existing neighbor/bridge record rather than a new gap filler.

## Fill execution model

The fill provider contract is debug-only and noncanonical.

Inputs:

- bounded deficit window
- route-distance window
- neighboring way IDs
- neighboring node IDs and coordinates
- canonical fill way IDs only when source-ref derivation already provides them

Outputs:

- supplemental topology-grade way records
- fill reason
- source lineage
- source refs where available
- `broadSearchUsed: false`

Rejected outputs remain fail-closed.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13BC — Urban Hazard Fixture Topology Validity Audit

Status: Accepted diagnostic correction.

## Direct Answer

`B. synthetic_visual_debug_route`

`public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx` is not a valid RouteLine V2 topology proof fixture.

The route was hand-authored as a Phase 0 visual/debug smoke route. Visual inspection showed that the line cuts across blocks and uses synthetic curves that do not follow the Kansas City street grid. That means real OSM/source candidates cannot be expected to match it as route truth.

## Classification

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| fixture route provenance | `synthetic_visual_debug_route` |
| fixture route topology validity | `invalid_for_topology_proof` |
| topology proof allowed | `false` |
| exact topology geometry coverage | `incomplete` |

## Consequence

Urban Hazard is no longer valid evidence for:

- provider-sourced V2 topology
- early-prefilter correctness
- substrate-first candidate acquisition
- source-completed equivalence
- route ownership equivalence

Prior provider/topology failures against this fixture are not evidence that the substrate provider cannot work. They are evidence that a synthetic route cannot validate DS-032 topology.

## Allowed Uses

Urban Hazard remains useful for:

- UI/debug overlay smoke
- Test drawer wiring
- synthetic route visualization
- guardrail tests that do not claim real topology validity

## Follow-Up Recommendation

Build a real short urban topology fixture from an actual street-following GPX/RWGPS/OSRM-routed line.

The replacement topology fixture should:

- follow actual OSM roads/paths
- avoid synthetic straight-line cuts across blocks
- have known source/provenance
- have expected ownership windows in route-distance terms
- be short enough for fast iteration
- include normal streets
- include one connector
- include one turn/handoff
- include one ambiguous nearby road or cross-street rejection case

The local candidate route supplied by the user is:

- `/Users/derekminner/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/iCloud Sync/lanterne/Test Loop 1 - CCW.gpx`

That route should be evaluated in a separate phase before being promoted to a topology proof fixture.

- no production SQL
- no persistence

The current local Test Loop corpus still falls back to `coordinate_derived_from_exact_member_geometry` because the checked diagnostic subset was extracted before the South Jersey source artifact preserved OSM way node refs.

The source artifact writer now preserves node refs when they are present in owned/local source inputs:

- `element.nodes` from source element JSON
- `ways[].nodeIds` from already-shaped substrate artifacts
- `properties.nodeIds` / `properties.nodes` from source GeoJSON when supplied

The exact missing field in the older artifact is `ways[].nodeIds`. RouteLine V2 provider records now use `real_osm_node_ids` when that field is available and use coordinate-derived node IDs only as a fallback. Diagnostics distinguish:

- `real_osm_node_ids`
- `coordinate_derived_from_exact_member_geometry`
- `mixed_real_and_coordinate_derived`

The raw RouteLine V2 source parser already preserves `element.nodes`; this hardening prevents the South Jersey substrate build artifact from dropping the same refs during source artifact conversion.

The diagnostic provider proof remains unchanged in behavior:

- accepted ways: `11613459`, `1388406931`, `1388406932`, `971362311`
- ownership spans: 2
- blockers: 0
- provider output selected: false
- substrate accepted as truth: false

The per-source-way contribution table remains the audit mechanism that prevents coalesced display spans from hiding actual OSM way participation.

Accepted way node source modes in the current local proof:

| OSM way ID | Node source mode |
| --- | --- |
| `11613459` | `coordinate_derived_from_exact_member_geometry` |
| `1388406931` | `coordinate_derived_from_exact_member_geometry` |
| `1388406932` | `coordinate_derived_from_exact_member_geometry` |
| `971362311` | `coordinate_derived_from_exact_member_geometry` |

Phase 13BE confirmed that the current local South Jersey artifact cannot prove end-to-end real OSM node continuity because it also lacks node refs. To get end-to-end real OSM node continuity, regenerate or replace `.tmp/substrate/south-jersey/source-overpass-ways.json` from the owned/local OSM source artifact that includes either `element.nodes` or `ways[].nodeIds`, then rebuild the Test Loop source subset from that artifact. Do not use public Overpass except as an explicit fallback.
