# EXEC-030 Phase 13BI — Test Loop V2S+S Replacement Readiness Report

Status: Diagnostic/reporting implementation.

## Direct Answer

For Test Loop only:

`A. yes_full_pre_scoring_parity`

V2S+S reaches full pre-scoring parity for `public/demo/fixture-test-loop-1-ccw-short.gpx`.

This means V2S+S can produce:

- route identity spans
- real-node handoffs
- truth-run-compatible output
- display-segment-compatible output
- cue/handoff summary
- per-source-way contribution diagnostics
- scoring missing-field audit
- heatmap missing-field audit

It does not mean scoring or heatmap integration is complete.

Current downstream parity remains `display_parity`, with scoring and heatmap fields explicitly missing rather than fabricated.

## Current Test Loop Facts

| Diagnostic | Value |
| --- | --- |
| fixture | `public/demo/fixture-test-loop-1-ccw-short.gpx` |
| provenance | `real_gpx_strava_route` |
| topology proof allowed | true |
| source mode | `queryable_substrate_provider_debug` |
| provider node ref mode | `real_osm_node_ids` |
| provider topology records | 8 |
| accepted way IDs | `11613459`, `971362311`, `1388406931`, `1388406932` |
| ownership spans | 2 |
| handoffs | 1 |
| blockers | 0 |
| relation valid | true |
| validation errors | 0 |
| recent V2S+S elapsed | roughly 28-38ms |
| provider output selected | false |
| substrate accepted as truth | false |

The 2 ownership spans are acceptable for display/ownership because same-family contiguous Tuckerton Road ways are coalesced. The per-source-way contribution table remains required so the coalescing does not hide OSM way participation.

## V1 Work Remaining Above V2S+S

| V1 bucket | Current status |
| --- | --- |
| ingest | measured only when same-fixture V1 route-load diagnostics are present |
| fetch/source acquisition | measured only when same-fixture V1 route-load diagnostics are present |
| build/match | closest identity-layer comparison bucket, measured only when emitted by V1 diagnostics |
| enrichment | measured only if emitted separately |
| scoring | not separately measured in this report |
| heatmap build | measured only if emitted separately |
| display/render handoff | measured only if emitted separately |
| cue generation | not separately measured in this report |
| unknown/unattributed | grouped/estimated from total minus known buckets when V1 same-fixture metrics are available |

The report helper labels grouped buckets as grouped/estimated. It does not fake precision.

## Consolidated Performance Table

| Row | Current value | Label |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| V1 total measured | not measured | same-fixture V1 full route-load total is required |
| V1 fetch/source acquisition | not measured | same-fixture V1 fetch/source bucket is required |
| V1 build/match | not measured | same-fixture V1 build/match bucket is required for identity-layer timing comparison |
| V1 enrichment/scoring/display/cue grouped | not measured | use `V1 total - ingest - fetch - build/match` when same-fixture buckets exist |
| V2S+S identity + adapters measured | roughly 28-38ms in recent runs | V2S+S measured identity + display parity |
| V2S+S missing scoring/heatmap fields | scoring: speed, traffic/AADT, shoulder, bike infra, hazard flags, surface; heatmap: speed/risk/traffic/AADT cache fields | scoring integration deferred; heatmap integration deferred |
| projected V2S+S full-app estimate using measured V1 downstream cost | not measured | `V2S+S identity + adapters + V1 downstream grouped` |
| confidence | low for full-app projection; high for pre-scoring parity | full-app estimate needs same-fixture V1 downstream buckets |

Projection formula:

```text
V2S+S projected full route-load =
  V2S+S measured identity + adapters
  + V1 measured downstream enrichment/scoring/display/cue work
```

Identity-layer comparison formula:

```text
identity-layer improvement =
  V1 build/match
  - V2S+S measured identity + adapters
```

No current result should be labeled "V2S+S beats V1 full-app" because V2S+S has not run equivalent scoring, heatmap, enrichment, cue, and production display work.

## Editorial Conclusion

For Test Loop, the replacement risk has moved past route identity/topology and display handoff. V2S+S has a valid pre-scoring replacement shape: it builds identity spans, real-node handoffs, truth-run adapters, display segment adapters, cue summaries, and source contribution diagnostics from queryable substrate provider records.

The remaining replacement work is downstream parity, not route identity. Scoring and heatmap fields are still missing and intentionally audited instead of fabricated.

V2S+S is therefore a pre-scoring replacement candidate, not a measured full-app replacement.

## Next Recommended Phase

EXEC-030 next: hydrate diagnostic scoring and heatmap input fields for Test Loop V2S+S without selecting provider output.

The next phase should keep V2S+S diagnostic-only and prove whether the missing scoring/heatmap fields can be supplied from existing source artifacts or bounded substrate/provider reads.

## Boundaries

- no production SQL
- no Supabase writes
- no persistence writes
- no lookup/reload
- no route_cache coupling
- no scoring cutover
- no heatmap cutover
- no default UI behavior change
- no V2S+S output selection
- no substrate-as-truth
- no arbitrary-GPX runner
- no Urban Hazard topology proof

V2S+S has proven the route identity and pre-scoring display surface for Test Loop:

- it produces 2 ownership spans, 1 handoff, 0 blockers, and 0 validation errors;
- it adapts to truth-run-compatible and display-segment-compatible outputs;

V2S+S has not proven full production replacement:

The identity layer is fast enough to justify continuing. Even with a conservative local diagnostic run at 81ms, the source envelope is tiny: 8 provider topology records and 4 accepted ways. # EXEC-030 Phase 13BL - V1 Evidence/Scoring Attachment Audit for V2S+S Migration

Status: Accepted audit/plan.

## Executive Summary

Direct answers:

1. V1 attaches score-driving evidence through the current route-analysis pipeline after corridor/tile road acquisition. OSM-like fields are first attached to `SpeedRoad` records, then projected onto sampled route points, cue entries, truth runs, canonical score slices, and heatmap segments.
2. The pieces that can move mostly as-is are the pure scoring math and presentation consumers once V2S+S emits the required input contracts. The current evidence attachment path itself should not move as-is.
3. Most evidence domains require adaptation to route-indexed V2 ownership spans because the V1 join surface is sample/cue/truth-run shaped.
4. Traffic, hazards, heatmap risk fields, and repeated display/scoring joins should be improved with a V2 route-indexed model instead of cloned from V1.

V2S+S Test Loop status is `pre_scoring_parity` / `display_parity`. It can produce route identity spans, real-node handoffs, truth-run-compatible output, display-segment-compatible output, cue/handoff summaries, per-source-way contribution diagnostics, and missing-field audits. It does not yet produce score-driving enrichment fields.

The recommended first implementation phase is a V2S+S evidence attachment contract that registers route-indexed layers needed for scoring, without selecting V2S+S output and without changing production scoring.

Biggest risks:

- Treating V2S+S display parity as scoring parity.
- Reusing V1 cue/sample joins and losing V2's route-distance ownership model.
- Hydrating broad corridor evidence instead of accepted source IDs.
- Letting heatmap/display adapters feed back into route truth.
- Collapsing coalesced display spans in a way that hides per-source-way scoring evidence.

## Current V1 Attachment Model

V1 builds a corridor road universe, parses OSM/source fields into road objects, matches route samples to roads, builds cue entries, exports truth runs, computes canonical score slices, then converts truth runs to heatmap/display segments.

Important current surfaces:

- `src/lib/corridor.ts`: parses source road elements into `SpeedRoad` objects with `id`, `coords`, `tags`, `speedLimit`, `speedClass`, `shoulder`, `scoreDomainType`, and safe-path/domain fields.
- `src/lib/route-analysis.ts`: matches sampled route points to `SpeedRoad` objects, builds cue entries, resolves traffic/lanes/shoulder/bike/surface evidence, emits truth runs, computes segment/crossing scoring, and synchronizes final truth evidence into display surfaces.
- `src/lib/hazards.ts`: detects route-relevant hazards from raw elements or parsed corridor roads.
- `src/lib/safety-scoring.ts`: owns DS-015 scoring math for continuous segments and crossing events.
- `src/lib/heatmap/types.ts` and `src/lib/heatmap/builder.ts`: define `TruthRunInput` / `HeatmapSegment` and convert scored truth runs into heatmap/display layers.
- `src/lib/traffic-time.ts`: applies time-of-day traffic multipliers for rider-facing traffic flow presentation.
- `src/lib/route-line-v2/v2ss-downstream-parity-adapter.ts`: current V2S+S diagnostic adapter into truth-run/display-compatible shapes, with explicit missing scoring/heatmap field audits.

## Evidence Attachment Matrix

| Evidence domain | Current V1 source/function | Current V1 join key | Current V1 consumer | V2S+S target layer | Migration class | Difficulty | Performance opportunity | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Speed / maxspeed | `corridor.ts` source parsing via `parseMaxspeed`; `route-analysis.ts` cue/truth-run speed resolution; `makeFinalTruthRunSpeedChosenInput` | Road object ID, sample index, cue entry, truth-run start/end indices | DS-015 scoring, score trace, heatmap, inspector/display | Route ownership span evidence keyed by accepted OSM way ID and route-distance interval | `adapt_to_route_indexed_spans` | Medium | Medium | Scoring math can reuse `speedRiskFactor`/`computeSegmentRisk`, but attachment should hydrate accepted ways instead of all corridor roads. |
| Traffic / AADT | `route-analysis.ts` HPMS/state DOT/OSM cue enrichment; `resolveCanonicalTraffic`; `resolveDs015TrafficFactor`; local-area predicted traffic | Route sample index, nearest matched road, HPMS/DOT geometry candidate, cue entry, truth run | DS-015 traffic factor, score trace, traffic provenance UI, heatmap risk fields | Route-indexed traffic evidence layer keyed by accepted way IDs plus route-distance overlap | `improve_with_v2_route_indexed_model` | High | Large | Biggest redesign opportunity. Hydrate accepted spans/source IDs and project once, instead of sampling over corridor candidates. |
| Shoulder | `corridor.ts` `parseShoulder`; `route-analysis.ts` HPMS/DOT shoulder overlay on cue entries; truth-run shoulder bucket | Road object tags, HPMS/DOT sample match, cue entry/truth run | DS-015 shoulder factor, display buckets, inspector | Route ownership span evidence with side/width provenance | `adapt_to_route_indexed_spans` | Medium | Medium | Preserve source and confidence. Do not infer missing shoulder silently. |
| Bike infrastructure | `route-analysis.ts` `detectBikeFacility`, sample bike facility override, strongest-wins infra bucket; OSM `cycleway*`/`bicycle` tags | Road object tags, sample index, cue entry/truth run | DS-015 infrastructure mitigation, safe-path/domain guard, heatmap/display | Route-indexed facility layer keyed by accepted source ways and source-member contributions | `adapt_to_route_indexed_spans` | Medium | Medium | V2 can preserve per-source-way contribution under coalesced display spans. |
| Surface | OSM `surface` tags through corridor roads and truth-run surface bucket; `estimateGravelKm(roads)` | Road tags, cue/truth-run modal bucket | Surface display, gravel estimate, hazard bridge rules, missing-field audit | Accepted-way surface evidence by route-distance contribution | `adapt_to_route_indexed_spans` | Medium | Small | Mostly stable route evidence. Needs no broad corridor scan if source records already carry tags. |
| Lane count | `route-analysis.ts` `parseOsmLaneCount`; HPMS `throughLanes`; state DOT lanes; `inferDs015LaneCount` | Road tags, traffic/DOT sample match, cue entry/truth run | Traffic per-lane resolution, crossing width, score trace | Route-indexed lane evidence with source-specific lane purpose | `adapt_to_route_indexed_spans` | Medium | Medium | V1 separates width lane count from traffic-trusted lane count. Preserve that distinction. |
| Road class / highway | `corridor.ts` `tags.highway`; `score-domain.ts` `classifyScoreDomainType`; truth-run highway/domain export | Road object tags, cue/truth-run modal highway | Speed baseline, traffic class proxy, domain, safe-path invariant, display | Accepted-way identity/domain layer | `move_as_is` for classifier, `adapt_to_route_indexed_spans` for attachment | Low | Small | The classifier can move as-is. Attachment should be per accepted way/span. |
| Hazards: railroad crossings | `hazards.ts` `detectHazardsFromElements` / `detectHazardsFromRoads`; `route-analysis.ts` route crossing filtering and clustering | Explicit OSM node, rail/road geometry intersection, nearest route point, matched/on-route road IDs | Crossing events, route score, overlays, inspector | Route-distance point/span event layer tied to handoffs and accepted route geometry | `improve_with_v2_route_indexed_model` | High | Medium | V2 real-node handoffs can improve event placement and dedupe. |
| Hazards: bridges, metal surfaces, dismount, covered, no-shoulder | `hazards.ts` bridge/surface/tag rules; `route-analysis.ts` bridge hazard export | Road-way tags, bridge outlines, route proximity, matched route roads | Hazard penalties/display, route receipt, overlays | Route-indexed hazard event/span layer keyed by accepted source way and route overlap | `adapt_to_route_indexed_spans` | Medium | Medium | Do not attach bridge hazards from nearby corridor roads that are not route-owned. |
| Hazards: underpasses / cattle grids / fords | `hazards.ts` `isSingleLaneUnderpass`, node/way barrier and ford rules; route snapping in `route-analysis.ts` | Explicit OSM node or road-way tag, route proximity, matched road IDs | Hazard penalties/display, receipt | Route-distance event layer | `adapt_to_route_indexed_spans` | Medium | Medium | Explicit nodes should join by real OSM node where available, then route-distance snap. |
| Time-of-day traffic multiplier | `traffic-time.ts` `getTrafficMultiplier`, `estimateArrivalHour`, `estimateTrafficFlow`, `formatTrafficAtTime` | Cue distance and rider start time / planned speed | Rider-facing traffic flow display | Contextual ride-time presentation layer on top of stable route traffic evidence | `move_as_is` for formatter, `defer` for score-driving use | Low | None | Contextual, not stable route identity. Do not bake into route truth. |
| Heatmap risk fields | `route-analysis.ts` truth-run `rawRisk`, `normalizedRisk`, `riskLevel`; `heatmap/builder.ts` `buildTruthSegments` | Truth-run route point index bounds and road identity | Route paint, heatmap, inspector, risk display | V2S+S scored truth-run adapter after scoring fields exist | `adapt_to_route_indexed_spans` | Medium | Medium | Heatmap builder can consume the same contract after V2 scoring. It must not be topology truth. |
| Cue generation inputs | `route-analysis.ts` cue sheet build; optional `topology-cues.ts`; left-turn/controlled/path crossing event logic | Sample index, road transition, route distance, truth-run boundary, handoff context | Cue sheet, crossing scoring, route receipt | V2 handoff summary plus route-distance cue event layer | `improve_with_v2_route_indexed_model` | Medium | Medium | V2 real-node handoffs should simplify transition cues and reduce sample-index fragility. |

## Migration Classification

### A. move_as_is

Use this only for pure logic that can consume V2 adapters without changing the evidence model:

- DS-015 segment and crossing scoring math in `src/lib/safety-scoring.ts`.
- Score-domain classification in `src/lib/score-domain.ts`, once V2 provides accepted way tags.
- Time-of-day traffic flow presentation helpers in `src/lib/traffic-time.ts`.
- Heatmap builder/display consumers after V2S+S emits complete `TruthRunInput` risk fields.
- Existing route paint/inspector consumers after V2S+S truth-run/display adapters are fully populated.

This does not mean V1 evidence attachment can move as-is.

### B. adapt_to_route_indexed_spans

These should attach to V2 ownership spans by accepted OSM way ID, real node handoff, and route-distance interval:

- Speed/maxspeed.
- Shoulder.
- Bike infrastructure.
- Surface.
- Lane count.
- Highway/road class attachment.
- Bridge/underpass/cattle grid/ford hazard events.
- Heatmap risk field export.

### C. improve_with_v2_route_indexed_model

These are structurally better in V2 than in the current V1 cue/sample model:

- Traffic/AADT hydration and propagation.
- Hazard event placement/dedupe.
- Cue generation around real-node handoffs.
- Per-source-way contribution under coalesced display spans.
- Shared route-indexed evidence layers reused by scoring, heatmap, inspection, and presentation.
- Worker-first staged pipeline where identity can return before score enrichment.

### Defer

- Production scoring cutover.
- Production heatmap cutover.
- Ride-time contextual traffic as score truth.
- Any-GPX provider generalization.
- Persistent route-indexed evidence cache.

## Scoring Pipeline Audit

Current V1 scoring path:

1. Corridor/source road acquisition produces `SpeedRoad` records with OSM tags, geometry, speed, shoulder, highway/domain, and source fields.
2. Route samples are matched to roads and cue entries are built.
3. Cue entries attach speed, traffic/AADT, lane count, shoulder, bike facility, safe-path/domain, surface, and road IDs.
4. Truth runs coalesce sampled road ownership and modal/strongest evidence buckets.
5. `computeSegmentRisk` scores continuous slices using speed severity, resolved traffic factor, infrastructure mitigation, shoulder factor, curvature factor, and route length.
6. Crossing events are built from left turns, controlled crossings, and path joins/exits, then scored with speed, traffic, width, control, and movement factors.
7. Route aggregation computes route risk per mile, road/crossing risk totals, worst 1 km band, confidence, and projection-layer score/grade surfaces.
8. Final truth runs carry `rawRisk`, `normalizedRisk`, `riskLevel`, resolved traffic fields, and provenance.
9. Heatmap/display layers consume those truth runs.

| Scoring stage | Reuse as-is? | Needs V2 route-indexed adapter? | Move to worker? | V2S+S speed opportunity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Speed severity math | Yes | Needs speed field attachment | Yes | Small |
| Traffic exposure math | Yes | Needs AADT/lane evidence attachment | Yes | Large, if hydrated only for accepted spans |
| Infrastructure mitigation | Yes | Needs bike facility evidence attachment | Yes | Medium |
| Shoulder factor | Yes | Needs shoulder evidence attachment | Yes | Medium |
| Curvature/geometry penalty | Mostly | Needs route-distance spans and route geometry mask | Yes | Small/medium |
| Hazard penalties/events | Partly | Needs route-indexed hazard events | Yes | Medium |
| Crossing scoring | Yes | Needs V2 handoff/cue event adapter | Yes | Medium |
| Risk per mile / route aggregation | Yes | Needs scored V2 spans/events | Yes | Small |
| Logistic normalization / letter grade projection | Yes, as projection | Needs full scored route result | Optional | None |
| Confidence/provenance rollup | Partly | Needs V2 evidence provenance fields | Yes | Medium |

The core DS-015 math should not be rewritten. The migration work is evidence attachment and adapter shape.

## Heatmap Audit

Current heatmap input is not raw roads. It is scored truth-run output:

- `TruthRunInput` carries route point bounds, road identity, display buckets, resolved traffic truth, and cached risk fields.
- `buildHeatmapLayers` builds truth segments from truth runs, then merges display segments by zoom band.
- Heatmap rendering expects cached risk fields and presentation buckets; it does not own route truth.

V2S+S needs to produce:

- `TruthRunInput` with route-distance/source identity represented as route point spans or an equivalent route-indexed projection.
- Scored fields: `rawRisk`, `normalizedRisk`, `riskLevel`.
- Traffic fields: `resolvedTrafficFactor`, `resolvedTrafficConfidence`, `resolvedAADTTotal`, lane count, provenance.
- Display buckets: speed, traffic, shoulder, infra, surface.
- Stable source lineage back to accepted way IDs and per-source-way contribution diagnostics.

Classification:

- Display geometry reusable: yes, after adapter output exists.
- Score/risk fields missing: yes, currently deferred.
- Route-distance spans enough: yes for target model, but current heatmap contract still expects point-index spans.
- Needs adapter: yes.
- Production cutover risk: medium/high until V2 scoring and heatmap parity are tested on more than Test Loop.

## Performance Hypothesis

V2S+S can improve total route analysis performance not because scoring arithmetic is faster, but because it can reduce evidence acquisition and attachment work by starting from accepted route ownership spans and hydrating only the evidence needed for those spans.

The likely wins are:

- Avoid broad corridor scans for evidence attachment.
- Attach evidence to accepted ownership spans instead of all corridor roads.
- Hydrate speed/AADT/shoulder/bike/surface only for accepted way IDs and bounded route windows.
- Batch evidence by accepted source IDs.
- Project evidence by route distance once and reuse it across scoring, heatmap, inspection, and cues.
- Avoid recomputing heatmap geometry from V1 truth fragments.
- Preserve per-source-way contribution under coalesced display spans.
- Run enrichment/scoring in a worker after identity is stable.
- Stream identity first, then score later.
- Cache route-indexed evidence layers independently in a future phase.
- Avoid duplicate joins across scoring, heatmap, cue, and inspector.
- Separate stable route evidence from ride-time/contextual evidence.

Counterpoint:

If V1 scoring/enrichment already operates only on matched roads after the broad route match, the biggest remaining gain may be reducing upstream source acquisition and matching cost, not the scoring arithmetic itself. The next benchmark needs to isolate evidence acquisition, evidence attachment, score math, heatmap build, and display handoff as separate buckets.

## Recommended Implementation Sequence

Phase A: V2S+S evidence attachment contract

- Define route-indexed evidence layers needed for scoring.
- Register required fields per layer.
- Keep missing fields audited, not fabricated.
- Preserve source IDs, route-distance intervals, node handoffs, and provenance.

Phase B: speed/road-class/surface/bike-infra attachment

- Attach from provider/source records by accepted OSM way ID and route-distance contribution.
- Reuse road-class/domain classifier.
- Produce scored-truth-run-compatible buckets, still diagnostic-only.

Phase C: AADT/traffic attachment

- Hydrate HPMS/DOT/source traffic by accepted spans/source IDs.
- Preserve total AADT, per-lane resolution, lane source, confidence, and provenance.
- Avoid broad corridor traffic scans where accepted IDs/window queries are sufficient.

Phase D: hazard attachment

- Attach railroad crossings, bridges, underpasses, cattle grids, fords, controlled crossings, and path/road crossing events as route-distance point/span events.
- Prefer real OSM node/event identity when available.
- Use V2 handoffs to improve event placement and dedupe.

Phase E: scoring adapter smoke

- Run DS-015 scoring against V2S+S evidence layers on Test Loop.
- Compare V1 and V2S+S score components, not just final score.
- Keep V2S+S unselected.

Phase F: heatmap adapter smoke

- Build V2S+S scored truth-run heatmap output in debug only.
- Compare display segments and risk fields with V1.
- Keep production heatmap unchanged.

Phase G: expand to another real route fixture

- Add one more topology-proof route with real street following, turns, hazards/crossings if possible, and nontrivial evidence fields.
- Do not use Urban Hazard as a topology proof fixture.

## Audit-Level Test Guidance

No production code changes are required for this phase. If pure mapping helpers are added later, test that:

- The evidence migration matrix covers every current V1 score-driving field.
- No field is marked `move_as_is` without a target V2S+S adapter.
- Missing scoring fields remain audited, not fabricated.
- Route distance is the target join key for V2S+S evidence layers.
- `substrateAcceptedAsTruth` remains false.

## Boundary Confirmation

This phase does not:

- implement scoring integration,
- change production scoring,
- change heatmap production behavior,
- select V2S+S output,
- touch route cache, persistence, lookup/reload, or default UI,
- treat substrate as route truth,
- generalize to arbitrary GPX,
- use Urban Hazard as topology proof.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13BM - V2S+S Worker and Scoring Contract

Status: Accepted diagnostic contract implementation.

## Direct Answer

B. `partial_v1_scoring_math_reusable_but_input_adapter_needed`

The existing V1 scoring engine can be exposed behind a V2 route-indexed scoring-worker contract without changing production scoring, but not by passing V1 cue/truth-run evidence attachment through unchanged.

Reusable now:

- DS-015 segment and crossing scoring math.
- Score-domain classification once V2 evidence layers provide highway/domain fields.
- Heatmap/display consumers after V2 scoring emits scored truth/heatmap input spans.

Blockers before real scoring parity:

- V2S+S does not yet have a route-indexed evidence worker.
- Score-driving fields are still missing from the V2S+S evidence bundle.
- Heatmap risk fields are still missing from V2S+S output.
- V1 traffic/hazard attachment is still coupled to sample/cue/truth-run shapes.
- Production scoring and heatmap cutover remain explicitly forbidden in this phase.

## Worker Architecture Summary

The target V2 route analysis pipeline is staged:

1. Identity worker
   - Route axis.
   - Substrate/provider topology.
   - Ordered path.
   - Ownership spans.
   - Handoffs.
   - Blockers.
   - Truth/display pre-scoring adapters.

2. Evidence worker
   - Attaches route-indexed evidence layers:
     - `speed_limit`
     - `traffic_aadt`
     - `shoulder`
     - `bike_infra`
     - `surface`
     - `road_class/highway`
     - `lane_count`
     - `hazard_events`
     - `time_of_day_traffic_multiplier`
   - Emits an evidence bundle keyed by route distance.

3. Scoring worker
   - Consumes the route-indexed evidence bundle.
   - Runs the shared scoring engine later.
   - Emits score spans, rollups, score trace, heatmap input spans, explanation payloads, and missing-field diagnostics.

4. Detour / route alternative scoring
   - Must call the same scoring worker contract.
   - Must not use a separate detour-only scoring shortcut.

## Why Not One Mega-Worker Forever

A single mega-worker would hide the distinction between route identity, evidence attachment, scoring, heatmap preparation, and presentation handoff. That is the same kind of coupling that made V1 hard to audit.

The staged boundary matters because V2S+S can prove identity first, then attach stable route evidence, then score. It also lets future UI stream identity before slower traffic/hazard/scoring work completes.

## Why Not Many Tiny Workers Yet

This phase should not split every evidence domain into its own worker. The immediate need is a stable message and data contract. Too many workers before the route-indexed evidence shape is proven would create orchestration noise without improving correctness.

Recommended initial split:

- Identity worker.
- Evidence worker.
- Scoring worker.

Domain-specific evidence modules can live inside the evidence worker first.

## Implemented Now

Added:

- `src/lib/route-line-v2/v2ss-worker-contracts.ts`
- `src/lib/route-line-v2/v2ss-worker-contracts.test.ts`
- `src/lib/route-line-v2/v2ss-route-indexed-evidence-contract.test.ts`

Implemented contract types:

- Worker lifecycle/message types:
  - `identity_worker_started`
  - `identity_worker_ready`
  - `evidence_worker_started`
  - `evidence_layer_ready`
  - `evidence_bundle_ready`
  - `scoring_worker_started`
  - `scoring_worker_ready`
  - `scoring_worker_blocked`
  - `detour_score_request`
  - `detour_score_response`
  - `worker_progress`
  - `worker_error`
  - `worker_cancelled`
- `V2SSRouteIndexedEvidenceBundle`
- `V2SSScoringWorkerInput`
- `V2SSScoringWorkerOutput`
- `V2SSDetourScoreRequest`
- `V2SSDetourScoreResponse`
- readiness diagnostics

Every worker message requires:

- `runId`
- `routeFingerprint`
- `stage`
- `elapsedMs`
- `status`
- `warnings`
- optional source/candidate counts
- `substrateAcceptedAsTruth: false` when relevant

## Contract Boundaries

### Identity Worker

Input and output remain centered on route identity:

- Route axis.
- Provider topology records.
- Ordered path.
- Ownership spans.
- Handoffs.
- Blockers.

It must not score, hydrate traffic, or produce production heatmap truth.

### Evidence Worker

The evidence worker target is `V2SSRouteIndexedEvidenceBundle`.

The bundle is keyed by:

- `routeFingerprint`
- `routeDistanceM`
- `ownershipSpans`
- source way/node contributions
- route-distance intervals inside each evidence layer

It carries:

- `evidenceLayers`
- `missingLayers`
- `coverageSummary`
- `provenanceSummary`
- `confidenceSummary`
- `scoringReadiness`
- `heatmapReadiness`

Missing fields remain explicit. They are not fabricated.

### Scoring Worker

The scoring worker target input is `V2SSScoringWorkerInput`.

It consumes:

- route fingerprint
- route distance
- ownership spans
- evidence bundle
- scoring model version
- optional rider context
- mode:
  - `full_route_score`
  - `detour_preview_score`
  - `route_alternative_compare`
- `debugOnly`

The output can represent blocked scoring:

- `scoringComplete: false`
- empty score spans
- missing score fields
- warnings

That is intentional for this phase.

### Detour Scoring

The detour contract is `V2SSDetourScoreRequest`.

It supports:

- `baseRouteFingerprint`
- `candidateRouteFingerprint`
- `candidateGeometry`
- `affectedRouteWindow`
- optional candidate ownership spans
- optional candidate evidence bundle
- mode `detour_preview_score`

The detour request converts into the same `V2SSScoringWorkerInput` shape. This prevents future detour routing from growing a separate scoring shortcut.

## Readiness Diagnostics

Current skeleton readiness:

- `identityWorkerContractReady: true`
- `evidenceWorkerContractReady: true`
- `scoringWorkerContractReady: true`
- `detourScoringContractReady: true`
- `scoringIntegrationDeferred: true`
- `heatmapIntegrationDeferred: true`
- `productionCutoverFalse: true`
- `providerOutputSelected: false`
- `substrateAcceptedAsTruth: false`

Direct answer remains:

`partial_v1_scoring_math_reusable_but_input_adapter_needed`

## Deferred Work

This phase does not:

- run real V2S+S scoring,
- integrate production scoring,
- change V1 scoring,
- change heatmap production behavior,
- change detour routing behavior,
- select V2S+S output,
- persist route relations,
- touch route cache,
- generalize to arbitrary GPX,
- use Urban Hazard as topology proof.

## Recommended Next Phase

13BN - Evidence Worker Skeleton for Low-Risk OSM/Provider Fields

Fields:

- `road_class/highway`
- `maxspeed` if present
- `surface` if present
- `bike_infra` if present
- `lane_count` if present

That phase should attach stable source/provider fields to V2S+S route-distance ownership spans and keep scoring/heatmap deferred until evidence coverage is measurable.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13BO: V2S+S Scoring Input Readiness Gate

## Direct Answer

C. `partial_score_input_shape_ready_but_fields_missing`

The Test Loop V2S+S evidence bundle can be adapted into the scoring worker input shape, but it is not score-runnable. The gate blocks scoring because required score-driving fields are missing. No score spans, route score, or heatmap input spans are emitted.

## Current Test Loop Evidence

Fixture: `public/demo/fixture-test-loop-1-ccw-short.gpx`

Provider mode: `queryable_substrate_provider_debug`

| Evidence field | Status | Coverage | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |

| `highway` | ready | 100% | Attached from provider highway tags |
| `surface` | missing | 0% | Provider tags do not include surface |

| `lane_count` | missing | 0% | Provider tags do not include lanes |

## Score-Driving Fields

Present:

- `road_class`
- `highway`

Missing:

- `speed_limit`
- `traffic_aadt`
- `shoulder`
- `bike_infra`
- `lane_count`

Required field groups can declare fallback policy later, but this phase does not apply fallback values. The readiness gate reports `fallback_policy_needed` and `fallback_not_applied` when a required field is absent.

## Gate Result

| Field | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `scoringInputShapeReady` | `true` |
| `scoringRunnable` | `false` |

| `heatmapIntegrationDeferred` | `true` |

| `substrateAcceptedAsTruth` | `false` |

Blocked scoring output follows the 13BM contract:

- `type`: `scoring_worker_blocked`
- `scoreSpans`: none
- `routeScore`: none
- `heatmapInputSpans`: none
- `scoringComplete`: `false`
- missing fields are listed explicitly

## Why Scoring Is Blocked

Highway/road-class tags are not enough to run the existing scoring model safely. The current scoring model needs speed/traffic exposure, shoulder or shoulder fallback, bike-support information, and lane count or an accepted lane fallback policy.

This phase intentionally does not infer:

- speed from highway class
- traffic from road class
- shoulder from road geometry
- bike support from road name or family key
- lane count from highway class

## Next Field Group

13BP should attach the first real score-driving field family from provider/source records or documented fallback policy.

Recommended order:

1. Attach `maxspeed` / speed-limit from owned source tags if present.
2. Attach `cycleway`, `cycleway:left`, `cycleway:right`, or `bicycle` tags as bike-infra evidence if present.
3. Attach `lanes` as lane-count evidence if present.
4. If Test Loop lacks all of those tags, use a richer real route fixture or regenerate the source artifact with the required tags. Do not fabricate values.

Traffic/AADT and shoulder likely require later external or provider-enriched evidence layers.

## Recommendation For 13BP

Proceed with:

`13BP - Attach first score-driving provider/source field family`

The phase should still be diagnostic-only. It should prove one required score-driving field can be attached to V2S+S route-distance ownership spans without V1 truth-run or sample-index internals.

Scoring and heatmap should remain deferred until the readiness gate reports all minimum score-driving field groups are satisfied by real evidence or explicitly approved fallback policy.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13BP: V2S+S Evidence Cache/Profile Strategy

## 1. Executive Decision

Direct answer:

B. `profile_model_directionally_right_but_needs_route_evidence_profiles_and_owned_source_language`

DS-034 and DS-035 are directionally right: the base Cyclist Mobility Substrate should stay compact, structural, noncanonical, and separate from exact/profile hydration and raw source evidence. The correction is that DS-035 is still too `viewport_speed`-centered and does not yet name the V2S+S route evidence profiles or owned-source hydration modes clearly enough.

Do not expand the base substrate just because speed was the first heatmap profile. Speed should be nationally prehydrated as the compact `viewport_speed` profile, not baked into base substrate. Speed, traffic, bike infrastructure, shoulder, and surface are all candidate viewport profiles. Any one of them may become the default auto-loaded profile later.

Production source authority should be named as owned-source first:

- `owned_canonical_source_hydration`
- `owned_route_evidence_profile_hydration`
- `owned_viewport_profile_hydration`

External hydration is fallback-only when the owned Nuremberg source is missing, stale, or unavailable.

## 2. Cache/Source Ownership Layers

| Layer | Owns | Does not own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base substrate descriptor | Corridor identity, salience, continuity, zoom eligibility, constituent refs, source/version metadata, core highway/domain where already structural | Score-driving truth, viewport default policy, raw source authority, route ownership truth |
| Viewport profile hydration | Fast full-map overlays by profile: speed, traffic, bike infra, shoulder, surface | Route truth, scoring rollups, raw inspection authority |
| Route evidence profile hydration | Batched evidence for accepted V2S+S ownership spans/source ways | Broad route-wide candidate search, display-only heat tile truth |
| Raw owned source hydration | OSM/HPMS/DOT/AADT source-of-record, provenance, conflict resolution, legal/source inspection | Hot display payload minimization |
| Model inference policy | Explicit documented fallbacks or inference with confidence loss | Silent fabrication |
| Derived scoring output | Score spans, route rollups, heatmap input spans, explanation payloads | Source evidence |

## 3. Field Ownership Matrix

| Field | Intended owner | Default map overlay eligible | Route scoring eligible | Prehydrate nationally | Lazy hydrate | Batch with other fields | Source-of-record required before scoring | Payload risk | Freshness sensitivity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `highway` / `road_class` | `base_substrate_descriptor`, `route_evidence_profile_hydration`, `owned_canonical_source_hydration` | Yes | Yes | Yes, structurally | Yes | Yes | Yes | Low | Low | Core structural field. Can live in substrate because it helps graph/domain classification, but raw source remains authority. |
| `maxspeed` / `speed_limit` | `viewport_profile_hydration`, `route_evidence_profile_hydration`, `owned_canonical_source_hydration`, `model_inference_policy`, `external_fallback_only` | Yes | Yes | Yes - nationally prehydrated as `viewport_speed` common profile, not base substrate | Yes | Yes | Yes | Low to medium | Medium | Do not make speed permanent base substrate. Use compact `viewport_speed` nationally and route evidence scoring profiles. Inference requires explicit fallback/confidence policy. External fallback only when owned source is unavailable/stale/missing. |
| `speed_class` / inferred speed environment | `model_inference_policy`, `viewport_profile_hydration`, `route_evidence_profile_hydration` | Yes | Yes, only when policy-approved | Regionally | Yes | Yes | Yes, if source value absent | Low | Low | Derived from highway/context only under an explicit fallback policy with confidence loss. |
| `traffic_aadt` | `owned_canonical_source_hydration`, `viewport_profile_hydration`, `route_evidence_profile_hydration` | Yes | Yes | Regionally where owned data is available | Yes | Yes | Yes | Medium | High | Treat traffic as a common overlay candidate. Owned HPMS/DOT/AADT is normal production source, not normal external hydration. |
| `shoulder` | `owned_canonical_source_hydration`, `viewport_profile_hydration`, `route_evidence_profile_hydration`, `model_inference_policy` | Yes | Yes | Regionally | Yes | Yes | Yes | Medium | Medium | Often sparse. Fallback policy must be explicit; no silent no-shoulder assumption. |
| `bike_infra` / `cycleway` / `bicycle` | `viewport_profile_hydration`, `route_evidence_profile_hydration`, `owned_canonical_source_hydration` | Yes | Yes | Regionally | Yes | Yes | Yes | Medium | Medium | Good viewport profile candidate. OSM tags can attach first; DOT/local facility data can enrich later. |
| `lane_count` / `lanes` | `owned_canonical_source_hydration`, `route_evidence_profile_hydration`, `viewport_profile_hydration` | Yes | Yes | Regionally | Yes | Yes | Yes | Medium | Medium | Important for traffic exposure and crossing context. Do not infer silently from class. |
| `surface` | `viewport_profile_hydration`, `route_evidence_profile_hydration`, `owned_canonical_source_hydration` | Yes | Yes, where model uses it | Regionally | Yes | Yes | Yes if score-driving for hazard/surface rules | Low to medium | Low | Useful for route inspection and hazard rules. Sparse OSM tags should remain explicit. |
| Hazard flags | `route_evidence_profile_hydration`, `viewport_profile_hydration`, `owned_canonical_source_hydration`, `model_inference_policy` | Yes | Yes | No, except curated regional hazard sets | Yes | Yes | Yes | Medium to high | High | Some are source facts, some are derived events. Keep source and derived event lineage separate. |
| `time_of_day_traffic_multiplier` | `model_inference_policy`, `derived_scoring_output` | No as default; optional contextual overlay | Contextual only | No | Yes | Yes | No raw source; policy/version required | Low | High | Ride-time/contextual. Not stable route identity evidence. |
| Heatmap risk fields | `derived_scoring_output` | Yes | Output, not input | No | Yes | Yes | No, because they are derived | Medium | Depends on inputs | `rawRisk`, `normalizedRisk`, risk buckets, and heat tile colors must never feed RouteLine truth or source evidence. |

## 4. Full-Map Heatmap Strategy

Full-map exploration should load substrate first, then a configurable viewport profile.

Candidate viewport profiles:

- `viewport_speed`
- `viewport_traffic_v1`
- `viewport_bike_infra_v1`
- `viewport_shoulder_v1`
- `viewport_surface_v1`

The default auto-loaded profile should be configuration, not doctrine. Speed may be the initial default viewport overlay because it is the best single-field approximation of road risk and its compact payload is small. Traffic is also a strong default candidate because HPMS/DOT/AADT is owned on the Nuremberg source side, but traffic has higher freshness/provenance complexity than speed.

Recommended compact `viewport_speed` payload:

- `substrateSpanId` or source way ref
- `speedMph` or `speedKph` when known
- `speedBucket` / `speedClass`
- `speedSource`: `posted`, `official_imported`, `osm_tag`, `inferred`, or `unknown`
- `confidence`
- `sourceVersion`
- `schemaVersion`

Do not store full raw source tags in `viewport_speed`. Exact raw/owned source evidence remains required for scoring provenance, legal/source inspection, conflict resolution, and high-confidence scoring.

Heat tile/display payloads are adapters. They may carry span ids, constituent refs, and profile values for rendering, but they must not feed RouteLine topology or route truth.

## 5. Route Scoring/Evidence Strategy

V2S+S route scoring should hydrate evidence after identity is stable:

```text
route axis
  -> V2S+S identity ownership spans
  -> accepted source way ids / source-way contributions
  -> batched owned_route_evidence_profile_hydration
  -> route-indexed evidence bundle
  -> scoring worker
```

Recommended route profiles:

- `route_evidence_core_v1`: highway/domain/source lineage/node refs and basic source tags.
- `route_evidence_scoring_v1`: score-driving fields needed by the scoring worker.
- `route_traffic_v1`: AADT/traffic fields when split profile size/freshness makes that useful.
- `route_hazard_events_v1`: point/span events, crossings, bridges, underpasses, cattle grids, and hazard flags.

Route distance remains the V2S+S join key. Accepted OSM way ids and source refs are metadata and hydration keys, not the final route join surface.

## 6. Traffic Overlay Strategy

Traffic/AADT should be treated as owned canonical evidence in production:

- normal path: `owned_canonical_source_hydration`
- route path: `owned_route_evidence_profile_hydration`
- viewport path: `owned_viewport_profile_hydration`
- external path: `external_fallback_only`

This is a correction to any language that implies HPMS/DOT/AADT is primarily an external runtime fetch. It may have started that way historically, but the production model should use the owned Nuremberg source export/cache as authority.

Traffic can be both:

- a common full-map overlay, and
- a score-driving route evidence field.

Those are different payload contracts even if they share the same owned source.

## 7. Batching/Round-Trip Strategy

Route evidence hydration should batch by accepted route evidence, not by broad corridor universe:

- accepted OSM way ids
- constituent source refs
- source member ids
- route-distance ownership windows
- route-local topology handoff windows

One request should be able to return a compact evidence bundle for the accepted route spans. It should not require materializing broad `merged.roads`.

Viewport profile hydration should batch by tile/subtile/window/profile and respect z-band/stage ordering.

## 8. National Hydration Strategy

National substrate cache:

- precompute structural cyclist mobility substrate nationally
- keep payload compact
- preserve constituent refs and source/version metadata
- do not embed every score-driving field in the base substrate

National/owned source profile caches:

- prehydrate high-value regional/national fields where payload and freshness are acceptable
- nationally prehydrate compact `viewport_speed`
- regionally prehydrate traffic/AADT where owned data coverage is strong
- lazily hydrate sparse/volatile fields by viewport or route evidence request
- keep source version and profile schema version explicit

Suggested prehydration posture:

- `highway` / `road_class`: national structural/base plus route evidence.
- `maxspeed`: national `viewport_speed` compact profile where owned source/tags are available; lazy route evidence fill and explicit missing elsewhere.
- `traffic_aadt`: regional where owned HPMS/DOT coverage is available; lazy by route/viewport elsewhere.
- `bike_infra`: regional/national where OSM tags are cheap; enrich later with local sources.
- `shoulder`: regional where owned DOT fields exist; lazy and explicit missing otherwise.
- `surface`: regional/national if payload is cheap; otherwise lazy.

## 9. Payload/Freshness Risk Notes

Low payload / low freshness sensitivity:

- highway/road_class
- substrate salience/continuity
- source refs

Medium payload or medium freshness sensitivity:

- maxspeed
- bike infrastructure
- lane count
- shoulder
- surface

High freshness or high conflict sensitivity:

- traffic/AADT where source year varies
- hazard events
- time-of-day multipliers
- derived score/risk outputs

Missing values must stay explicit. Profile hydration can say "missing", "stale", "fallback needed", or "fallback not applied"; it must not fabricate scoring inputs.

## 10. Blunt Current-State Assessment

The current implementation state from 13BN/13BO is correct but incomplete:

- Test Loop V2S+S has route identity and pre-scoring display parity.
- The evidence worker can attach `road_class` and `highway`.
- The scoring readiness gate correctly blocks scoring.
- `surface`, `speed_limit`, `bike_infra`, `lane_count`, `traffic_aadt`, and `shoulder` are not yet attached.

The docs/code direction is not "make substrate bigger." The right direction is:

1. keep base substrate structural,
2. expose profile-specific owned-source hydration for viewport and route evidence,
3. hydrate score-driving fields against accepted V2S+S ownership spans,
4. only then call scoring.

## 11. Recommended Next Implementation Phase

Recommended 13BQ:

`Define route_evidence_scoring_v1 descriptor and batched hydration request contract`

Minimum contract:

- route fingerprint
- accepted ownership spans
- accepted OSM way ids
- source way contributions
- requested evidence profile key
- source/version policy
- owned-source required by default
- external fallback allowed only with explicit reason
- route-distance evidence output
- missing/stale/fallback diagnostics

Alternative 13BQ if the next phase should stay closer to fixtures:

`Preserve/provider-map score-driving source tags`

That phase would audit whether the Test Loop source artifact strips `maxspeed`, `surface`, `cycleway`, `bicycle`, or `lanes`, then preserve those tags if present. It should still not fabricate missing values or call scoring.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13BQ: Profile Cache Authority And Freshness Contract

## 1. Direct Answer

A. `yes_profile_authority_contract_ready`

Profile cache entries can carry enough version, freshness, and authority metadata to support fast first paint while preventing stale, conflicted, or superseded data from driving scoring.

This phase defines a pure authority/freshness contract only. It does not implement scoring, heatmap cutover, cache writes, route cache coupling, production UI changes, or V2S+S selection.

## 2. Authority State Definitions

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `fresh_authoritative` | Descriptor matches expected schema/profile/source/model versions, is inside freshness windows, and has adequate owned-source authority. |
| `fresh_display_only` | Descriptor can render but cannot drive route evidence/scoring, usually due to low confidence, inferred-only authority, or external fallback. |
| `stale_usable` | Descriptor passed `staleAfter` but not `authoritativeUntil`; viewport display may continue while refresh runs. |
| `stale_blocking` | Descriptor is too stale, version-stale, or model-stale for scoring. |
| `missing` | No descriptor is available. |
| `conflicted` | Descriptor conflicts with raw owned source; raw source wins. |
| `superseded_by_source` | Source version or source timestamp indicates the descriptor is older than current owned source. |
| `unavailable` | Required metadata or source hydration is unavailable for the requested use. |

## 3. Use Permission Matrix

| Authority state | mayRenderViewport | mayDriveRouteEvidence | mayDriveScoring | mustRefreshInBackground | mustBlockScoring | mustHydrateOwnedSource |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fresh_authoritative` | yes | yes | yes | no | no | no |
| `fresh_display_only` | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |
| `stale_usable` | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |
| `stale_blocking` | no | no | no | no | yes | yes |
| `missing` | no | no | no | no | yes | yes |
| `conflicted` | no | no | no | no | yes | yes |
| `superseded_by_source` | no | no | no | no | yes | yes |
| `unavailable` | no | no | no | no | yes | yes |

## 4. Required Descriptor Metadata

Every profile descriptor should carry, where available:

- `profileKey`
- `schemaVersion`
- `profileVersion`
- `sourceVersion`
- `sourceSnapshotId`
- `modelVersion` if derived/inferred
- `generatedAt`
- `staleAfter`
- `authoritativeUntil`
- `freshnessSensitivity`
- `provenanceSummary`
- `confidence`
- `sourceAuthority`
- `fallbackAllowed`
- `rawSourceHydrationAvailable`

`sourceAuthority` values:

- `owned_canonical_source`
- `owned_profile_descriptor`
- `inferred_model`
- `external_fallback_only`

## 5. `viewport_speed` Examples

Fresh `viewport_speed`:

- can render viewport immediately
- can be treated as authoritative for display
- may drive scoring only when source/profile/model versions match and raw owned source hydration remains available

Stale-but-usable `viewport_speed`:

- can render first paint
- must schedule background refresh
- cannot drive scoring

Stale-blocking or source-superseded `viewport_speed`:

- cannot drive scoring
- must hydrate owned source before scoring

Speed remains a national compact viewport profile, not base substrate truth.

## 6. `route_evidence_scoring_v1` Examples

`route_evidence_scoring_v1` uses stricter permissions than viewport profiles.

If it is stale past `staleAfter`, it is `stale_blocking`, not `stale_usable`, because it feeds route evidence and future scoring.

For route scoring, the descriptor must:

- match schema/profile/source versions
- match model version when derived fields are present
- be generated after the source snapshot it summarizes
- have raw owned source hydration available or explicitly approved fallback policy
- avoid external fallback as normal production authority

## 7. Conflict Behavior

Raw owned source wins over cached profile descriptors.

If a descriptor conflicts with raw owned source, the authority state is `conflicted`, scoring is blocked, and owned source hydration is required.

If source version mismatches or source generated time is newer than the descriptor generated time, the authority state is `superseded_by_source`.

## 8. Background Refresh Behavior

`stale_usable` exists for viewport first paint. It allows fast rendering while a refresh runs in the background.

It does not permit scoring. Scoring requires `fresh_authoritative` route evidence or direct owned source hydration.

Reason codes include:

- `stale_after_elapsed`
- `display_allowed_scoring_blocked`
- `raw_source_available`
- `raw_source_unavailable`
- `conflict_requires_owned_source_hydration`
- `external_fallback_only_not_production_authority`

## 9. Why This Prevents National Recalc On Every Model Bug

Version metadata separates descriptor freshness dimensions:

- `schemaVersion` covers payload shape
- `profileVersion` covers profile semantics
- `sourceVersion` covers source imports and source interpretation
- `modelVersion` covers derived/inferred profile values

If a model bug affects only inferred values, model-derived descriptors can be invalidated without rebuilding the base substrate. If a source import changes, source-versioned descriptors can be refreshed without treating the entire national substrate as invalid. If a viewport profile changes shape, its profile/schema versions can roll independently from route evidence profiles.

This keeps base substrate structural and compact while allowing profile-specific refresh.

## 10. Recommended Next Phase

Recommended 13BR:

`define route_evidence_scoring_v1 batched hydration request/response contract`

That phase should connect accepted V2S+S ownership spans/source-way IDs to the route evidence profile request shape while preserving missing-field semantics and owned-source authority boundaries.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13BQ: Route Evidence Scoring Profile Contract

## 1. Direct Answer

A. `yes_route_evidence_scoring_profile_contract_ready`

V2S+S can build a batched `route_evidence_scoring_v1` request for the Test Loop accepted ownership spans/source ways without using V1 truth-run or sample-index internals.

This phase defines the contract and a deterministic diagnostic mock response only. It does not query the owned source server, call scoring, emit heatmap risk, select V2S+S output, or mark substrate as truth.

## 2. Request Contract

`V2SSRouteEvidenceProfileRequest`:

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `profileKey` | `route_evidence_scoring_v1` |
| `schemaVersion` | Payload shape version |
| `sourceVersion` | Owned source/profile version |
| `routeFingerprint` | Route identity key |
| `routeDistanceM` | Route-distance join surface length |
| `ownershipSpans` | V2S+S accepted route ownership spans |
| `sourceWayContributions` | Per-source-way contribution diagnostics |
| `acceptedSourceWayIds` | Accepted source way IDs used as hydration references |
| `requestedLayers` | Requested score-driving/context layers |
| `hydrationMode` | Normally `owned_route_evidence_profile_hydration` |
| `debugOnly` | `true` in this phase |
| `externalFallbackAllowed` | `false` by default |
| `usesV1TruthRunSampleIndex` | `false` |
| `usesBaseSubstrateAsScoreTruth` | `false` |
| `routeCacheUsed` | `false` |
| `substrateAcceptedAsTruth` | `false` |

Requested layers:

- `speed_limit`
- `traffic_aadt`
- `shoulder`
- `bike_infra`
- `lane_count`
- `surface`
- `hazard_events`
- `time_of_day_traffic_multiplier`

## 3. Response Contract

`V2SSRouteEvidenceProfileResponse` contains:

- `attachedLayers`
- `missingLayers`
- `unavailableLayers`
- `deferredLayers`
- `coverageSummary`
- `provenanceSummary`
- `confidenceSummary`
- `sourceRecordCount`
- `elapsedMs`
- `warnings`
- `scoringStillBlocked: true`
- `heatmapStillDeferred: true`
- `providerOutputSelected: false`
- `substrateAcceptedAsTruth: false`

Layer records use a DS-031 route-indexed shape:

- `layerId`
- `geometryType`: `span`, `point`, or `series`
- `startDistM` / `endDistM` or `distM`
- `value`
- `sourceLineage`
- `sourceOwnership`
- `provenance`
- `confidence`
- `diagnostics`

Source ownership enum:

- `owned_provider_tags`
- `owned_canonical_osm`
- `owned_hpms_dot_aadt`
- `owned_dot_attributes`
- `model_inference_policy`
- `derived_route_context`
- `external_fallback_only`
- `missing`

## 4. Test Loop Request Example

Fixture:

`public/demo/fixture-test-loop-1-ccw-short.gpx`

Accepted source ways:

- `11613459`
- `971362311`
- `1388406931`
- `1388406932`

Ownership spans:

- Oakwood Drive
- Tuckerton Road

The request uses ownership span route distances and accepted source way IDs. Rejected nearby source ways remain in contribution diagnostics, but they are not used as accepted hydration targets.

## 5. Diagnostic Mock Response Example

The deterministic mock response proves these semantics:

Attached:

- `road_class` from provider tags
- `highway` from provider tags

Missing:

- `speed_limit`
- `shoulder`
- `bike_infra`
- `lane_count`
- `surface`

Unavailable:

- `traffic_aadt`, with `owned_source_profile_required`

Deferred:

- `hazard_events`
- `time_of_day_traffic_multiplier`

No speed, AADT, shoulder, bike-infra, lane-count, or surface values are fabricated.

## 6. Missing/Deferred Semantics

`missing` means the diagnostic fixture/provider tags do not currently carry that value.

`unavailable` means the contract knows the layer should come from owned source/profile hydration, but this phase does not wire the owned provider.

`deferred` means the layer belongs to a later route-context or hazard/event stage.

`external_fallback_only` is not used by default. It is only valid when owned source is missing, stale, unavailable, or not yet imported.

## 7. Owned-Source Hydration Boundary

The production owner for route evidence is:

- `owned_route_evidence_profile_hydration`
- `owned_canonical_source_hydration`

Traffic/AADT is represented as owned-source required through `owned_hpms_dot_aadt`. It is not normal external hydration.

## 8. Why This Is Not `route_cache`

`route_cache` stores completed route analysis. `route_evidence_scoring_v1` is an evidence hydration profile request/response for an active route identity. It does not cache or select completed route analysis.

## 9. Why This Is Not Base Substrate

Base substrate remains structural and compact. It can provide acceleration, source refs, continuity, and salience. It does not become score truth.

## 10. Why This Is Not A Viewport Heatmap Profile

Viewport profiles such as `viewport_speed` serve map exploration without a route loaded. `route_evidence_scoring_v1` is keyed by accepted V2S+S route ownership spans and source-way contributions. It attaches route-indexed evidence by distance for scoring/inspection.

## 11. Recommended Next Phase

Recommended 13BR:

`wire Test Loop route_evidence_scoring_v1 to a local owned-source fixture provider`

The provider should remain diagnostic-only and should return real source-backed values only when present. If the Test Loop source artifact lacks `maxspeed`, `surface`, `cycleway`, `bicycle`, or `lanes`, the phase should report missing values rather than infer them.


- No shadow console log appeared.
- No app crash occurred.
- No persistence, lookup, or reload behavior occurred.

This failure occurred before the route was accepted into the normal route-load flow, so the shadow path correctly did not start.

## Diagnostic Payload Review

The captured flag-on GPX shadow diagnostic contained compact fields only:

- request id/event name,
- route source type,
- route point count,
- route distance,
- V2 status,
- candidate/ownership/blocker/handoff counts,

- relation validation status,
- validation error count/codes,
- timing through the emitted diagnostic object,
- explicit false boundaries for persistence, lookup, reload, `route_cache`, scoring, heatmap, default UI, route save/history, current revision pointer, member index writes, aggregate writes.

The captured diagnostic did not include:

- full graph,
- full substrate graph,
- full road arrays,
- full relation payload,
- `route_cache` payload,
- scoring payload,
- heatmap payload,
- Supabase payload,
- UI state.

## Red Flag Review

Red flags observed:

- normal route load failed because shadow failed: **no**
- heatmap/scoring changed when flag enabled: **no visible change observed**
- `route_cache` behavior changed: **no new behavior observed**
- Supabase writes to Route Relations occurred: **no Route Relation write behavior observed**
- full relation payload appeared in React state/logs: **no**
- full graph/substrate graph appeared in logs: **no**
- stale shadow result appeared after newer route: **not manually exercised**
- rider-facing UI changed unexpectedly: **no**
- substrate source appeared as accepted ownership truth: **no**

Commands run:


- `lanterne-route-relation-v1.test.ts` passed: 24 tests.
- `review-page-adapter.test.ts` passed: 6 tests.
- `substrate-candidate-hints.test.ts` passed: 11 tests.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Recommendation

Recommended next phase: **A. Phase 13F debug-only diagnostic drawer or admin panel for shadow results**.

Reason:

- Manual flag-off and flag-on GPX testing passed.
- The shadow diagnostic exists but is currently console/event based.
- A debug-only compact panel would make repeated manual tests, stale/cancel observations, and future RWGPS/manual comparisons easier without adding persistence, lookup, reload, `route_cache`, scoring, heatmap, default UI, route save/history, or V1 behavior changes.

Do not proceed directly to persistence, lookup, reload, or scoring/heatmap cutover from Phase 13E.

At the end of Phase 13E:

- no SQL was executed,

- full reconstruction remains fallback.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13K: V2 Baseline and Substrate Shadow Diagnostics

## Scope

Phase 13K stayed inside debug/test diagnostics only. No SQL was executed. No Supabase writes, persistence writes, relation lookup, reload, route_cache reads/writes, scoring cutover, heatmap cutover, route save/history behavior, default rider UI behavior, or production V1 behavior was added.

## V2 Baseline Audit

The Test drawer's V2 Baseline column was unavailable because the main-app drawer had no baseline diagnostic source. The existing V2 review page can load a GPX route and then run the V2 worker, but that review state was not wired into the main-app Test drawer and the drawer did not have its own baseline worker event.

The observed immediate purple route in non-shadow V2 is consistent with the existing review/ownership overlay path rendering route state before a completed baseline diagnostic is available. The code audit did not find a production route mutation or route_cache dependency. The main app comparison problem was missing baseline diagnostic plumbing, not a requirement to cut over to V2.

## Baseline Repair Status

Added a debug-only V2 Baseline Comparison path:

- Test drawer toggle: `Enable V2 Baseline Comparison`
- Baseline event: `lanterne-route-line-v2-main-app-baseline`
- Baseline runner uses the existing RouteLine V2 worker/review options.
- Baseline diagnostics are compact and diagnostic-only.
- Baseline failure, cancellation, timeout, or stale result does not affect production route load.

The baseline run is intentionally user-enabled because it launches an additional V2 worker. It is not started just to fill the table unless the debug/test toggle is enabled before loading a GPX/RWGPS route.

## Substrate Hint Wiring Status

The reason substrate hint count was `0` in the prior shadow output was that the main-app shadow runner did not pass a substrate candidate hint provider or serializable hint data to the worker. The topology builder already supports candidate hints, but worker options did not have a structured-clone-safe hint input.

Phase 13K added worker-safe optional hint arrays:

- `candidateWayHints`
- `candidateNodeHints`
- `continuityHints`
- `candidateHintOptions`

The shadow runner now accepts noncanonical substrate candidate hints when explicitly enabled, and only passes them when real hint rows are supplied. If the toggle is enabled but no debug-safe provider is available, diagnostics report `hintsRequested=true`, `providerAvailable=false`, and `unavailableReason=no_main_app_substrate_hint_provider`.

No substrate hints are invented. Substrate remains a candidate reducer only and cannot become accepted source-owned truth.

## Test Drawer Changes

Added Test drawer toggles:

- `Enable RouteLine V2 Main App Shadow`
- `Show Shadow Diagnostics Panel`
- `Enable V2 Baseline Comparison`
- `Enable Cyclist Substrate Hints for V2 Shadow`

Readiness state now includes:

- baseline comparison enabled
- last V2 baseline diagnostic available
- substrate hints requested
- substrate provider available

The three-way table remains:

- `V1 / Current Production`
- `V2 / Baseline`
- `V2 / Shadow`

## Metrics and Labels

The prior `V2 candidate way count` label was ambiguous. It now reads `V2 candidate evidence row count` because the worker field comes from compact evidence candidate telemetry and is not guaranteed to mean unique OSM ways.

Substrate-specific candidate rows now use unique-way wording only where the topology hint diagnostics actually report unique OSM way counts:

- `V2 pre-substrate unique candidate ways`
- `V2 post-substrate unique candidate ways`

The repeated baseline-unavailable note was reduced to a global panel note. Row notes now focus on the metric.

## Proven By Tests

Focused tests prove:

- V2 baseline unavailable renders as unavailable/n/a without treating it as zero.
- V2 baseline available renders real compact metrics.
- Baseline failure/cancellation/staleness is diagnostic-only.
- Baseline toggle is debug/test UI only and does not affect production analysis.
- Substrate disabled/provider-unavailable state is explicit.
- Serializable substrate hints are passed only when explicitly enabled and supplied.
- Substrate hints remain noncanonical.
- Candidate reduction metrics render when available.
- Candidate count labels are deterministic and less ambiguous.
- Forbidden payloads are not rendered.
- Boundary rows remain false/no-op.

## Manual Smoke

Manual browser smoke was not rerun in this phase. The change is ready for the next local manual pass in the Test drawer:

- enable `Enable V2 Baseline Comparison`
- enable `Enable RouteLine V2 Main App Shadow`
- optionally enable `Enable Cyclist Substrate Hints for V2 Shadow`
- load a simple GPX/RWGPS route
- confirm production analysis remains authoritative
- confirm baseline/shadow diagnostics populate only the Test drawer

## Remaining Unavailable Items

The main app still does not have a real cyclist substrate candidate hint provider wired to route-load context. Until such a provider exists, the substrate toggle correctly reports provider unavailable instead of faking hint counts.

V2 baseline metrics require the baseline toggle and a fresh route load. Existing completed shadow diagnostics are not backfilled.

## Boundary Statement

No SQL was executed. No production DB migration happened. No persistence writes, lookup, reload, route_cache behavior, scoring cutover, heatmap cutover, default UI behavior, route save/history behavior, or production V1 behavior was added. Cyclist substrate remains noncanonical candidate/hint metadata only. Route Relation candidates remain diagnostic-only. Full reconstruction remains fallback.

## Recommended Next Phase

Recommend Phase 13L: manual/local Test drawer pass with baseline and substrate toggles enabled, capturing the V1 / V2 Baseline / V2 Shadow output and verifying substrate provider availability remains honest.

# EXEC-030 Phase 13P: Short Urban Substrate Fixture Provider

## Scope

Phase 13P added a debug/test-only cyclist substrate fixture provider for V2 Shadow diagnostics. No SQL was executed. No Supabase writes, persistence writes, relation lookup, reload, route_cache mutation, scoring cutover, heatmap cutover, route save/history behavior, default rider UI behavior, or production V1 behavior was added.

## Fixture Chosen

Selected fixture:

```text
public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx
```

This is the shortest stable urban hazard/golden route currently available in the repo. It has 63 GPX track points and targets a Kansas City urban route with railroad crossings, bridge approaches, downtown grid segments, Independence Avenue, Paseo, Troost, and a 47th Street return. It is useful before DC or Cape May because it is small enough for fast local feedback while still having realistic urban candidate clutter.

## Provider Behavior

New debug fixture provider:

```text
src/lib/route-line-v2/substrate-golden-fixture-provider.ts
```

The provider:

- is deterministic
- matches only the short urban hazard fixture by label/file name plus endpoint geometry and point-count bounds
- returns worker-serializable noncanonical candidate way and continuity hints when matched
- returns provider-available / route-not-in-fixture-scope diagnostics for unrelated routes
- returns disabled diagnostics when the Test drawer substrate toggle is off
- does not fetch external data
- does not write data
- does not use Supabase
- does not touch route_cache

The fixture hints are candidate reducers only. They are not accepted ownership truth.

## V2 Shadow Wiring

The Test drawer now keeps the simplified primary lane selector:

- `V1`
- `V2`
- `V2 Shadow`

It also has a small secondary debug/test control:

- `Enable Cyclist Substrate Hints for V2 Shadow`

When that substrate control is enabled and V2 Shadow runs, the main app passes the fixture provider result into `startMainAppRouteRelationShadow`. V2 Baseline remains substrate-free. V1/current production remains unaffected and authoritative.

If the loaded route does not match the fixture, the drawer reports provider available plus `route_not_in_fixture_scope` and does not fake reduction.

## Diagnostics Surfaced

Compact substrate diagnostics now distinguish:

- fixture provider available
- fixture route matched
- fixture id/name
- hints requested
- hints returned
- pre-substrate unique candidate ways, when measured by the V2 worker
- post-substrate unique candidate ways, when measured by the V2 worker
- candidate reduction percent, when comparable counts exist
- accepted-as-candidate hint count
- rejected hint count
- fallback expansion count
- unavailable reason

The panel still does not display full substrate graphs, full hint arrays, full road arrays, full Route Relation payloads, route_cache payloads, scoring payloads, heatmap payloads, Supabase payloads, or UI state blobs.

## Candidate Count Clarity

The table keeps `V2 candidate evidence row count` separate from substrate unique-way counts. Candidate evidence rows are compact V2 worker telemetry and are not guaranteed to be unique OSM ways. The substrate pre/post rows use unique-way wording only for the topology candidate-hint diagnostics that report unique OSM way counts.

## Reduction Metrics

Candidate reduction is measured only when the V2 topology worker receives matching candidate hints and reports comparable pre/post unique candidate counts. Disabled substrate, provider unavailable, route not matched, zero hints, and not measured remain separate states.

The initial short urban fixture provider is intentionally local/debug scoped. Manual testing is still needed to confirm whether the current route evidence source contains the fixture hint IDs and whether actual candidate reduction occurs on this GPX route.

## Manual Smoke

Manual browser smoke was not run in this phase. The next manual pass should:

- open the Test drawer locally
- select `V1 + V2 Shadow`
- enable `Enable Cyclist Substrate Hints for V2 Shadow`
- load `public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx`
- confirm fixture route matched
- inspect hints returned and pre/post candidate counts
- confirm production analysis remains authoritative
- confirm no persistence, lookup, reload, route_cache, scoring, heatmap, default UI, or route save/history behavior changed

## Verification

Commands run:

```bash
npx vitest run src/lib/route-line-v2/substrate-golden-fixture-provider.test.ts
npx vitest run src/lib/route-relations/main-app-shadow-route-relation.test.ts
npx vitest run src/lib/route-relations/main-app-shadow-diagnostic-panel-model.test.ts
npx vitest run src/components/MainAppShadowTestDrawer.test.tsx src/components/MainAppShadowRouteRelationPanel.test.tsx
npx vitest run src/lib/route-line-v2/substrate-candidate-hints.test.ts
npx vitest run src/lib/route-relations/lanterne-route-relation-v1.test.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
git diff --check
```

All listed commands passed. Boundary grep over the changed shadow/test drawer modules found no Supabase, persistence, reload, route_cache, scoring, or heatmap imports.

## Next Fixtures

Recommended next fixture phases:

- Phase 13Q: DC golden route substrate fixture
- Phase 13R: Cape May golden route substrate fixture

Do not start with DC or Cape May until the short urban fixture proves the wiring and diagnostic path.

## Source File: docs/04-execution/exec-030-phase-13q-benchmark-lane-instrumentation-repair.md

# EXEC-030 Phase 13Q Benchmark Lane Instrumentation Repair

## Scope

Phase 13Q repaired debug/test instrumentation for the RouteLine V2 Test drawer benchmark lanes.

No SQL was executed. No Supabase writes, Route Relation persistence, lookup, reload, route_cache mutation, scoring cutover, heatmap cutover, default rider UI behavior, route save/history behavior, production telemetry pipeline, or production V1 cutover was added.

## Root Cause

The Test drawer kept production/V1 comparison metrics only in an internal ref used to merge into V2 shadow diagnostics. That meant:

- V1-only mode had no first-class lane result.
- V2-baseline-only mode could show baseline metrics while the V1 lane stayed awaiting.
- Production metrics were effectively coupled to the shadow request id, even though the drawer now supports independent lanes.

Phase 13Q promotes the production comparison event into drawer state and passes it to the comparison model independently from baseline and shadow diagnostics.

## Lane State Model

The drawer now treats lanes independently:

- V1 / Current Production can render from compact production metrics alone.
- V2 / Baseline can render from a standalone debug worker diagnostic.
- V2 / Shadow can render from the main-app sidecar diagnostic.

Lane states are distinct:

- disabled: lane not selected in the manual benchmark controls
- awaiting: lane selected but no matching compact result yet
- completed: compact lane result exists
- failed: compact failure diagnostic exists
- unavailable/not measured: metric was not exposed by that lane
- zero: real numeric zero, not the same as unavailable

Production metrics merge by compact route identity where available: source type, route point count, and route distance. Baseline and shadow updates no longer wipe out V1 metrics.

## Timing Scope Labels

The comparison table keeps timing scopes separate:

- V1 total route-load time is the existing production analysis total.
- V1 fetch, build/match, enrich, and display/render rows come from existing stage timings where available.
- V2 total diagnostic elapsed includes local diagnostic orchestration.
- V2 worker construction time is the cleaner apples-to-apples baseline versus shadow comparison.
- V2 diagnostic overhead is derived from elapsed time minus worker construction and measured relation serialization/validation.

The table notes explicitly avoid comparing V1 total route-load time to V2 worker-only timing as equivalent.

## Candidate Count Semantics

Labels were tightened:

- V2 candidate evidence row count is compact worker telemetry and is not guaranteed to be unique OSM ways.
- V2 named candidate evidence row count is also worker telemetry.
- Pre/post substrate unique candidate ways are labeled as unique only when they come from the candidate hint diagnostics' unique OSM way counts.
- Evidence rows are not compared to unique ways without a note.

If a metric's uniqueness cannot be proven, it remains labeled as candidate evidence rows.

## Substrate Hint Semantics

The substrate rows now use clearer names:

- Directly accepted hint candidates: hinted ways present in the reduced candidate universe. This is not accepted route truth.
- Hints rejected as direct candidates: hints that were not direct candidate acceptances or were not selected by RouteLine validation.
- RouteLine fallback/safeguard candidates added: route-aligned safeguards added after hint filtering.

Rejected direct hints can still coexist with a useful candidate-universe reduction because RouteLine may add fallback/safeguard candidates. Substrate remains noncanonical candidate metadata only and cannot satisfy missing OSM/source refs, validate a Route Relation, bypass RouteLine validation, write member indexes, write aggregates, or touch route_cache.

## Blocker And Span Summaries

The shadow/baseline diagnostics now expose compact relation summaries when available:

- blocker reason summary
- blocker distance windows
- way span count
- coordinate span count
- unmatched span count
- inferred span count

These are compact strings/counts only. They do not expose blocker coordinates, graph objects, ordered members, matched span payloads, road arrays, substrate graphs, or relation payloads.

## Manual Smoke

Manual browser smoke was not rerun in Phase 13Q. The next phase should manually verify:

- V1-only shows V1 metrics after a GPX/RWGPS load.
- V1 + V2 baseline shows both lanes.
- V1 + V2 shadow shows both lanes.
- All lanes selected show all matching compact results.
- Short urban substrate fixture rows use the clarified direct-hint/fallback semantics.

## Remaining Limitations

- V1 is still required for the current app route-load state.
- Cache suppression is not implemented.
- Benchmark lanes are manual/debug-only and not a production telemetry pipeline.
- DC and Cape May substrate fixtures should wait until the short urban benchmark labels are manually trusted.

## Recommendation

Proceed to Phase 13R: manual retest of repaired lane instrumentation before adding DC or Cape May fixtures.

## Boundary Statement

Production DB migration remains deferred. No SQL was executed. No persistence writes, relation lookup, reload, route_cache mutation, scoring/heatmap/default UI behavior change, route save/history behavior change, or production V1 behavior change was added. Substrate remains noncanonical. Route Relation candidates remain diagnostic-only. Full reconstruction remains fallback.
