## Source File: docs/04-execution/exec-030-phase-13s-short-urban-substrate-performance-attribution.md

# EXEC-030 Phase 13S Short Urban Substrate Performance Attribution

## Scope

Phase 13S added debug/test attribution for the short urban substrate fixture only.

No SQL was executed. No Supabase writes, Route Relation persistence, lookup, reload, route_cache mutation, scoring cutover, heatmap cutover, default rider UI behavior, route save/history behavior, production telemetry pipeline, production V1 cutover, or substrate-as-truth behavior was added.

## Question

The short urban substrate fixture proves a large candidate-universe reduction, but the latest manual run did not show a matching V2 worker construction-time improvement.

The phase investigated whether the reduction is being applied early enough to avoid expensive work, and whether the displayed counts are measuring the same units.

## V2 Construction Phase Timing

The Test drawer now surfaces both end-to-end V2 lane timing and compact RouteLine V2 topology phase timings when the worker exposes them:

- V2 end-to-end route-load elapsed: starts at the main app route-load handler and ends when the selected V2 diagnostic lane completes.
- V2 route artifact prep before worker: time from route-load start until the V2 worker lane is queued.
- V2 total diagnostic elapsed time: time from V2 worker lane start to diagnostic completion.
- V2 worker construction time: worker pipeline elapsed time reported by the RouteLine V2 evidence pipeline.

- topology edge/index build time
- candidate generation time, if separately measured
- topology path solve time
- continuity analysis time
- handoff extraction time
- blocker extraction/reporting time
- topology serialization/span build time

Current limitation: the topology worker exposes several core phase timings, but not every upstream evidence/candidate-preparation stage is separately timed yet. Candidate generation can still be `not measured` when it is grouped into edge/index build or upstream evidence preparation.

The V2 lane still does not mutate production output. The end-to-end V2 timing is a debug/test measurement of the selected V2 lane, not a production cutover.

## Substrate Application Stage

Substrate hints are applied inside `buildRouteLineV2TopologyPathWithCandidateHints`.

The current placement is:

- after route-window evidence candidates already exist
- after the hint provider is called
- after route-aligned safeguards are selected
- before the hinted topology edge build/path solve

The diagnostic rows now show:

- substrate application stage: `pre_topology_edge_build`
- filtering applied before path solve: `true`
- filtering applied before expensive candidate generation: `false`

This explains the current performance mismatch. The candidate universe can shrink before the hinted topology solve, but the code may already have paid full-universe costs for evidence preparation and route-aligned safeguard selection.

## Candidate Count Semantics

The table keeps these count units separate:

- V2 candidate evidence row count: compact worker telemetry, not guaranteed unique OSM ways.
- V2 named candidate evidence row count: compact worker telemetry for named evidence rows.
- V2 pre-substrate unique candidate ways: unique OSM way ids before hint filtering, when candidate hint diagnostics run.
- V2 post-substrate unique candidate ways: unique OSM way ids after hint filtering and safeguards, when candidate hint diagnostics run.

The short urban fixture's reported `9,783 -> 1,107` substrate reduction is a unique OSM way-id reduction from the candidate hint diagnostics, not a full worker evidence-row reduction.

## Hint Accepted/Rejected/Fallback Semantics

The substrate diagnostic labels were clarified:

- Directly accepted hint candidates: hint way ids present in the reduced candidate universe. This is not accepted route truth.
- Hints rejected as direct candidates: hint way ids not selected as direct RouteLine candidate ownership. They never become source-owned truth.
- RouteLine fallback/safeguard candidates added: route-aligned safeguards added around the hint-filtered universe.
- Substrate fallback to full baseline: whether the worker selected a full baseline topology result after the hinted run.
- Substrate selected result source: whether the displayed diagnostic came from the hinted candidate universe or full-baseline fallback.
- Substrate compare-to-baseline run: whether a full baseline topology run was performed for equivalence diagnostics.

Rejected direct hints can still be useful as diagnostic candidate reducers. They do not validate a Route Relation, satisfy missing OSM/source refs, bypass RouteLine validation, or become accepted ownership truth.

## Runtime Attribution

The likely reason reduction is not yet a runtime win is that the current debug mode still pays for one or more full-universe paths:

- Evidence/candidate preparation occurs before substrate filtering.
- Route-aligned safeguard selection currently builds/scans topology candidates over the full road universe before reducing candidate roads.
- `compareToBaseline` can run a full baseline topology for equivalence diagnostics.
- `fallbackOnBlockers` can select a full baseline topology if the hinted path has blockers or an empty candidate universe.

The new rows expose:

- substrate hint fetch time
- substrate filter time
- RouteLine safeguard expansion time
- hinted topology run time
- baseline compare/fallback topology run time
- fallback reason
- selected result source

Those rows should make the next manual run show whether the no-speedup case is due to safeguard expansion, baseline compare/fallback, upstream evidence preparation, or a real hinted-path solve cost.

The Test drawer now also makes the end-to-end V2 lane elapsed visible so worker-only timing can be separated from route artifact preparation and local diagnostic overhead.

## Blocker And Span Summary

The panel now carries compact span-quality context where available:

- blocker reason summary
- blocker distance windows
- relation average matched span length
- relation short matched span count
- way/coordinate/unmatched/inferred span counts

This is enough to flag whether `171` ownership spans and `2` blockers look like fragmentation without rendering geometry, graph payloads, road arrays, or relation payloads.

## Manual Smoke

Manual browser smoke was not rerun in Phase 13S. The next manual run should compare:

- V1 + V2 Shadow, substrate off
- V1 + V2 Shadow, substrate on

Capture the new rows for worker phase timing, substrate filter timing, safeguard expansion time, hinted topology time, baseline compare/fallback topology time, selected result source, blocker summary, relation validity, and pre/post unique candidate way counts.

## Verification

Passed:

- `npx vitest run src/lib/route-relations/main-app-shadow-diagnostic-panel-model.test.ts src/components/MainAppShadowRouteRelationPanel.test.tsx src/components/MainAppShadowTestDrawer.test.tsx src/lib/route-relations/main-app-shadow-route-relation.test.ts src/lib/route-line-v2/substrate-golden-fixture-provider.test.ts src/lib/route-line-v2/substrate-candidate-hints.test.ts src/lib/route-relations/lanterne-route-relation-v1.test.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `git diff --check`
- Boundary import grep over the touched Test drawer/shadow/substrate modules found no new Supabase, persistence, reload, route_cache, scoring, or heatmap imports.

## Remaining Optimization Hypotheses

Do not optimize until the new attribution rows are manually captured.

Likely next hypotheses:

- Move substrate filtering earlier, before expensive candidate/evidence generation.
- Optimize route-aligned safeguard expansion so it does not rebuild too much of the full candidate universe.
- Disable or isolate full-baseline compare/fallback in a debug timing mode to measure the hinted path alone.
- Inspect the two short-urban blockers and short-span count if the new span-quality rows show fragmentation.

## Recommendation

Proceed to Phase 13T: manual retest of short urban substrate performance attribution. If the new rows show full-baseline compare/fallback or safeguard expansion dominates, Phase 13T should repair that instrumentation or optimize that debug path before adding DC or Cape May fixtures.

## Boundary Statement

Production DB migration remains deferred. No SQL was executed. No persistence writes, relation lookup, reload, route_cache mutation, scoring/heatmap/default UI behavior change, route save/history behavior change, or production V1 behavior change was added. Substrate remains noncanonical. Route Relation candidates remain diagnostic-only. Full reconstruction remains fallback.

- `90013001` through `90013006`
- fixture display labels such as `Main Street railroad corridor`
- fixture family keys such as `fixture:kc-main-st`
- route-distance windows
- confidence/freshness metadata

Those IDs are not canonical RouteLine V2 candidate source identities. They are fixture/merged-run placeholders, not individual OSM way IDs from the worker candidate universe.

## Substrate Hint Identity Mode

The fixture provider now marks the short urban hints explicitly as:

- identity mode: `merged_substrate_run`
- merged substrate run metadata: present
- canonical constituent source refs: not present

Merged run metadata remains diagnostic only. It is not accepted as source truth and is not used as a direct RouteLine candidate identity.

## RouteLine Candidate Identity Mode

RouteLine V2 candidate evidence rows use canonical source identity fields such as:

- `osmWayId`
- optional `nodeIds`
- domain/source metadata
- display label/family key for diagnostics and grouping

Canonical matching should use source identities such as OSM way/node refs or future source-member refs. It must not use display labels, road names, fixture family keys, or merged substrate run IDs as direct candidate identity.

## Matching Repair

The debug substrate matching boundary now distinguishes:

- canonical source refs present
- merged substrate run refs present
- direct candidate match count
- direct candidate unique way match count
- constituent way expansion count
- constituent node expansion count
- matching identity used
- direct hint rejection reason summary

The matching path now supports future merged hints that carry constituent OSM way refs. If a merged hint has `constituentOsmWayIds`, those refs are expanded for direct matching. If it does not, the hint is rejected with an explicit reason instead of being treated as a missing OSM way.

The new rejection reason for the current short urban fixture is:

- `merged_substrate_run_missing_constituent_source_refs`

This replaces the misleading generic interpretation that the synthetic `9001300x` IDs were real OSM ways missing from the candidate source.

## Direct Match Result

Current short urban fixture outcome: Outcome B.

- direct accepted hint candidates remain `0`
- direct candidate unique way match count remains `0`
- constituent way expansion count remains `0`
- canonical source refs present: `false`
- merged substrate run refs present: `true`
- rejection reason summary should become `merged_substrate_run_missing_constituent_source_refs:6`

This is the correct result until the fixture/provider is given real constituent source refs.

## Candidate Reduction Interpretation

The fixture can still reduce the candidate universe through route-aligned safeguards, but not through direct canonical hint matches.

That means:

- candidate reduction can still be real
- direct hint acceptance remains unavailable
- fallback/safeguard reliance is still expected
- `hinted_path_blockers` can still force full-baseline fallback

The fixture currently proves the debug plumbing and merged-run mismatch, not a clean per-way substrate speed path.

## Test Drawer Diagnostics

The Test drawer now has compact rows for:

- hint identity mode
- canonical source refs present
- merged substrate run refs present
- direct candidate match count
- direct candidate unique way match count
- constituent way expansion count
- constituent node expansion count
- matching identity used
- direct hint rejection reason summary

No full hint arrays, candidate arrays, road arrays, substrate graph, route geometry, or relation payloads are rendered.

## Boundary Review

Confirmed:

- substrate hints remain candidate reducers only
- substrate cannot become accepted `source_way` or `source_node` truth
- substrate cannot satisfy missing OSM/source refs
- substrate cannot make a Route Relation candidate valid
- substrate cannot bypass RouteLine validation
- substrate cannot update member indexes or aggregates
- substrate cannot touch `route_cache`
- Route Relation candidate remains diagnostic-only

## Manual Smoke

Manual smoke was not run in this phase.

The next manual short urban run should capture:

- direct accepted hint candidates
- rejected direct hints
- rejection reason summary
- constituent expansion count
- pre/post candidate counts
- selected result source
- fallback reason
- relation validity
- worker construction time

Expected current result is not direct matching success. Expected result is clearer proof that the fixture lacks constituent source refs.

## Verification

Commands run:

- `npx vitest run src/lib/route-line-v2/substrate-candidate-hints.test.ts` - passed
- `npx vitest run src/lib/route-line-v2/substrate-golden-fixture-provider.test.ts` - passed

# EXEC-030 Phase 13X: Hinted-Path Blocker Equivalence Audit

## Purpose

Phase 13X inspected the short urban substrate fixture fallback behavior after Phase 13V repaired substrate hints with canonical constituent source refs and Phase 13W manually verified direct matching.

The question for this phase was narrow:

- can the substrate-hinted RouteLine V2 result be considered structurally equivalent to the full-baseline fallback result when both have the same blockers?
- if yes, what future debug/test policy would allow selecting the hinted result?

This phase is diagnostic-only. It does not change selected result behavior.

## Current Fallback Policy

The current RouteLine V2 candidate-hint fallback rule is conservative:

- build the hinted topology result from the reduced candidate universe,
- optionally build a full-baseline topology result for comparison,
- if `fallbackOnBlockers` is enabled and the hinted result has any blockers, select the full-baseline fallback result,
- otherwise select the hinted candidate-universe result.

The current rule does not yet consider:

- blocker equivalence between hinted and full-baseline runs,
- ownership span count equivalence,
- handoff count equivalence,
- relation validation status,
- candidate reduction percentage,
- whether blockers are shared with the full baseline.

This explains why Phase 13W still selected `full_baseline_fallback` with reason `hinted_path_blockers` even though the hinted and full-baseline blocker counts matched.

## Diagnostics Added

Phase 13X added compact diagnostics only:

- `blockerEquivalenceStatus`
- `structuralEquivalenceStatus`
- `futureSelectableHintedResult`
- `hintedOwnershipSpanCount`
- `fullBaselineOwnershipSpanCount`
- `hintedHandoffCount`
- `fullBaselineHandoffCount`

The Test drawer now surfaces these rows in the Substrate section. The selected result source remains unchanged.

## Blocker Equivalence

Blocker equivalence is classified by:

- reason code,
- start distance,
- end distance,
- a small distance-window tolerance,
- count.

Statuses:

- `equivalent`
- `different_count`
- `different_reason`
- `different_window`
- `unknown`

Phase 13W manual data for `public/demo/fixture-urban-hazard.gpx` showed:

- hinted blockers: 2
- full-baseline blockers: 2
- shared blockers: 2
- hinted-only blockers: 0
- baseline-only blockers: 0

That result is consistent with `blockerEquivalenceStatus = equivalent`.

## Structural Equivalence

Structural equivalence is currently compact and conservative. It checks:

- blocker equivalence,
- ownership span count,
- handoff count,
- blocker count.

Statuses:

- `hinted_equivalent_to_baseline`
- `hinted_equivalent_with_shared_blockers`
- `hinted_not_equivalent`
- `equivalence_unknown`

For the Phase 13W short urban result, the expected classification is:

- `hinted_equivalent_with_shared_blockers`

This means the hinted result appears equivalent to the baseline at the compact diagnostic level, but the shared blockers still exist.

## Future Selection Policy Candidate

A future debug/test-only policy could select `hinted_equivalent_with_shared_blockers` instead of falling back to full baseline, but only if all of the following are true:

- blockers are equivalent by reason and route-distance window,
- ownership span count is equivalent,
- handoff count is equivalent,
- relation validation remains valid,
- validation error count remains zero,
- no hinted-only blockers exist,
- no baseline-only blockers exist,
- substrate remains candidate-reduction metadata only,
- full-baseline fallback remains available for comparison.

This future policy should first be debug/test-only. It should not be production fallback behavior.

## Manual Smoke

No new manual browser smoke test was run in Phase 13X. Phase 13X used the Phase 13W manual output as the known short urban observation and added unit-covered compact diagnostics for the next manual retest.

## Remaining Questions

- Whether the short urban route's two shared blockers are expected diagnostic blockers or real topology gaps.
- Whether `hinted_equivalent_with_shared_blockers` should be selectable in debug/test mode while still recording the shared blocker set.
- Whether additional compact span coverage checks are needed before allowing hinted selection.

## Recommended Next Phase

Recommended next:

**Phase 13Y: debug-only select hinted result when blockers and structure are equivalent.**

The selection should remain debug/test-only, retain full-baseline fallback comparison, and keep substrate noncanonical.

## Boundary Statement

- No SQL was executed.
- No persistence writes were added.
- No lookup or reload path was added.
- No route_cache mutation was added.
- No scoring, heatmap, or default UI behavior changed.
- Substrate remains noncanonical.
- Route Relation candidate remains diagnostic-only.
- Full reconstruction remains fallback.

- handoffs: 6 in both lanes
- selected result: `full_baseline_fallback`
- fallback reason: `hinted_path_blockers`

The goal was to explain the 169 vs 171 ownership span delta without changing selection behavior.

## Span Inputs

The compact span comparison uses `RouteOwnershipSpan` fields only:

- `domain`
- `reason`
- `sourceWayIds`
- `sourceNodeIds`
- `startDistM`
- `endDistM`
- span length
- blocker adjacency
- handoff adjacency

It does not use or render geometry, full relation members, road arrays, graph payloads, or route payloads.

## Diagnostics Added

Phase 13Z added diagnostic-only span delta fields:

- `sharedSpanCount`
- `baselineOnlySpanCount`
- `hintedOnlySpanCount`
- `spanDeltaStatus`
- `structuralEquivalenceReasonCodes`
- `equivalentRouteDistanceCoverage`
- `equivalentSourceCoverage`
- `deltaNearBlockerCount`
- `deltaShortSpanCount`
- `baselineOnlySpanSummary`
- `hintedOnlySpanSummary`

The summaries are capped and compact. Each summary contains source ids, span kind, route-distance window, span length, blocker adjacency, and handoff adjacency only.

## Span Delta Statuses

The comparison can classify:

- `equivalent_by_coverage`
- `equivalent_except_fragmentation`
- `baseline_has_missing_source_spans`
- `hinted_has_extra_source_spans`
- `different_source_identity`
- `different_route_distance_coverage`
- `near_blocker_delta`
- `unknown`

This is diagnostic-only and does not select the hinted result.

## Structural Reasons

Phase 13Z added reason codes so `hinted_not_equivalent` is no longer only a count mismatch:

- `ownership_span_count_diff`
- `ownership_span_fragmentation_only`
- `route_distance_coverage_diff`
- `source_identity_diff`
- `baseline_only_spans_present`
- `hinted_only_spans_present`
- `near_blocker_delta`
- `handoff_count_diff`
- `blocker_count_diff`
- `blocker_equivalence_diff`

The Test drawer now shows these reason codes in compact form.

## Current Finding

No new manual browser smoke test was run in Phase 13Z. Based on the Phase 13W manual dump, the known mismatch is:

- blockers are equivalent,
- handoffs are equivalent,
- ownership span count differs by 2.

Phase 13Z now provides the missing diagnostic rows needed to determine whether the 169 vs 171 delta is:

- harmless fragmentation,
- near the two shared blocker windows,
- missing meaningful full-baseline source spans,
- extra hinted source spans,
- different source identity coverage,
- or different route-distance coverage.

The code does not assume the delta is harmless. The next manual retest must read the new span-delta rows.

## Future Debug Selection Requirements

A future debug-only hinted-result selection policy should require:

- blockers equivalent by reason and route-distance window,
- handoffs equivalent,
- route-distance coverage equivalent,
- source identity coverage equivalent,
- no meaningful baseline-only source spans,
- no meaningful hinted-only source spans,
- relation validation valid,
- no hidden gaps,
- substrate remains noncanonical,
- full-baseline fallback remains available.

Phase 13Z does not implement that policy.

## Recommended Next Phase

Recommended next:

**Phase 13AA: manual retest of the short urban fixture span-delta diagnostics.**

If the new rows show harmless fragmentation or equivalent coverage, a later debug-only hinted selection phase can be considered. If they show meaningful baseline-only source spans, repair hinted span coverage first.

## Boundary Statement

- No SQL was executed.
- No persistence writes were added.
- No lookup or reload path was added.
- No route_cache mutation was added.
- No scoring, heatmap, or default UI behavior changed.
- Substrate remains noncanonical.
- Route Relation candidate remains diagnostic-only.
- Full reconstruction remains fallback.

# EXEC-030 Phase 14C - V2 Evidence Source Abstraction Contract

## Direct Answer

**A. yes_evidence_abstraction_contract_ready**

V2S+S `route_evidence_scoring_v1` can be backed by a normalized multi-source evidence abstraction without changing V1 behavior. The current V2S+S route evidence request already has the important stable inputs: route-distance ownership spans, accepted source-way IDs, and source-way contributions. The missing layer is not route identity shape; it is a normalized source/evidence/resolver contract between raw source facts and scoring-ready route evidence.

## Why This Abstraction Is Needed

The direct fixture provider is useful for Test Loop, but it is still too source-specific. Production evidence will come from owned OSM, HPMS, DOT/AADT, state bike infrastructure sources, city feeds, ArcGIS FeatureServer, Socrata, CKAN, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage, international datasets, and manual corrections.

The target data flow is:

`raw source data -> normalized evidence records -> resolved route evidence -> route_evidence_scoring_v1 -> scoring worker`

The key rule is: move facts, not assumptions. Raw source facts are stored separately. They do not overwrite each other. Resolution is an explicit policy step.

## Not Implemented Yet

- no production tables
- no schema migrations
- no durable source registry
- no production importers
- no scoring call
- no heatmap output
- no V1 migration
- no V2S+S output selection
- no route cache coupling

This phase defines contract shapes and proves the Test Loop fixture can adapt into them.

## Source Registry Shape

`EvidenceSourceRegistryEntry` records:

- `sourceId`
- `sourceName`
- `agency`
- `country`
- `stateOrRegion`
- `sourceType`
- `sourceUrl`
- `license` / `attribution`
- `authorityLevel`
- `refreshCadence`
- `enabled`
- `notes` / `caveats`

Supported source types:

- `osm`
- `hpms`
- `dot`
- `arcgis_feature_server`
- `socrata`
- `ckan`
- `geojson`
- `shapefile`
- `geopackage`
- `manual`
- `fixture`

## Source Version Shape

`EvidenceSourceVersion` records:

- `sourceVersionId`
- `sourceId`
- `fetchedAt`
- `sourceUpdatedAt`
- `checksum` / `contentHash`
- `recordCount`
- `importerVersion`
- `schemaVersion`
- `status`
- `error` / `caveats`

This keeps raw source freshness separate from route evidence resolution.

## Raw Feature References

`RawSourceFeatureRef` is a pointer, not a full raw feature copy:

- `sourceId`
- `sourceVersionId`
- `sourceFeatureId`
- `geometryRef`
- `rawPropertiesRef`
- `importedAt`
- `bbox`
- `tileKeys`

The normalized layer keeps enough lineage to inspect source facts later without stuffing every raw feature into the route evidence response.

## Normalized Evidence Record Shape

`NormalizedEvidenceRecord` represents source-owned facts:

- `evidenceId`
- `sourceId`
- `sourceVersionId`
- `sourceFeatureId`
- `evidenceType`
- `geometry`
- `value`
- `confidence`
- `authorityLevel`
- `semanticGranularity`
- `validFrom`
- `validTo`
- `provenance`
- `rawFeatureRef`
- optional route window overlap diagnostics
- stale/conflict/scoring eligibility flags

Evidence types currently modeled:

- `road_geometry`
- `road_class`
- `speed_limit`
- `traffic_aadt`
- `lane_count`
- `shoulder`
- `bike_infra`
- `surface`
- `access`
- `hazard`
- `crossing_control`

## Resolver Policy Shape

The simple diagnostic resolver takes:

- requested layer
- route span/window
- candidate normalized records
- source priority
- authority level
- freshness/conflict flags
- geometry/route overlap
- semantic granularity
- fallback allowance

It returns:

- selected evidence, if any
- rejected candidates with reasons
- unresolved/missing state when no candidate is acceptable

The implemented diagnostic policy is intentionally small:

- higher authority wins
- stale/conflicted records cannot drive scoring
- exact route/span overlap beats broad corridor context
- source priority breaks ties
- missing evidence remains missing
- no fabricated values

## Test Loop Fixture Adapter Result

The Test Loop adapter converts current owned fixture records into normalized evidence records.

Attached/source-backed facts:

- `road_class` / `highway`
- `surface=asphalt` for the Tuckerton source ways
- `lane_count=2` for the Tuckerton source ways
- `hazard` source fact from `bridge=yes` on `1388406932`

Still missing:

- `speed_limit`
- `traffic_aadt`
- `shoulder`
- `bike_infra`

The resolved route evidence remains route-distance keyed and keeps `substrateAcceptedAsTruth: false`.

## Future Source Support

This contract lets future adapters normalize heterogeneous sources into the same record shape:

- ArcGIS FeatureServer: normalize feature IDs, layer names, geometry refs, and attributes.
- Socrata: normalize row IDs, dataset version, and tabular evidence.
- CKAN: normalize package/resource IDs and imported files.
- GeoJSON/Shapefile/GeoPackage: normalize local feature IDs, geometry refs, and imported properties.
- HPMS/DOT/AADT: preserve official traffic records as candidates rather than overwriting OSM tags.
- Manual corrections: add high-authority source facts with explicit lineage and validity windows.

## V1 Boundary

V1 remains unchanged. The abstraction is pure RouteLine V2/V2S+S diagnostic code. It does not alter V1 source paths, scoring, heatmap, route cache, persistence, lookup/reload, RouteMap, or default UI behavior.

## Recommended Next Phase

14D should either:

1. Build the Test Loop `route_evidence_scoring_v1` response from normalized/resolved evidence in the diagnostic provider path, or
2. Add owned-source fixture records for the next missing score-driving field family, likely speed or traffic/AADT, if available.

Do not call scoring until the readiness gate has enough source-backed required fields.

# EXEC-030 Phase 14D - Route Evidence Profile From Resolved Evidence

## Direct Answer

A. `yes_route_evidence_profile_uses_resolved_evidence`

The Test Loop `route_evidence_scoring_v1` diagnostic provider can now build its response from normalized evidence records resolved through the 14C resolver policy. The direct fixture tag path remains available only as a comparison guard and is not used as the primary provider response.

## Resolved Provider Flow

1. Build the `route_evidence_scoring_v1` request from Test Loop V2S+S ownership spans and accepted source-way contributions.
2. Add core route evidence layers (`road_class`, `highway`) to the diagnostic request.
3. Adapt Test Loop owned fixture source records into `NormalizedEvidenceRecord` rows.
4. Resolve normalized candidates into `ResolvedRouteEvidence` using `v2ss_simple_authority_freshness_overlap_v1`.
5. Build `V2SSRouteEvidenceProfileResponse` from resolved route evidence.
6. Compare resolved output against the direct fixture provider semantically.
7. Fail closed if direct and resolved diagnostics disagree.

No V1 truth-run/sample-index joins are used. Route distance remains the join key.

## Test Loop Resolved Evidence Matrix

| Layer | Resolved status | Values | Notes |

## Source File: docs/04-execution/exec-030-phase-14f-speed-profile-descriptor-contract.md

# EXEC-030 Phase 14F - Speed Profile Descriptor Contract

## Direct Answer

A. `yes_speed_profile_descriptor_contract_ready`

One compact speed profile descriptor can support both `viewport_speed` full-map speed rendering and V2S+S route `speed_limit` evidence, without making speed part of base substrate truth.

The key boundary is authority and use permission:

- A descriptor may render a viewport when it is display-authoritative.
- A descriptor may become route evidence only when route-distance span context is supplied by V2S+S.
- A descriptor may drive scoring only when freshness, source version, provenance, and raw source references pass the stricter route-evidence authority gate.
- Base substrate remains structural and noncanonical.

## Why Speed Is National But Not Base Substrate

Speed is nationally prehydrated because it is compact and useful for first-paint full-map exploration. It is the best single-field approximation of road risk for many users.

Speed is not base substrate truth because:

- the default overlay must remain configurable;
- speed has source/provenance/freshness concerns;
- scoring needs authority checks and raw source traceability;
- raw owned source evidence remains the scoring/provenance authority.

## `ViewportSpeedProfileDescriptor`

The contract is implemented in:

`src/lib/route-line-v2/v2ss-speed-profile-descriptor.ts`

Core fields:

| Field group | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| profile identity | `profileKey: viewport_speed`, `schemaVersion`, `profileVersion`, `sourceVersion`, `sourceSnapshotId` |
| freshness | `generatedAt`, `staleAfter`, `authoritativeUntil` |
| map/source key | `substrateSpanId`, `sourceWayRef`, `geometryRef` |
| speed value | `speedMph`, `speedKph`, `speedBucket`, `speedClass` |
| provenance | `speedSource`, `confidence`, `provenanceSummary`, `sourceLineage` |
| authority | `sourceAuthority`, `freshnessSensitivity`, `fallbackAllowed`, `rawSourceHydrationAvailable`, `rawSourceHydrationRef` |
| allowed use | `viewport_render`, `route_evidence`, `scoring` |
| guardrail | `substrateAcceptedAsTruth: false` |

Supported `speedSource` values:

- `posted`
- `official_imported`
- `osm_tag`
- `owned_dot`
- `inferred_policy`
- `unknown`

## `RouteSpeedEvidenceDescriptor`

Route speed evidence is a derived route-indexed descriptor:

| Field group | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| profile/layer | `profileKey: route_evidence_scoring_v1`, `layerId: speed_limit` |
| route join | `routeFingerprint`, `startDistM`, `endDistM` |
| metadata | `sourceWayId`, `sourceWayContributionId` |
| speed value | `speedMph`, `speedKph`, `speedBucket`, `speedClass` |
| provenance | `speedSource`, `confidence`, `provenance`, `sourceLineage` |
| authority | `authorityState`, `mayDriveScoring`, `rawSourceHydrationRef` |
| guardrail | `substrateAcceptedAsTruth: false` |

Route distance is the join key. Source way ID is metadata and a hydration reference, not the route join key.

## Conversion Rules

`convertViewportSpeedDescriptorToRouteEvidence` converts a viewport descriptor to route evidence only when all required checks pass.

Blocked reasons:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `speed_unknown` | No known speed value or speed source is `unknown`. |
| `display_only_descriptor` | Descriptor may render the viewport but is not allowed to become scoring evidence. |
| `stale_for_scoring` | Descriptor is stale, conflicted, or otherwise unsafe for scoring. |
| `source_version_mismatch` | Descriptor is superseded by current owned source. |
| `missing_raw_source_ref` | No raw source/provenance reference is available. |
| `missing_route_span` | V2S+S did not supply route-distance span context. |
| `not_authoritative_for_route_evidence` | Authority evaluation does not permit route evidence. |

No speed value is fabricated. Inferred speed is allowed only when explicitly marked `inferred_policy` with reduced confidence and provenance.

## Authority Examples

| Descriptor state | Viewport render | Route evidence | Scoring |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fresh authoritative, source-backed | yes | yes | yes |
| stale usable viewport profile | yes, with refresh | no | no |
| display-only profile | yes | no | no |
| source version mismatch | no | no | no |
| missing raw source ref | maybe display, depending authority | no for scoring | no |
| unknown speed | no route evidence | no | no |

## Test Loop No-Speed Diagnostic

Test Loop remains blocked because no speed descriptor exists for the accepted ways:

- 11613459
- 971362311
- 1388406931
- 1388406932

Diagnostic result:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| speed descriptor available | false |
| route speed evidence available | false |
| blocked reason | `speed_unknown` |
| scoring still blocked | true |
| heatmap still deferred | true |
| provider output selected | false |
| substrate accepted as truth | false |

## Future National Viewport Speed Hydration

The national `viewport_speed` cache should store compact speed descriptors, not full raw tags:

- source way or substrate span reference
- compact speed value/bucket/class
- speed source
- confidence
- source/profile/schema versions
- freshness timestamps
- provenance summary
- raw source hydration reference

This supports quick first paint while preserving a path back to owned source evidence for route scoring and inspection.

## Future V2S+S Route Scoring

V2S+S identity supplies accepted ownership spans and source-way contributions. The evidence worker may use a scoring-authoritative speed descriptor only after adding route-distance span context. The scoring worker should consume route-indexed speed evidence, not viewport display geometry and not base substrate truth.

## Recommended Next Phase

14G should add a source-backed speed profile fixture for Test Loop or a nearby richer route.

Preferred path:

1. Build a tiny owned `viewport_speed` or `route_evidence_scoring_v1` fixture for the accepted source ways.
2. Include units, provenance, confidence, source version, and raw source hydration refs.
3. Convert it into route speed evidence through this contract.
4. Keep scoring blocked until traffic, shoulder, bike infra, and other required fields are handled.

## Projection Formula Status

Required formula:

`V2S+S projected full route-load = V2S+S measured identity + adapters + V1 measured downstream grouped work`

Current measured values:

| Value | Status |
| --- | --- |
| V2S+S measured identity + adapters | `81ms` |
| V1 measured downstream grouped work | unavailable |
| projected V2S+S full route-load | not computable |

V1 measured downstream grouped work requires:

`V1 total - V1 ingest - V1 fetch/source acquisition - V1 build/match`

Those same-fixture V1 buckets are not available without either using current app route-load state or running the production V1 route-analysis path directly.

## Exact V1 Fixture-Run Blockers

1. The current fixture-scoped benchmark runner still reports `partial_v1_still_requires_app_route_load` for V1.
2. Current app route-load diagnostics can reflect the full Test Loop route, not the 22-point short fixture.
3. Direct `analyzeRoute` on the fixture is not safe under this task because `skipCache` only skips the route-cache read; the production path can still call `setCachedRoute` on high-quality results.
4. No V1 fixture-run mode currently exposes a no-route-cache-write guarantee with full production scoring/heatmap/display included.

## What V2S+S Did Prove Here

- Same short Test Loop fixture route scope for the V2S+S lane.
- Actual V2 worker/path construction pipeline ran from queryable provider records.
- Provider source mode: `queryable_substrate_provider_debug`.
- Broad merged roads read by provider lane: `false`.
- Public Overpass used by provider lane: `false`.
- Provider topology records: `8`.
- Accepted way IDs: `11613459`, `971362311`, `1388406931`, `1388406932`.
- Ownership spans: `2`.
- Handoffs: `1`.
- Blockers: `0`.
- Relation valid: `true`.
- Validation errors: `0`.
- Truth-run adapter count: `2`.
- Display-segment adapter count: `2`.
- Cue/handoff summary count: `1`.

## Caveats

- `fixture_provider_read_is_local_debug_not_national_cache_promise`.
- This does not include scoring integration.
- This does not include heatmap integration.
- This does not prove V2S+S beats V1 full app route-load.
- It does support the architectural implication that V2S+S can avoid V1's broad corridor/candidate universe for this fixture once a comparable V1 fixture runner exists.

## Verdict

**not_comparable**

V2S+S is still the right direction: `81ms` for identity plus adapters on the short real fixture, with 0 blockers and a valid relation, is promising. But the V1 side is not currently measurable on the exact same fixture under the no-route-cache/no-production-change guardrails, so there is no honest projected full route-load win yet.

## Recommended Next Step

Add a diagnostic V1 fixture-run harness that:

- loads `public/demo/fixture-test-loop-1-ccw-short.gpx` directly,
- runs the same production V1 route-load stages,
- disables route-cache reads and writes,
- exposes ingest, fetch/source, build/match, downstream grouped, and output counts,
- does not change production default behavior.

Only then compute the projected full-route-load estimate and verdict.

# EXEC-030 Phase 14J - Enterprise Substrate/Profile Cache Foundation

## Direct Answer

**B. partial_cache_foundation_needs_contract_hardening**

The current architecture is directionally right and no longer requires fake golden-harness hydration. The core contracts now exist for source registry/versioning, normalized evidence records, resolved route evidence, route evidence profiles, profile authority/freshness, speed descriptors, V2S+S evidence worker skeleton, and scoring worker contracts.

The gap is enterprise productization: there is not yet a server-authorized product evidence provider/cache write path that can warm viewport or route evidence profiles from owned source during real cold route loads. Until that exists, golden harness routes must remain read-only consumers and must not inject fake evidence.

## Executive Summary

- Golden harness must not fake hydration.
- Product cache/evidence system is the authority.
- Golden harness routes should exercise only the same cache/profile/evidence paths real routes use.
- Cold route loads may warm profile caches only through an authorized product hydration/write path.
- Diagnostic runners must report `cacheWarmingAttempted: false` with reason `diagnostic_read_only_guardrail`.
- Product warming is not yet production-ready because the server-authorized profile cache write path is missing.

Current product posture:

| Decision | Status |
| --- | --- |
| base substrate stays structural and compact | yes |
| viewport profiles are modular and configurable | yes |
| `viewport_speed` is national/common-profile eligible | yes |
| speed is not base substrate truth | yes |
| traffic/AADT is owned-source-backed common overlay candidate | yes |
| route evidence attaches by route distance | yes |
| raw owned source remains authority | yes |
| profile cache can distinguish display vs scoring authority | contract exists |
| product cache warming write path | missing |
| golden harness fake hydration | rejected |

## Current Architecture Inventory

| Component | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base cyclist substrate cache | partial | DS-034/DS-035 define the compact structural substrate. Test/queryable providers exist, but production cache warming/read APIs are not enterprise-complete. |
| viewport profile hydration cache | partial | DS-035 defines viewport profiles including `viewport_speed`, `viewport_traffic_v1`, `viewport_bike_infra_v1`, `viewport_shoulder_v1`, `viewport_surface_v1`. `v2ss-profile-cache-authority` and speed descriptor contracts exist. Durable product read/write provider is missing. |
| route evidence profile hydration cache | partial | `route_evidence_scoring_v1` request/response contract exists and consumes ownership spans/source-way contributions. Product provider/cache backing is missing. |
| raw owned source evidence | partial | Source registry/version and raw feature ref contracts exist. Local owned artifacts exist for proofs. Production source preservation/import/query contracts are not fully wired to route evidence provider. |
| route cache | implemented but separate | `route_cache` stores completed route analysis reuse. It is not substrate, not raw evidence, and not profile hydration. It must not be used for route evidence/profile warming. |
| product evidence provider | missing | This is the major 14J gap. V2S+S needs a product provider interface that can read profile caches, hydrate owned source on miss/stale, resolve evidence, and optionally perform authorized cache writes. |
| V2S+S evidence worker | diagnostic-only | Skeleton emits route-indexed layers for low-risk provider/source fields. It does not yet call a product evidence provider. |
| scoring worker contract | contract-only | Worker message/input/output contracts exist. Scoring remains deferred. |

## Cache Boundary Table

| Cache/layer | Primary purpose | Read key | Write authority | Version metadata | Freshness metadata | Allowed consumers | Forbidden consumers | Route truth allowed | Scoring truth allowed | Golden harness allowed | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base cyclist substrate cache | structural cyclist mobility, low-zoom first paint, candidate narrowing, route identity acceleration | tile, z-band, region, corridor/source refs | server/import pipeline only | source/version metadata required | low/medium freshness by source snapshot | viewport substrate renderer, V2S+S candidate helper | scoring engine as truth, heatmap risk truth, route relation truth | no | no | read-only exercise only | Stores corridor/salience/continuity/constituent refs, not every evidence field. |
| viewport profile hydration cache | full-map overlays before route load | profile key + viewport/tile/zoom + source/schema/profile version | server-authorized profile hydration | schemaVersion, profileVersion, sourceVersion, sourceSnapshotId, modelVersion when derived | staleAfter, authoritativeUntil, authority state | map overlays, exploration UI, planning display | RouteLine topology truth, scoring without route evidence validation | no | only after stricter route evidence conversion, not directly | read-only assert miss/hit only | `viewport_speed` may be nationally prehydrated but is not base substrate truth. |
| route evidence profile hydration cache | route/span/source-way evidence for V2S+S | route fingerprint/window, accepted source way IDs, route-distance spans, profile key | server-authorized route evidence hydration | schemaVersion, profileVersion/sourceVersion, sourceSnapshotId | strict scoring authority/freshness states | V2S+S evidence worker, scoring readiness gate, future scoring worker | viewport display as route truth, V1 truth-run/sample-index internals | no | yes, only after authority/freshness/resolution | read-only unless using product authorized warming mode | Outputs route-indexed evidence layers. |

| route cache | completed route analysis reuse | route hash / completed analysis key | production route analysis cache policy | data version/current route cache version | cache TTL/version policy | production route result reuse | substrate/profile/evidence hydration, raw source, V2S+S evidence provider | no | no | no | Boundary must stay separate. |

## Enterprise Readiness Checklist

| --- | --- | --- |

| cache warming | missing | No server-authorized profile cache write path in V2S+S product provider. |

| rollback | partial | Docs discuss fallback; operational toggle/write rollback missing here. |
| rebuild/replay strategy | missing | No enterprise rebuild/replay tooling for profile descriptors yet. |

## Cold-Load Warming Model

Intended product flow:

1. Route load starts.
2. V2S+S identity requests substrate/provider topology.
3. Identity produces ownership spans, real-node handoffs, source-way contributions, and route windows.
4. V2S+S evidence worker requests missing profile/evidence descriptors from the product evidence provider.
5. Product evidence provider reads profile cache first.
6. If profile data is missing, stale, conflicted, or superseded:
   - hydrate from owned canonical source,
   - preserve raw source refs,
   - produce normalized evidence records,
   - resolve route evidence through explicit policy,
   - optionally write a profile descriptor through the server-authorized cache write path.
7. V2S+S consumes route-indexed evidence.
8. Scoring readiness evaluates whether required score-driving fields are present.
9. Future scoring worker consumes only the route-indexed evidence bundle.
10. Golden harness observes the same path.

Diagnostic mode:

```text
cacheWarmingAttempted: false
reason: diagnostic_read_only_guardrail
```

Current product readiness:

```text
cacheWarmingSupported: false
missing: server_authorized_profile_cache_write_path
```

`route_cache` is not involved in evidence/profile warming.

## Golden Harness Policy

- Golden harness routes should load cold through the same product path as user routes.
- Golden harness can assert cache miss/hit/warming behavior.
- Golden harness cannot inject fake values.
- Golden harness cannot bypass the product evidence provider.
- Fixture values require source/provenance records.
- Manual observations are diagnostic-only unless promoted to source-backed fixture records.
- Golden harness may run read-only and then must explicitly report that cache warming was not attempted.
- Golden harness should never become a hydration pack.

## Required Code Seams Before National Hydration

Before national profile hydration, these seams must exist and be enforceable:

| Seam | Status |
| --- | --- |
| source registry/version contract | exists |
| raw source feature preservation | partial |
| normalized evidence record contract | exists |
| resolver policy | exists, basic |
| profile cache authority/freshness contract | exists |
| viewport profile descriptor contract | exists for speed |
| route evidence profile descriptor/request contract | exists |
| product evidence provider interface | missing |
| server-authorized profile cache write path | missing |
| cache invalidation/version gates | partial contract only |
| cache warming telemetry | missing |
| diagnostic read-only mode | policy defined; provider interface missing |
| replay/rebuild tooling | missing |

## Enterprise Risks Found

| Risk | Current finding | Required mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| substrate stores evidence as route truth | guarded in current V2S+S diagnostics | Keep substrate noncanonical; enforce in provider contracts. |
| profile descriptors lack version/freshness metadata | contracts include metadata | Ensure storage/provider implementation requires it. |
| viewport profile reused as scoring truth | conversion/authority contracts block this | Product provider must enforce the same rule. |
| route evidence profiles cannot batch by accepted ways/spans | contract supports batching | Product provider must implement batch reads/hydration. |
| golden harness bypasses product provider | still possible if future code adds fixture shortcuts | Reject fixture-only hydration; harness must be product-path consumer. |
| V2S+S reads source-specific end tables directly | current diagnostic modules can adapt local records | Product scoring path must use evidence provider/abstraction, not end tables. |
| cache warming path unclear | missing | Define product evidence provider v1. |
| cache write authorization unclear | missing | Server-authorized write boundary required before warming. |
| invalidation/versioning incomplete | partial | Implement source/profile/model version gates and rebuild/replay. |
| stale display vs scoring block missing | contract exists | Product profile reads must call authority evaluator. |
| route_cache/profile cache blurred | docs/tests guard this | Keep route cache out of evidence/profile warming. |

## What Not To Do

- Do not hydrate golden harness routes with fake data.
- Do not bake speed into base substrate.
- Do not let viewport profiles become RouteLine truth.
- Do not make `route_cache` a road/evidence/profile cache.
- Do not let scoring read OSM/HPMS/DOT end tables directly.
- Do not require a national rebuild for every scoring model bug.
- Do not silently infer missing score-driving fields.
- Do not write browser/diagnostic rows into shared profile cache.
- Do not use external APIs as normal production authority when owned source exists.

## Product Evidence Provider Boundary

The missing enterprise seam is a product evidence provider that can run in two modes:

| Mode | Cache read | Owned source hydration | Cache write | Use case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| diagnostic_read_only | yes | optional read-only/provenance check | no | tests, golden harness, local diagnostics |
| authorized_product_warming | yes | yes | server-authorized only | real cold route loads, viewport profile hydration |

The provider must return:

- cache hit/miss/stale/conflict status,
- profile authority state,
- source versions used,
- normalized evidence record counts,
- resolved evidence layer counts,
- cacheWarmingAttempted,
- cacheWarmingSupported,
- externalFallbackUsed,
- warnings/blockers.

## Recommended Next Phase

**14K - Product Evidence Provider v1 cache interface**

Goal:

Define the product evidence provider read/write/cache-warming interface, with read-only diagnostic mode and authorized product warming mode.

Do not implement national hydration yet. The interface should make fake golden-harness hydration impossible by construction: harnesses may request evidence through the provider, but only the authorized product mode may warm profile caches.

# EXEC-030 Phase 14K - Product Evidence Provider Cache Interface

## Direct Answer

**A. yes_product_evidence_cache_interface_ready**

The Product Evidence Provider v1 cache interface is now defined as a pure contract/facade. It supports read-only diagnostics now and server-authorized profile warming later without writing cache records, touching `route_cache`, calling scoring, or changing production behavior.

This phase did not implement national hydration or production cache writes. It made the boundary explicit and testable.

## What Was Hardened From 14J

14J identified the missing enterprise seam:

1. Product Evidence Provider interface
2. server-authorized profile cache warming/write path
3. clear diagnostic read-only vs authorized product warming modes

14K adds the pure interface and policy checks for that seam:

- `ProductEvidenceRequest`
- `ProductEvidenceResponse`
- `ProductEvidenceCacheReadSummary`
- `ProductEvidenceCacheWriteSummary`
- cache warming policy by caller type
- route-cache rejection as evidence/profile cache
- mockable provider facade

Implementation file:

`src/lib/route-line-v2/v2ss-product-evidence-cache-interface.ts`

## Product Evidence Provider v1 Interface

The provider request includes:

- request/run identity
- route fingerprint and distance
- ownership spans
- source-way contributions
- accepted source way IDs
- requested profile key
- requested layers
- authority/freshness policy
- mode:
  - `diagnostic_read_only`
  - `product_authorized_warming`
- caller type:
  - `product_route_load`
  - `admin_diagnostic`
  - `golden_harness`
  - `unit_test`
  - `manual_fixture`

The provider response includes:

- attached/missing/unavailable/deferred layers
- resolved evidence
- source records used
- cache read summary
- cache write summary
- authority summary
- freshness summary
- provenance summary
- confidence summary
- diagnostics
- guardrails:
  - scoring still blocked
  - heatmap still deferred
  - provider output not selected
  - substrate accepted as truth false

## Cache Read Summary Contract

`ProductEvidenceCacheReadSummary` reports:

- profile key
- whether lookup was attempted
- hit/miss/stale status
- authority/freshness state
- source/schema/profile/model versions when present
- read mode:
  - `profile_cache`
  - `raw_owned_source`
  - `route_cache`
  - `none`
- route-cache rejection
- reason codes

Important rule:

`route_cache` is rejected as an evidence/profile cache. Completed route analysis reuse is not the source of scoring evidence, profile descriptors, or raw road facts.

## Cache Warming / Write Summary Contract

`ProductEvidenceCacheWriteSummary` reports:

- `cacheWarmingSupported`
- `cacheWarmingAttempted`
- `cacheWriteAuthorized`
- `cacheWritePerformed`
- skipped reason
- write authority:
  - `none`
  - `diagnostic_forbidden`
  - `server_authorized`
  - `fixture_forbidden`
- would-write descriptor count
- actual written descriptor count
- reason codes

No real writes were implemented in this phase. Tests use an in-memory mock writer only.

## Diagnostic Read-Only vs Product-Authorized Warming

| Mode | Cache reads | Owned source hydration | Cache writes | Intended use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `diagnostic_read_only` | yes | yes, through mocks/contracts | never | golden harness, admin diagnostics, unit tests |
| `product_authorized_warming` | yes | yes | only if server-authorized | future product route loads / viewport profile warming |

Required read-only behavior:

```text
cacheWarmingAttempted: false
cacheWriteSkippedReason: diagnostic_read_only_guardrail
```

Required unauthorized product behavior:

```text
cacheWarmingAttempted: true
cacheWritePerformed: false
cacheWriteSkippedReason: server_authorization_missing
```

## Golden Harness Policy

Golden harness routes default to `diagnostic_read_only`.

They may:

- request evidence through the Product Evidence Provider,
- assert cache miss/hit/stale diagnostics,
- observe source-backed normalized/resolved evidence,
- verify scoring remains blocked when fields are missing.

They may not:

- inject fake hydration,
- write cache,
- bypass the product provider,
- use manual observations as scoring authority,
- use `route_cache` as evidence/profile cache.

If a golden harness ever warms cache, it must do so only by explicitly running `product_authorized_warming` through the real product provider with server authorization. That path is not implemented here.

## Route Cache Boundary

`route_cache` remains completed-analysis reuse only.

It is forbidden as:

- substrate cache,
- viewport profile cache,
- route evidence profile cache,
- raw owned source evidence,
- V2S+S source truth,
- scoring evidence source.

The 14K helper explicitly rejects `readMode: route_cache` for product evidence reads.

## Profile Cache Boundary

Profile caches store descriptors and route/viewport evidence payloads with authority/freshness metadata.

Viewport profile examples:

- `viewport_speed`
- `viewport_traffic_v1`
- `viewport_bike_infra_v1`
- `viewport_shoulder_v1`
- `viewport_surface_v1`

Route evidence profile examples:

- `route_evidence_scoring_v1`

Viewport profiles may render when display-authorized. They cannot become route truth, and stale/display-only descriptors cannot drive scoring.

Route evidence profiles require stricter authority for scoring readiness.

## Raw Owned Source Authority

Raw owned source remains the authority for:

- provenance,
- conflict resolution,
- source inspection,
- exact source fields,
- scoring authority when profile descriptors are stale, missing, conflicted, or superseded.

When a cached profile conflicts with raw owned source, the provider must hydrate owned source and resolve evidence again. Raw source wins conflict.

## Failure Modes

| Failure | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| diagnostic runner requests warming | skip write with `diagnostic_read_only_guardrail` |
| product route load lacks server authorization | report `server_authorization_missing` |
| manual fixture requests write | reject with `fixture_or_test_write_forbidden` |
| route cache returned as evidence source | reject as `route_cache_rejected_as_evidence_profile_cache` |
| stale viewport descriptor | may render if `stale_usable`; cannot drive scoring |
| stale route evidence descriptor | block scoring and require owned source hydration |
| cached descriptor conflicts with raw source | hydrate owned source; raw source wins |
| required score-driving fields missing | keep scoring blocked; do not fabricate values |

## Test Coverage

Added:

`src/lib/route-line-v2/v2ss-product-evidence-cache-interface.test.ts`

Covered:

- diagnostic read-only never writes cache
- product warming requires authorization
- authorized product warming reports would-write/mock-write counts
- golden harness defaults to read-only
- golden harness cannot fake hydration
- manual fixture/unit test cannot write cache
- `route_cache` is rejected as evidence/profile cache
- stale viewport profile may render but cannot drive scoring
- stale route evidence profile blocks scoring
- raw owned source wins profile conflict
- cache miss can hydrate from owned source through mock hydrator
- scoring remains blocked
- heatmap remains deferred
- provider output remains unselected
- substrate remains noncanonical

## Recommended Next Phase

**14L - Product Evidence Provider read-only integration with V2S+S evidence worker**

Goal:

Wire the V2S+S evidence worker skeleton to call the Product Evidence Provider in `diagnostic_read_only` mode for Test Loop/Medford diagnostics.

Do not implement national hydration or server-authorized writes in 14L. Keep cache warming disabled and explicit:

```text
cacheWarmingAttempted: false
reason: diagnostic_read_only_guardrail
```

## Guardrail Confirmation

- production SQL: false
- Supabase writes: false
- persistence writes: false
- lookup/reload: false
- route_cache writes: false
- scoring cutover: false
- heatmap cutover: false
- default UI behavior change: false
- V2S+S output selection: false
- substrate-as-truth: false
- any-GPX runner: false
- synthetic urban topology proof: false
- detour behavior change: false
- golden-harness-only hydration path: false
- fake evidence values: false

# EXEC-030 Phase 14L - V2S+S Product Evidence Provider Read-Only Integration

## Direct Answer

**A. yes_v2ss_evidence_worker_uses_product_provider_read_only**

The V2S+S diagnostic evidence worker now builds a `ProductEvidenceRequest`, calls the Product Evidence Provider v1 facade in `diagnostic_read_only` mode, and builds its route-indexed evidence bundle from the product provider response.

No cache writes, SQL, Supabase writes, scoring, heatmap, production selection, or production route-analysis behavior changed.

## What Path Changed

Before 14L, the evidence worker skeleton attached low-risk evidence directly from Test Loop provider/source tags.

After 14L, the worker path is:

```text
V2S+S ownership spans/source-way contributions
-> route_evidence_scoring_v1 request
-> ProductEvidenceRequest
-> Product Evidence Provider v1 facade
-> normalized/resolved owned fixture evidence through provider deps
-> ProductEvidenceResponse
-> V2SSRouteIndexedEvidenceBundle
```

The availability matrix still reports source-way field presence for diagnostics, but the emitted evidence layers come from the Product Evidence Provider response.

## Product Provider Request / Response

The worker requests:

- profile: `route_evidence_scoring_v1`
- mode: `diagnostic_read_only`
- caller: `golden_harness`
- cache write authorization: false
- requested layers:
  - `road_class`
  - `highway`
  - `speed_limit`
  - `traffic_aadt`
  - `shoulder`
  - `bike_infra`
  - `lane_count`
  - `surface`
  - `hazard_events`
  - `time_of_day_traffic_multiplier`

The response includes:

- attached layers
- missing layers
- unavailable layers
- deferred layers
- cache read summary
- cache write summary
- provenance and confidence summaries
- scoring blocked / heatmap deferred guardrails

## Test Loop Evidence Result

The Test Loop evidence result remains semantically equivalent:

| Layer | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `road_class` / `highway` | attached |
| `surface` | partially attached from source-backed records |
| `lane_count` | partially attached from source-backed records |
| `speed_limit` | missing |
| `bike_infra` | missing |
| `traffic_aadt` | unavailable in current fixture |
| `shoulder` | unavailable in current fixture |
| `hazard_events` | deferred |
| `time_of_day_traffic_multiplier` | deferred |

Scoring remains blocked because required score-driving fields are still missing. Heatmap remains deferred.

## Cache Read / Write Summary

Expected read-only behavior:

```text
productEvidenceProviderUsed: true
productEvidenceProviderMode: diagnostic_read_only
productEvidenceProviderCaller: golden_harness
cacheReadSummary.readMode: profile_cache
cacheReadSummary.routeCacheRejected: false
cacheWriteSummary.cacheWarmingAttempted: false
cacheWriteSummary.cacheWritePerformed: false
cacheWriteSummary.cacheWriteSkippedReason: diagnostic_read_only_guardrail
```

The provider may hydrate from local owned fixture records through mocked provider dependencies for tests, but it does not write profile cache descriptors.

## Why Diagnostic Read-Only Does Not Warm Cache

`diagnostic_read_only` is intentionally non-mutating. It can prove that the product evidence path works and that missing fields remain explicit, but it cannot create cache state.

This keeps golden harnesses from becoming fake hydration packs.

## Golden Harness Boundary

Golden harnesses are consumers of the Product Evidence Provider.

They may:

- request evidence through the product provider,
- observe attached/missing/unavailable/deferred layers,
- assert read-only cache behavior,
- verify scoring remains blocked when evidence is incomplete.

They may not:

- inject fake evidence values,
- bypass the product provider,
- warm cache without explicit product authorization,
- treat fixture values as production scoring truth without source/provenance.

## Remaining Blocker Before Product-Authorized Warming

The product-authorized warming path is still not wired to a server-authorized writer.

The missing production seam remains:

```text
server_authorized_profile_cache_write_path
```

Until that exists, product cache warming should remain diagnostic or mock-only.

## Recommended Next Phase

**14M - server-authorized profile cache warming design/spec**

Define the server-authorized write boundary, descriptor write shape, invalidation/version gates, and telemetry needed before any real product route load or viewport profile request can warm profile cache records.

Do not implement national hydration in 14M.

## Guardrail Confirmation

- production SQL: false
- Supabase writes: false
- persistence writes: false
- lookup/reload: false
- route_cache writes/coupling: false
- scoring cutover: false
- heatmap cutover: false

# EXEC-030 Phase 14M - Speed Evidence Abstraction Hardening

## Direct Answer

**B. partial_direct_osm_source_path_remains**

The route evidence path already used normalized/resolved evidence for Medford and Test Loop response building, but the Test Loop speed profile fixture provider still created `viewport_speed` descriptors directly from source tags before normalization/resolution. That made the fixture path too easy to read as:

```text
OSM maxspeed tag -> speed profile descriptor truth
```

This pass hardened that path. Direct source reads for `maxspeed` now happen only inside source adapters that emit `NormalizedEvidenceRecord`. Speed profile descriptors and route speed evidence are derived from resolved evidence.

## Current Speed Path

The intended path is now enforced in the diagnostic fixtures:

```text
raw source facts
-> NormalizedEvidenceRecord candidates
-> resolver policy
-> ResolvedRouteEvidence
-> viewport_speed descriptor and/or route_evidence_scoring_v1 speed_limit layer
```

OSM `maxspeed` remains a candidate source. It is not final speed truth.

## Direct OSM Coupling Found

Found and removed from the speed profile fixture provider:

- direct source tag to `ViewportSpeedProfileDescriptor`
- direct source tag to route speed evidence descriptor

The provider now:

- adapts source tags into normalized evidence,
- resolves speed candidates,
- derives route speed descriptors from selected resolved evidence,
- derives viewport speed descriptors from selected resolved evidence.

## Resolver Policy For OSM vs HPMS/DOT/NJDOT

Speed conflict/corroboration reasons are explicit:

| Condition | Resolution reason |
| --- | --- |
| OSM and official candidates agree | `corroborated_speed_agreement` |
| official DOT/HPMS/NJDOT candidate supersedes conflicting OSM speed | `official_source_supersedes_osm` |
| OSM is the only acceptable candidate | `osm_only_speed` |
| no speed candidate exists | `missing_speed` |
| conflicting candidates remain without authoritative selection | `conflict_requires_review` |

Source facts are retained separately:

- `candidateEvidenceIds` preserves all speed candidates.
- `selectedEvidenceId` identifies the resolver-selected speed fact.
- stale/conflicted/display-only profile descriptors cannot drive scoring.
- `route_cache` remains rejected as evidence/profile cache.

## Medford Examples

### Stokes Road

Current diagnostic fixture candidates:

- OSM `maxspeed=35 mph`
- manual-observed NJDOT/HPMS 35 mph, diagnostic-only until backed by source record

Resolver result:

- selected: OSM source-backed speed
- candidates retained: OSM and manual-observed NJDOT/HPMS
- reason: `corroborated_speed_agreement`

Additional hardening test:

- if source-backed DOT reports 40 mph while OSM reports 35 mph, DOT is selected and reason is `official_source_supersedes_osm`.

### Tabernacle Road

Current diagnostic fixture candidates:

- OSM `maxspeed=25 mph`
- manual-observed NJDOT 25 mph, diagnostic-only until backed by source record

Resolver result:

- selected: OSM source-backed speed
- candidates retained: OSM and manual-observed NJDOT
- reason: `corroborated_speed_agreement`

Existing DOT-only fixture behavior remains:

- source-backed DOT speed attaches even when OSM maxspeed is absent.

## Remaining Blockers Before Scoring

Speed abstraction is hardened, but scoring is still not runnable because other required score-driving fields remain missing or unavailable:

- traffic/AADT
- shoulder
- bike infrastructure
- complete lane coverage where required

No scoring engine was called. No heatmap output was emitted.

## Recommended Next Phase

**14N - Product-authorized profile cache warming mock**

Now that speed evidence is abstraction-safe, the next step should mock the product-authorized profile cache warming path behind explicit server authorization. It should still avoid real SQL/Supabase writes and should keep golden harnesses read-only by default.

# EXEC-030 Phase 14N - Product-Authorized Cache Warming Mock

## Direct Answer

**A. yes_authorized_warming_mock_ready**

Product Evidence Provider v1 can now perform a mock-only `product_authorized_warming` pass when explicitly server-authorized, while diagnostic, admin, manual, and default golden harness paths remain read-only.

No real cache writes, SQL, Supabase writes, route cache writes, scoring, heatmap, V1 behavior, or UI behavior changed.

## Read-Only vs Authorized Warming Matrix

| Mode / caller | Warming attempted | Writer called | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `diagnostic_read_only` | false | false | `diagnostic_read_only_guardrail` |
| `golden_harness` default | false | false | read-only consumer |
| `manual_fixture` | false | false | fixture write forbidden |
| `unit_test` | false | false | test write forbidden |
| `admin_diagnostic` | false | false | diagnostic write forbidden |
| `product_authorized_warming` without authorization | true | false | `server_authorization_missing` |
| `product_authorized_warming` with authorization | true | true, mock only | `server_authorized_mock_write` |

## Caller Policy

Golden harnesses still default to `diagnostic_read_only`.

They cannot fake hydration or write cache. A golden harness can only exercise warming when explicitly routed through `product_authorized_warming` with server authorization and the Product Evidence Provider facade.

Manual fixtures and unit tests cannot write cache, even if they request product warming mode.

## Mock Write Payload Shape

The mock writer receives profile descriptor-shaped payloads, not route-cache records.

Each descriptor includes:

- profile key
- schema/profile/source/model version metadata where available
- generated/stale/authoritative timestamps
- authority state
- provenance summary
- confidence
- source lineage
- descriptor records
- selected evidence ID
- candidate evidence IDs
- conflict/corroboration reason
- `derivedFromResolvedEvidence: true`
- `routeCacheWrite: false`
- `substrateAcceptedAsTruth: false`

The descriptor payload is produced from `ResolvedRouteEvidence`, not raw OSM tags.

## Why Route Cache Is Rejected

`route_cache` stores completed route analysis reuse. It is not:

- profile cache,
- route evidence cache,
- raw owned source evidence,
- speed truth,
- scoring truth.

The Product Evidence Provider continues to reject `readMode: route_cache` as evidence/profile cache.

## Test Loop Missing-Speed Behavior

Test Loop still has no source-backed speed on accepted ways.

For `viewport_speed` / `speed_limit` warming:

- no speed descriptor payload is produced,
- mock writer is not called,
- cache write summary reports `no_descriptors_to_write`,
- no speed is inferred or fabricated.

## Medford Resolved-Speed Descriptor Behavior

Medford source-backed speed evidence can produce mock descriptor payloads after resolution:

- OSM speed remains candidate evidence.
- DOT/NJDOT/HPMS can supersede OSM by resolver policy.
- equal candidate speeds are marked `corroborated_speed_agreement`.
- descriptor records preserve `candidateEvidenceIds` and `selectedEvidenceId`.
- manual-observed values remain diagnostic-only unless promoted to source-backed records.

## Why This Is Still Not Real Cache Writes

The writer is a test/mock dependency. It records descriptor payload shape and count only.

There is still no production write adapter, SQL, Supabase mutation, cache persistence, route cache mutation, national hydration, scoring call, or heatmap output.

Before production warming:

- define the server-authorized profile cache write adapter,
- define descriptor storage schema and invalidation/version gates,
- add write telemetry,
- add replay/rebuild controls,
- prove cache hit/miss behavior without route truth leakage,
- keep golden harnesses read-only by default.

Define the server-only write boundary and descriptor storage contract before any real cache writes are attempted.

# EXEC-030 Phase 14O — Product Evidence Cache Lifecycle Simulation

## Direct Answer

A. `yes_cache_lifecycle_simulation_ready`

Product Evidence Provider v1 can simulate a cold cache miss, owned/mock source hydration, resolved evidence generation, authorized mock descriptor warming, and a second-request cache hit without real writes and without `route_cache`.

This remains a pure diagnostic/mock lifecycle. It does not write SQL, Supabase, persistence, `route_cache`, scoring output, or heatmap output.

## Cold Miss Flow

Input:

- Fixture: Medford source-backed speed evidence fixture
- Profile: `viewport_speed`
- Requested layer: `speed_limit`
- Mode: `product_authorized_warming`
- Caller: `product_route_load`
- Authorization: server-authorized mock write

Cold request behavior:

- `cacheReadSummary.cacheMiss: true`
- In-memory profile cache has no descriptor.
- Owned/mock source hydrator supplies normalized speed evidence.
- Resolver produces `ResolvedRouteEvidence`.
- Speed descriptors are built from resolved evidence, not direct OSM tags.
- `cacheWarmingAttempted: true`
- `cacheWriteAuthorized: true`
- `cacheWritePerformed: true` in mock only
- `routeCacheUsed: false`
- scoring is not called
- heatmap output is not generated

## Authorized Mock Warm Flow

The mock writer stores profile-shaped descriptors in memory.

Descriptor payloads include:

- `profileKey`
- `schemaVersion`
- `profileVersion`
- `sourceVersion`
- `sourceSnapshotId`
- `generatedAt`
- `staleAfter`
- `authoritativeUntil`
- `authorityState`
- `provenanceSummary`
- `confidence`
- `sourceLineage`
- descriptor records with `selectedEvidenceId`, `candidateEvidenceIds`, and `conflictResolutionReason`
- `routeCacheWrite: false`
- `derivedFromResolvedEvidence: true`
- `substrateAcceptedAsTruth: false`

## Warm Hit Flow

The second request uses the same route fingerprint, profile key, requested layer, and source version.

Warm request behavior:

- `cacheReadSummary.cacheHit: true`
- cached descriptor authority/freshness is evaluated before use
- owned source hydration is skipped
- cache write is skipped in diagnostic read-only mode
- selected evidence IDs are preserved
- candidate evidence IDs are preserved
- provenance and speed values are preserved
- `routeCacheUsed: false`

The warm-hit response preserves the resolved evidence semantics from the warmed descriptor path.

## Stale Descriptor Flow

For a stale `viewport_speed` descriptor:

- viewport rendering can remain allowed under `stale_usable`
- scoring is blocked
- route evidence use is blocked
- background refresh is recommended
- diagnostic read-only mode does not write a replacement

Cache hits do not bypass authority/freshness checks.

## Conflict / Superseded Flow

If cached profile evidence conflicts with newer owned source evidence:

- raw owned source wins
- cached descriptor is treated as `conflicted` or `superseded_by_source`
- scoring cannot use the stale/conflicted descriptor
- authorized mode can mock-warm a replacement descriptor
- diagnostic read-only mode cannot write a replacement

## Why Route Cache Is Not Involved

`route_cache` stores completed route analysis reuse. It is not:

- a profile descriptor cache
- raw source evidence
- route evidence truth
- scoring evidence authority

The lifecycle simulation rejects `route_cache` as an evidence/profile cache and keeps descriptor writes profile-shaped.

## Why This Is Still Not Real Cache Writes

This phase uses an in-memory mock cache only.

It does not implement:

- SQL schema
- Supabase writes
- national hydration
- real server write authorization
- production cache persistence
- scoring cutover
- heatmap cutover

The purpose is to prove the read/write contract and lifecycle semantics before a production write adapter exists.

## Remaining Work Before Production Warming

Before product-authorized warming can be real:

- define the server-authorized profile cache write adapter
- define descriptor storage schema and indexes
- enforce write authorization server-side
- add cache invalidation/version gates
- add replay/rebuild tooling
- add telemetry for miss/hit/stale/conflict/refresh behavior
- keep raw owned source as authority on conflict

## Recommended Next Phase

14P — Server-authorized profile cache write adapter design/spec.
